args.summary:
This is an academic journal article by Liu Yi-chun (劉怡君), published in the Bulletin of Chinese (國文學報), Vol. 56 (December 2014, pp. 35-66), titled "Analyzing on 'The Theory of Mind-Nature' of Wu Cheng's 'Annotation of Daode Zhenjing'" (吳澄《道德真經註》「心性論」探微——以理學詮解《老子》的義理向度). The article explores how Wu Cheng (吳澄), a renowned Neo-Confucian (理學) scholar of the Yuan Dynasty known as one of the "two great Confucian masters" of the era (paired with Xu Heng (許衡) as 南吳北許), used Neo-Confucian "mind-nature theory" (心性之學) to interpret the Daodejing in his work Annotation of Daode Zhenjing (《道德真經註》).

Key arguments and content:
1. **Context and significance**: During the Song-Yuan-Ming period, Neo-Confucians (理學家) increasingly used "reliance on Confucianism to interpret Laozi" (援儒解老) methods. Wu Cheng's work is identified by scholars like Liu Gu-sheng (劉固盛) as best exemplifying how Neo-Confucianism influenced Laozi studies (老學), and is one of only four Laozi commentaries included in the Siku Quanshu for the Song/Yuan/Ming period.

2. **The "Dao equals Li" (道理合一) interpretation**: Wu Cheng equated the Daoist "Dao" (道) with Neo-Confucian "Principle" (理/天理), infusing the Dao with Confucian moral attributes (仁義禮智 - benevolence, righteousness, propriety, wisdom). He used the "Li Yi Fen Shu" (理一分殊, one principle, many manifestations) concept to interpret the Dao-De relationship as "Dao producing myriad virtue" (道一分殊). He viewed "Dao" as metaphysical principle and "De" as its manifestation in all things.

3. **Mind-nature theory (心性論)**: Wu Cheng drew on Lu Xiangshan's (陸九淵) concept that "mind is principle" (心即是理), arguing that all principles of things are inherent in the mind (萬事萬物之理皆備於我). He emphasized "inner contemplation" (內觀) over external seeking, distinguishing "virtue-knowledge" (德性之知) from "hearing-seeing knowledge" (聞見之知). Wu Cheng's philosophy reconciles Zhu Xi and Lu Xiangshan, though leaning toward Lu's "revering virtue" (尊德性).

4. **"Removing external delusions, taking inner truth" (去外妄，取內真)**: Wu Cheng argued that external desires (五色, 五音, 五味, fame and profit) harm life and obscure the pure human nature. He advocated returning to the infant-like (嬰兒/赤子) state of simplicity and true purity (真樸), achieving unity with the Dao.

5. **Cultivation practices (工夫修養)**: Wu Cheng proposed principles for nurturing form, qi, and spirit (形、氣、神). For recluses (出世之人): preserving form, qi, and spirit (存形、存氣、存神); for those in the world (住世之人): nourishing them (養形、養氣、養神). Additional methods include: exhausting one's nature and reaching destiny (盡性達命), overcoming self and being brave in goodness (克己勇善), inner contemplation of the mind (內觀本心), seeing truth and guarding it firmly (見真守固), mind-environment dual forgetting (心境兩忘), using qi to ward off externals (以氣禦外), mind empty without things (心虛無物), and preserving stillness and returning to destiny (守靜復命).

6. **Conclusion**: The study demonstrates two important points about Yuan Dynasty intellectual history: (1) the reconciliation of Zhu Xi and Lu Xiangshan (會通朱陸) was a trend in Yuan Neo-Confucianism, with Wu Cheng's mind-nature theory leaning toward Lu while his Dao-qi theory inherited Zhu Xi; (2) Yuan-era Neo-Confucianism and Laozi studies interacted significantly. The article also notes Wu Cheng used Confucian classics (the Analects, Mencius) and figures (Confucius, Yan Hui) to interpret Laozi, blurring the boundaries between Confucianism and Taoism.

吳澄《道德真經註》的詮解向度──以「道德」為討論中心 383 吳澄《道德真經註》的詮解向度 ──以「道德」為討論中心 楊筑 一、問題的提出 吳澄（1249-1333），字幼清，晚號伯清，學生稱之曰草盧先生。 其為朱子四傳弟子，一生以繼承朱子學術為志；然其思想亦受象山影響 甚鉅，是以前人多以「和會朱陸」為其學術定調。他一生遍注群經，兼 及老莊，元成宗大德十一年（1307）就醫於富州而寓居清都觀時，嘗 與門人論及《老子》、《莊子》、《太玄》等，而後遂校訂之 1。他深 厚的儒學基砥，使其《道德真經註》展現十分濃厚的理學韻味。劉固盛 嘗用「以理釋《老》」概括南宋金元時期的老學特徵 2，並視吳澄《道 德真經註》為最重要的代表之作，他說： 以理學家身分注《老》並產生較大影響者，則首推元代的吳澄。 吳澄是元代理學重要的代表人物，與許衡齊名，有「南吳北許」 之稱。由於他是由宋入元（27 歲以前生活於南宋），故能直接 宋代理學之端緒，對朱熹和陸九淵的學說都有所繼承。因此，他 的《道德真經註》雖然「發揮老氏之旨，清淨玄妙，暢所欲言」， 1 吳澄校訂《老子》一事，於其〈行狀〉及《年譜》中均有記載。詳見［元］虞集： 〈故翰林學士資善大夫知制誥同修國史臨川先生吳公（澄）行狀〉，頁861。〔元〕 危素：《臨川吳文正公年譜》，見于浩輯：《宋明理學家年譜》（北京：北京圖書館 出版社，2005 年據清光緒四年刻本影印），頁32b。 2 劉固盛嘗言：「南宋金元之際，理學開始成為封建社會的統治思想，對社會的影響日 益擴大，老學研究者們也將理學的思想引入了老學，以『理』釋《老》成為該時期老 學發展的重要特點。相對於南宋來說，該特點在元代更加明顯。」見氏著：《宋元老 學研究》（成都：巴蜀書社，2001 年8 月），頁15。 《東亞漢學研究》2017 特別號 384 但同時帶有濃厚的理學色彩，無論是宇宙本體論還是政治道德層 面，所論老子之道都與理學家之理具有高度的一致性。3 吳澄由宋入元，無論自身師承以至元朝官方均推崇朱子之學，故其在詮 解《老子》時，自然無法擺脫自身的「前見」 4，而呈現濃厚的理學色 彩。究竟吳澄論老子之「道」時，是如何與理學之「理」關聯起來── 即「以理釋《老》」的詮解向度是為何可以展現、如何展現，為本論文 首先需釐清的問題。進而筆者欲就劉氏言吳澄「所論老子之道都與理學 家之理具有高度的一致性」這一評價進行反思，因按筆者觀察，吳澄乃 視老子為「異端之說」 5，其注《老子》，似乎隱含分判儒、道二家的 用意。是以若言老子之「道」和理學之「理」「高度一致」，或許未必 符合吳澄之意。究竟吳澄論老子之「道」與理學之「理」的主要差異為 何、其所批判老氏的理由為何，是為本論文欲探析的第二個問題。另外， 由於《道德真經註》中往往將「道」、「德」並提，是以若要深刻理解 吳澄對於老子之「道」的詮解，實不可脫離關於「德」的論述，故今將 「道德」綜合而言，期使論述更臻完備。 二、「以理釋《老》」的詮釋基砥──「縱貫縱講」的詮釋視域 吳澄能將老子之「道德」與宋儒之「天理」關聯起來，最重要的原 因是，他以理解儒家「天理」的「縱貫縱講」詮解視域來理解老子的 「道德」。眾所周知，「縱貫橫講」、「主觀境界形上學」 6是牟宗三 對於道家所作的學術判斷，也是二十世紀道家形上學的「視域革命」 7。 3 劉固盛：《宋元老學研究》，頁164-165。 4 關於「前見」一詞的意涵，乃參考自洪漢鼎的解釋：「在海德格爾看來，解釋從不是 無前提地把握事先給定的事物，而是具有他所謂理解的前結構，這就是所謂前理解。 前理解包括三種要素：前有（Vorhabe ）、前見（Vorsicht ）和前把握 （Vorgriff）。……前有指此在的理解存在與它先行理解的因緣關係整體的先行占 有關係；前見指前有中的那些可以在這種特殊的理解事件中被解釋的特殊方向，也就 是解釋者理解某一事物的先行立場或視角；在前結構裡被給出的可達到理解的概念則 被稱之為前把握。」詳見氏著：《當代哲學詮釋學導論》（臺北：五南圖書出版公司， 2008 年9 月），頁56。」 5 此說可見吳澄：〈答田副使第三書〉，《吳文正集》（臺北：臺灣商務印書館，1983 年《景印文淵閣四庫全書》，冊1197），卷3，頁32a。 6 此說散見於牟宗三：《中國哲學十九講：中國哲學之簡述及其所涵蘊之問題》（臺北： 臺灣學生書局，1983 年10 月）第五至七講，頁87-156。 7 此說為賴錫三所提出：「牟宗三在二十世紀的客觀實有視域之觀看潮流中，就是第一 位堅持回歸主體實踐，以觀看道家形上學的『視域革命』者。他可以說是在西方實有 吳澄《道德真經註》的詮解向度──以「道德」為討論中心 385 依牟先生之說，老子之「道」所展現的客觀實體性，實際上只是一種姿 態： 此道之遍在而為體為母，亦不是「存有形態」之為體為母，只是 境界形態沖虛之所照……此遍在之體是「虛」義，非「實」義。 儼若有客觀實體之姿態，（有客觀性、實體性之姿態），實則只 是一姿態，故非「存有形態」也。 8 牟先生將道家之「道」貞定在實踐的意義中，認為「道」不宜由思辨開 出本體義，不似儒家「天理」具實有創生義，「『道生』是個境界，道 就寄託于這個主觀實踐所呈現的境界；由此講生，就是消極意義的不生 之生」 9。此認為道家形上學為一種靜觀式、美學式的「境界形態」， 而非思辨的、創生的「實有形態」，可謂近代學界的典範之說。然而， 在吳澄對於《老子》的詮解中，老子之「道德」並非僅具橫攝、觀照的 意義，而是同於儒家「縱貫縱講」的實有創生形態，既具「作用層」亦 具「存有層」的意義。在《道德真經註》中，「道」不只是境界，同時 是宇宙萬物創生的根源、存在的第一因： 無名者，道也，天地亦由此道而生，故謂之始。 10 宗，猶宗子之宗。宗者，族之統；道者，萬物之統，故曰「萬物 之宗」。……謂道果誰之子乎？天先乎萬物，而道又在天之先， 則天亦由道而生，無有在道之先者矣。（卷1，第4 章，頁6b） 「道」創生天地萬物，其次序乃先生「天地」，進而再生「萬物」，故 言「道」是天地之始，這是就時間上言。而就邏輯上言，「道」是天地 萬物生成的第一因，是天地之所以為天地、萬物之所以為萬物的依據； 在「道」之前無可追溯，故言「道」是「萬物之統」、「萬物之宗」、 形上學的觀看潮流中，第一位造成《老子》實踐形上學觀看方式的突破和回歸。」見 然等同於「德」，而是「德之容」，言下之意是我們必須以形氣所見， 方可窺知此似可見又不可見的「德」的容貌、樣態。在此意義下，「德」 似乎與「形氣」不同層次，而與「道」同為形上層次。退一步說，即便 「德」未必同於「道」，然借用徐復觀所言，至少應是「介乎無形質與 有形質之間的一種狀態」 16，介於「要分化而尚未分化」 17之間，仍屬 形上層次，而不會落於形下。按筆者觀察，吳澄所詮解的「德」，實具 「以理釋《老》」可以作為吳澄解《老》的概括性總結，若聚焦在 「道德」這個主題上，吳澄乃用宋儒慣用的「理氣」作為詮解時的方便 法門。然而，若因此而將老子之「道德」與理學家之「理氣」視作等同， 15 歷代註解多將首章此處斷句在「此兩者，同出而異名」，吳澄以己意改為「此兩者 同，出而異名」，將「兩者」解為道與德，「出」解為「德自道中出」，甚能扣合前、 後註解脈絡，可謂其創見。 16 莊子所謂『無有』也。」理學家所講的「天理」，包括儒家所提 倡的仁、義、禮、智等道德規範。吳氏《老子注》中的「道」義 具有此種屬性。 18 按此，黃釗認為吳澄所詮解的老子之「道」，實可和理學家之「太極」 或「理」相通，而具儒家道德規範屬性。劉怡君亦曾言： 吳澄於注解《老子》第一章時，開宗明義指出：「道指形而上之 理不雜乎氣者而言。」認為老子思想中的「道」與理學思想中的 「理」可以統一融攝，此句話誠為「道理合一」詮解模式的根基， 透顯出老學與理學融合互攝的無限可能。……吳澄為了會通儒道， 在詮解《老子》時就必然有所發揮，所謂發揮，意指吳澄賦予老 子之「道」新的內涵，使「道」也成為儒家倫理的根本，與儒家 之「理」相通，成為天地萬物「所以然」的最高準則。 19 前輩學者大抵是依傍第一章「道為形而上之理不雜乎氣者而言」一句， 言此「理」即理學家之「理」，包含了儒家的倫理道德規範。劉怡君更 進一步認為吳澄有「會通儒道」的目的，而將老子之「道」與儒家之 「理」相融通，成為「道理合一」的詮解模式。筆者欲提出的反思是， 是否我們在文本中見一「理」字，便能將它和理學家所談之「理」等同 視之？吳澄所詮解的老子之「道」，果真和理學家的「理」字之義理內 蘊相同嗎？筆者認為答案是否定的，理由有二，以下分而述之。 （一）「無為」為終極價值，「仁義」為次德目 18 黃釗主編：《道家思想史綱》（長沙：湖南師範大學出版社，1991 年），頁559。另 外，劉固盛亦和黃氏有相同的見解，詳見氏著：《宋元老學研究》（成都：巴蜀書社， 2001 年），頁165。 19 劉怡君：《吳澄《道德真經註》研究──兼論理學與老學的交涉》，（臺北：東吳 大學中國文學系碩博士班碩士論文，2006 年），頁113。 第十八章，吳澄將其與十七章、十九章合併為一段完整的政治論，是以 他說這段話乃是沿著前述「大道廢有仁義」的進一步延伸說明。吳澄詮 解的「大道廢有仁義」，是指理想政治的「一降」。當「相忘於無為」 的「大道之世」無法實現，便降下一等而為「仁義之世」。按此，他並 非以為老子從根本上否定仁義，而是深刻地理解老子是以「無為」作為 終極價值，而將「仁義」置為次德目 20。所謂「無為之治」，即是要讓 百姓自然而然各安其生，不受外在力量的干涉、限制，是以他注文中接 著說「尊卑長幼各由其道」、「君臣上下各由其道」的「道」的意涵， 雖確實指尊卑長幼、君臣上下要各自安頓在自己的位份上，但更重要的 是要強調他們是「自然而然地實踐他們的位份」，不是基於外在力量的 約束，也不是因為價值標榜的追求。整段注解的重點應在後面的「子之 孝者迺其常分，不知其為孝」、「臣之忠者亦其常分，不知其為忠」， 20 細察吳澄的註解脈絡可以發現，他仍是在老學系統內而非儒學系統內作詮解。而分 判老學系統抑或為儒學系統的標準，在於終極價值的定位差異。若是老學系統，便以 「無為」為終極價值；而若是儒學系統，則以「仁義」為最終價值。誠如杜保瑞所言： 「無為是老學最高價值，仁義是其次德目，未能先做到無為，仁義即淪於虛假，真做 到無為，仁義才可逐步實現。……儒學價值始終入世心切，故而永遠以仁義關懷為價 值標舉，只其操作時以無為為實得之境界，故而我們說儒學系統內的孔老互補是以仁 義為終極價值及以無為為境界，以有別於老學系統內的孔老互補是以無為為終極價值 而以仁義為次德目。」見氏著：〈儒道互補價值觀念的方法論探究〉，《哲學與文化》 28 卷11 期（2001 年11 月），頁1006、1007。 吳澄《道德真經註》的詮解向度──以「道德」為討論中心 391 意即當「孝」和「忠」不必再特別提倡、表彰，而是自然而然實踐之時， 方是「相忘於無為」的「大道之世」、「無為之治」。按照這樣的思路， 吳澄所說的「尊卑長幼君臣」之「道」，是以「無為」作為前提而言的 人倫規範，「自然無為」是較人倫規範更高一層的追求。在這樣的意義 之下，吳澄雖言老子之「道」是「理」，然是否可斷然等同於儒家之 「天理」，則需更謹慎地判斷。且若進一步仔細考察《道德真經註》中 對於「理」的論述，也可發現它確是以「無為自然」作為基本精神，已 和理學家所論之「天理」展現不同的風貌，例如其注第五十四章云： 凡此不欲、不學者，蓋以萬物之理無為而自然，故吾亦無為而與 萬物同一自然，如輔之於輪輻相依附而為一也。（卷4，頁8a-b） 所謂「不欲、不學者」，按前文所論即指聖人。當財貨被推擁成難得珍 貴、所學受標榜而使人追求，則容易造成人心的貪圖與爭逐，導致社會 紛擾不安。聖人不追求眾人所欲、眾人所學，而與「萬物之理」相同， 同樣「無為而自然」，意即聖人不落入相對價值對於人心的拘鎖，僅順 任自然而為。「萬物之理」既「無為而自然」，那麼只要人能做到「無 為」，便是實踐此天地之理，便可和此天理貫通為一。此種工夫和境界 的展現，明顯有別於儒家，全然是道家義理特色。另外，前文中嘗論及 老子注解第一章云：「其道其德以虛無自然為體，以柔弱不盈為用」 （卷1，第1 章，頁2b），以「虛無自然」、「柔弱不盈」作為「道 德」的體用，所展現的，仍是一派道家本色，而異於理學家所論之「天 理」。 （二）藉注《老》分判儒、道 按筆者觀察，吳澄注《老》的目的，或許根本不是為會通儒道，而 是為分判儒道。吳澄對於老子所論的「道」的性質，是相當不以為然的。 他在《吳文正集》中，有諸多針對老子之「道」和理學家之「理」的義 理分判，可見他很清楚地意識到，在不同論述系統下的「道」／「理」， 義理內蘊自然有所不同。例如在〈答田副使第二書〉中，他說： 《東亞漢學研究》2017 特別號 392 蓋宋儒之言道，周子微發其端而已，其說之詳而明，直待張子、 二程子出，而後人知二子所言之道與老莊所言自無而有者不同， 故論程、張二子，有功於吾道者，以其能辨異端似是之非也。 21 吳澄明確指出，由周敦頤至張載、二程為宋儒一系代表，他們所論之 「道」和老莊所言之「道」是不同的，並說老莊之論為「異端似是之 非」。究其原因，在於老子所言之「道」（即「理」）、「氣」關係， 是「自無而有」、「有無二分」，然宋儒所論之「理氣」，是「有無不 二」。這樣的論述在《吳文正集》中所在多有： 老子云：「天下萬物生於有，有生於無」者，指動植之類而言。 「有」字，指陰陽之氣而言，「無」字，指無形之道體而言，此 老子本旨也。理在氣中，元不相離，老子以為先有理而後有氣， 横渠張子詆其有生於無之非，晦庵先生詆其有無為二之非。 22 老子謂有氣之陰陽，自無形之理而生，以有無為二，而不知理氣 之不可分先後。 23 吳澄以「無形之道體」釋「有生於無」的「無」，以「氣」釋「有」， 若按此詮解，老子之「有生於無」便成為「氣生於道（理）」，有「道 （理）在氣先」、「（道）理氣二分」之意。此說為吳澄所大大反對， 他認為「有無」應「為一」，即「理氣」應無分先後、相即不離 24，他 更依此作為儒道之辨的依據。蓋宋儒以至吳澄會反老子「有生於無」之 說，乃因將「無」視作「虛無」、「空無」，一旦為「虛無」、「空 無」，自然無法和宋儒亟欲建立的儒家的道德形上實體相契。實際上， 21 ［元］吳澄：〈答田副使第二書〉，《吳文正集》（臺北：臺灣商務印書館，1983 年《景印文淵閣四庫全書》，冊1197），卷3，頁12b。 22 ［元］吳澄：〈答田副使第三書〉，《吳文正集》，卷3，頁29a-b。 23 ［元］吳澄：〈答田副使第三書〉，《吳文正集》，卷3，頁30b。 24 吳澄認為理氣無分先後且相即不離，這在《吳文正集》中多有論述，例如〈答人問 性理〉中言：「理者，非别有一物在氣中，只是為氣之主宰者；即是無理外之氣，亦 無氣外之理。」此即明言理為氣之主宰，然理氣不二；理為氣之形上根據，氣則使無 形之裡有頓放之處，是以〈答海南海北道廉訪副使田君澤問〉中說：「蓋老、莊、列 之意，皆以為先有理而後有氣，至宋朝二程、横渠出，力闢老氏自無而有之說為非， 而曰：『理氣不可分先後，理是無形之物，若未有氣，理在那處頓放？』又曰：『理 與氣有則俱有，未嘗相離，非知道者孰能識之！』程、張之所以為知道，正以其能識 得此與老氏之說不同故也。」凡此種種，均表現出吳澄認為理氣不二、未有先後的觀 念。分見《吳文正集》，卷2，頁18a；卷3，頁2b-3a、。 吳澄《道德真經註》的詮解向度──以「道德」為討論中心 393 老子所言之「無」為遮詮字，其遮「有」所顯示的正面意義為「自然無 為」，吳澄雖明白提示出「無為」為《老子》一書之旨 25，但其對於 「有生於無」的理解卻落入消極之「虛無」義，老子「有生於無」又在 其詮解下成為「氣生於理」、「理先氣後」，如此，遂使其所詮解的老 子之「道」（「理」），和理學家所談之「理」，展現截然不同的樣貌。 二者雖均用「理」字表詮，但各自之義理內蘊、與「氣」的關聯等實不 相同，故若要說吳澄將老子之「道」和理學家之「理」相綰合，實會略 顯牽強。 四、結論 吳澄《道德真經註》的詮解向度，學者多以「以理釋《老》」概括 論之。此一詮解向度的基砥在於吳澄將宋儒論述「天理」的「縱貫縱講」 詮釋視域沿用至對老子「道德」的討論，使「縱貫橫講」、「主觀境界 型態」的《老子》不再只有靜觀式、美學式的形上學，而為實有創生型 態。是以在《道德真經註》中，可以見到吳澄賦予老子「道德」有本體 宇宙論的實有創生意義，就這一點而言，確可視《道德真經註》中的 「道德」和儒家的「天理」有高度的一致性。「理」和「道」因具十分 相似的形上學意味而能交相比附，然而，實不可斷言二者可以完全通同， 原因有二：一是綜觀《道德真經註》中對於「道」或「理」的討論，均 可發現吳澄乃視「無為」為終極價值，「仁義」則為次德目。由此可知， 其詮解仍在道家系統裡；老子之「道」，在吳澄的解釋下，仍不同於於 穆不已的「天理」。二是無論在《道德真經註》或《吳文正集》的書信 紀錄中，均可發現吳澄對於儒、道二家實有極為明確的分判意識，而其 分判的切入點，即是二家對於「道」／「理」和「氣」關係詮釋的不同 ──老子是「自無而有」、「理氣二分」，這是吳澄極不贊同的。因此， 前人學者論吳澄詮解老子之「道」即等於理學之「理」，或許是較為倉 促及過度詮釋的結果。 25 吳澄嘗明確指出「無為」為《老子》一書之宗旨，其注第五十四章云：「凡以無為 而為者，老氏宗旨也」（卷4，頁5b）。

This academic paper, written by 楊筑 and published in 《東亞漢學研究》2017 特別號, examines Wu Cheng's (吳澄, 1249-1333) interpretive approach in his commentary 《道德真經註》 on the Laozi, focusing on the concept of "moral/dao and de" (道德). Wu Cheng, a fourth-generation disciple of Zhu Xi who was also influenced by Lu Xiangshan (known for "和會朱陸" or reconciling Zhu and Lu), was a Yuan dynasty Neo-Confucian scholar who commented on the Laozi while at Qingdu Temple in 1307. His commentary is characterized by "以理釋《老》" (interpreting the Laozi through the concept of li/principle).

The paper's central arguments are threefold:
1. **The interpretive foundation**: Wu Cheng understood the Laozi's "道" (Dao) through the Neo-Confucian "縱貫縱講" (vertical/creative) interpretive framework rather than the "縱貫橫講" (horizontal/subjective) framework that Mou Zongsan later applied to Daoism. In Wu's commentary, Dao is not merely a state/boundary (境界形態) but possesses real creative ontological status, generating the universe ("無名者，道也，天地亦由此道而生"). Wu interprets the creation sequence as 道→一(沖虛一氣) →二(陰陽) →三, incorporating "德" (virtue/de) as the "一" into the cosmic generation scheme, thereby bridging the gap that Han dynasty 氣化宇宙論 (qi-based cosmology) had created between Dao and all things.

2. **A critical reassessment**: The paper challenges scholars like Huang Zhao and Liu Yijun who equate Wu's interpretation of the Dao with the Neo-Confucian "天理" (Heavenly Principle). The author argues against this for two reasons:
   - **First**, in Wu's commentary, 無為 (non-action) serves as the ultimate value, while 仁義 (benevolence and righteousness) remain secondary virtues. This places Wu's interpretation firmly within the Daoist system, differentiating it from Neo-Confucian thought where 仁義 constitutes the Heavenly Principle itself. Wu's commentary on chapters 16/18 emphasizes that filial piety and loyalty should be practiced naturally as "常分" (ordinary duty), not through external promotion.
   - **Second**, Wu's purpose in commenting on the Laozi was to distinguish (分判) rather than reconcile Confucianism and Daoism. In the 《吳文正集》, Wu explicitly criticizes the Laoist view of "自無而有" ("有生於無") as implying 理氣二分 (division of li and qi) and 理先氣後 (li prior to qi), which Wu rejects in favor of the Neo-Confucian position that 理氣 are inseparable and without priority. Wu regarded the Laozi's teaching as "異端似是之非" (heterodox doctrine resembling the truth).

**Conclusion**: While Wu's commentary does grant the Dao real creative ontological status similar to the Neo-Confucian 天理 (justifying the "以理釋《老》" characterization), the author argues that Wu maintained a clear distinction between the Daoist interpretation of 道/理 and the Neo-Confucian 理. Wu never equated the Dao of the Laozi with the 天理, as the ultimate values differ (無為 vs. 仁義) and their respective relationships with qi differ fundamentally (理氣二分 vs. 理氣不二). Thus, prior scholars' claims of full identity between Wu's Dao and the Neo-Confucian 理 constitute over-interpretation.

|  | 吳澄（1249-1333）《道德真經註》的詮解向度，學者多以「以理釋《老》」概括論之。此一詮解向度的基砥在於吳澄依其身為理學家的「前見」，將宋儒論述「天理」的「縱貫縱講」詮釋視域沿用至對老子「道德」的討論，使「縱貫橫講」、「主觀境界型態」的《老子》不再只有靜觀式、美學式的形上學，而為實有創生型態。是以在《道德真經註》中，可以見到吳澄賦予老子「道德」有本體宇宙論的實有創生意義，就這一點而言，確可視《道德真經註》中的「道德」和儒家的「天理」有高度的一致性。 　　「理」和「道」因具十分相似的形上學意味而能交相比附，吳澄遂融攝張載、朱熹之理氣論於注解之中，使得《道德真經註》富有濃厚的儒道會通氣息。然而，或不可斷言「理」、「道」二者可以完全通同，原因有二：一是綜觀《道德真經註》中對於「道」或「理」的討論，均可發現吳澄乃以「無為」為終極價值，「仁義」則為次德目，由此可知，其詮解仍在道家脈絡之中。二是無論在《道德真經註》或《吳文正集》的書信紀錄中，均可發現吳澄對於儒、道二家實有極為明確的判教意識，而其分判的切入點，即是儒、道二家對於「道」／「理」與「氣」的關係理解有異──老子是「自無而有」、「理氣二分」，這是吳澄極不贊同的。因此，前人學者論吳澄詮解老子之「道」即等於理學之「理」，或許是可再商榷的。 　　至於吳澄對《老子》心性修養工夫與政治論述所運用的詮解策略，均是採取形上學的進路，即由形下的人間世向形上的「道」作探求；其操作的模式蓋是先由「內觀」契悟形上之「道」的原理，再以「道」的性徵作為人行於世的原則。「道」的核心要義為「自然」，通徹到人身是「人性自然」，落實到政治是「無為之治」。在「人性自然」的前提下，遂開展出由無身到有身的精神修養與養生工夫；而在「無為之治」的意義下，則能勾稽聖人與百姓之間「無為－自化」的「治道－道治」結構，進而能勾勒由此結構所開顯的理想政治圖景。 |

args.key_excerpts: 吳澄（1249-1333）《道德真經註》的詮解向度，學者多以「以理釋《老》」概括論之。此一詮解向度的基砥在於吳澄依其身為理學家的「前見」，將宋儒論述「天理」的「縱貫縱講」詮釋視域沿用至對老子「道德」的討論，使「縱貫橫講」、「主觀境界型態」的《老子》不再只有靜觀式、美學式的形上學，而為實有創生型態。", "綜觀《道德真經註》中對於「道」或「理」的討論，均可發現吳澄乃以「無為」為終極價值，「仁義」則為次德目，由此可知，其詮解仍在道家脈絡之中。", "無論在《道德真經註》或《吳文正集》的書信紀錄中，均可發現吳澄對於儒、道二家實有極為明確的判教意識，而其分判的切入點，即是儒、道二家對於「道」／「理」與「氣」的關係理解有異──老子是「自無而有」、「理氣二分」，這是吳澄極不贊同的。", "吳澄對《老子》心性修養工夫與政治論述所運用的詮解策略，均是採取形上學的進路，即由形下的人間世向形上的「道」作探求；其操作的模式蓋是先由「內觀」契悟形上之「道」的原理，再以「道」的性徵作為人行於世的原則。", "「道」的核心要義為「自然」，通徹到人身是「人性自然」，落實到政治是「無為之治」。
args.summary:
This webpage is a record from Taiwan's National Digital Library of Theses and Dissertations (NDLTD) detailing a Master's thesis titled "吳澄《道德真經註》之詮解向度" (The Hermeneutic Dimensions of Wu Cheng's 'Annotation of the True Classic of the Way and Virtue').

**Thesis Bibliographic Details:**
- Author: 楊筑 (Yang, Zhu)
- Advisor: 江淑君 (Jiang Shujun)
- Institution: 國立臺灣師範大學 (National Taiwan Normal University), Department of Chinese Literature
- Degree type: Master's thesis (碩士)
- Year: 2017 (graduating year 105)
- Language: Chinese (中文)
- Pages: 130
- Permanent URL: https://hdl.handle.net/11296/86fj4f
- Chinese keywords: 吳澄 (Wu Cheng), 《道德真經註》, 詮解向度 (hermeneutic dimensions), 儒道會通 (Confucian-Daoist integration), 宋元老學 (Song-Yuan Laozi studies)
- Usage statistics: cited once, 297 views, 46 downloads, 0 bookmarks

**Abstract (Core Argument):**
Wu Cheng (1249-1333), a Neo-Confucian thinker, interpreted the Laozi (Dao De Jing) through the lens of "以理釋《老》" (explaining Laozi through principle/li). Wu applied the Song Confucian vertical hermeneutic framework of "天理" (Heavenly principle) to Laozi's concepts of "道/德" (Way/Virtue), giving them an ontological and cosmological creative meaning. His interpretation incorporated Zhang Zai and Zhu Xi's li-qi (principle-material force) theory, creating a strong Confucian-Daoist integration.

However, the thesis argues that "理" and "道" cannot be completely equated for two reasons:
1. In his commentary, Wu Cheng still treats "無為" (wu-wei/non-action) as the ultimate value and "仁義" (benevolence/righteousness) as secondary, placing his interpretation within the Daoist framework
2. Wu maintained a clear distinction between Confucianism and Daoism based on their differing understanding of the relationship between "道/理" and "氣" — Laozi's "自無而有" (from nothing to being) and "理氣二分" (separation of li and qi) is something Wu disagreed with

The thesis also examines Wu's metaphysical approach to spiritual cultivation (內聖) and political discourse (外王), where "自然" (naturalness/ziran) in personal cultivation becomes "人性自然" (natural human nature) and in politics becomes "無為之治" (governance through non-action).

**Thesis Structure (Table of Contents):**
- Chapter 1: Introduction (problem formation, prior research, scope and methods)
- Chapter 2: Wu Cheng's life and works (biography, historical context, academic tendencies, overview of works)
- Chapter 3: "Ethics" discussion under Confucian perspective ("以理釋道" and "以《易》解道" hermeneutic approaches)
- Chapter 4: Integrating Confucian-Daoist "inner sage" cultivation and "outer king" political vision
- Chapter 5: Conclusion and future prospects

**Reference List Highlights:**
The thesis includes extensive references to classical texts (Heshang Gong's commentary, Wang Bi, Zhang Zai, Cheng brothers, Zhu Xi, Wu Cheng's own texts), modern scholarship (Mou Zongsan, Xu Fuguan, Laozi studies), and related theses including 劉怡君's "吳澄《道德真經註》研究──兼論理學與老學的交涉" (2006).

**Related Theses (User-Provided Citations):**
Related works include studies on Wu Cheng's Yijing commentaries, his Dao De Jing commentary, and other Laozi commentary studies.

吳澄（1249-1333）《道德真經註》的詮解向度，學者多以「以理釋《老》」概括論之。此一詮解向度的基砥在於吳澄依其身為理學家的「前見」，將宋儒論述「天理」的「縱貫縱講」詮釋視域沿用至對老子「道德」的討論，使「縱貫橫講」、「主觀境界型態」的《老子》不再只有靜觀式、美學式的形上學，而為實有創生型態。是以在《道德真經註》中，可以見到吳澄賦予老子「道德」有本體宇宙論的實有創生意義，就這一點而言，確可視《道德真經註》中的「道德」和儒家的「天理」有高度的一致性。 　　「理」和「道」因具十分相似的形上學意味而能交相比附，吳澄遂融攝張載、朱熹之理氣論於注解之中，使得《道德真經註》富有濃厚的儒道會通氣息。然而，或不可斷言「理」、「道」二者可以完全通同，原因有二：一是綜觀《道德真經註》中對於「道」或「理」的討論，均可發現吳澄乃以「無為」為終極價值，「仁義」則為次德目，由此可知，其詮解仍在道家脈絡之中。二是無論在《道德真經註》或《吳文正集》的書信紀錄中，均可發現吳澄對於儒、道二家實有極為明確的判教意識，而其分判的切入點，即是儒、道二家對於「道」／「理」與「氣」的關係理解有異──老子是「自無而有」、「理氣二分」，這是吳澄極不贊同的。因此，前人學者論吳澄詮解老子之「道」即等於理學之「理」，或許是可再商榷的。 　　至於吳澄對《老子》心性修養工夫與政治論述所運用的詮解策略，均是採取形上學的進路，即由形下的人間世向形上的「道」作探求；其操作的模式蓋是先由「內觀」契悟形上之「道」的原理，再以「道」的性徵作為人行於世的原則。「道」的核心要義為「自然」，通徹到人身是「人性自然」，落實到政治是「無為之治」。在「人性自然」的前提下，遂開展出由無身到有身的精神修養與養生工夫；而在「無為之治」的意義下，則能勾稽聖人與百姓之間「無為－自化」的「治道－道治」結構，進而能勾勒由此結構所開顯的理想政治圖景。

args.summary:
This webpage presents an academic thesis page from the Airiti Library (華藝線上圖書館) for a master's thesis titled 《吳澄《道德真經註》之詮解向度》(The Interpretive Dimensions of Wu Cheng's Commentary on the Daodejing), authored by 楊筑 (Yang Zhu), advised by 江淑君 (Jiang Shujun), at the Department of Chinese Literature, National Taiwan Normal University (國立臺灣師範大學/國文學系), dated 2017. DOI: https://doi.org/10.6345/NTNU202202745.

COMMUNITY SUMMARY OF THE THESIS:
- Scholars have generally characterized Wu Cheng's (吳澄, 1249-1333) interpretation of the Daodejing Commentary as "interpreting the Laozi through principle (li)" (以理釋《老》), based on Wu's status as a Neo-Confucian (理學家).
- Wu Cheng applied the Song Confucian "vertical-preaching" interpretive horizon of "Heavenly Principle" (天理) to Laozi's discussion of "moral/way and virtue" (道德), transforming the Laozi from a contemplative, aesthetic metaphysics into one with genuinely creative (generative) significance—giving Laozi's "moral" an ontological-cosmological creative meaning, making it highly consistent with Confucian "Heavenly Principle."
- Because "principle" (理) and "Way" (道) share similar metaphysical implications and can be compared, Wu Cheng integrated the li-qi (理氣, principle-energy) theories of Zhang Zai (張載) and Zhu Xi (朱熹) into his annotations, giving the Commentary a strong flavor of Confucian-Daoist convergence.

HOWEVER, the thesis argues that "principle" and "Way" cannot be fully equated, for two reasons:
1. Throughout the Commentary, Wu Cheng took "non-action" (無為) as the ultimate value with "benevolence and righteousness" (仁義) as secondary virtues, showing his interpretation remained within the Daoist framework.
2. Both in the Commentary and his correspondence in the Wu Wenzheng ji (吳文正集), Wu Cheng displayed a clear doctrinal-differentiation (判教) consciousness between Confucianism and Daoism, centered on differing understandings of the relationship between "Way"/"principle" and "qi" (氣)—Laozi's view that the universe arises "from nothing to being" (自無而有) with "principle-qi split" (理氣二分) was something Wu Cheng strongly disapproved of. Therefore, previous scholars' equation of Wu Cheng's "Way" with Neo-Confucian "principle" is questionable.

INTERPRETIVE STRATEGY: Wu Cheng's approach to Laozi's self-cultivation practices and political discourse both adopted a metaphysical route—seeking from the physical human world upward to the metaphysical "Way." The operational model involves first penetrating the principle of the "Way" through "inner contemplation" (內觀), then taking the Way's characteristics as principles for human conduct. The core meaning of "Way" is "spontaneity/naturalness" (自然): applied to the self it is "natural human nature" (人性自然), and applied to politics it is "governance through non-action" (無為之治). From "natural human nature" unfolds cultivation of spirit and regimen from having no self (無身) to having self (有身); from "governance through non-action" is traced the "non-action–self-transformation" (無為－自化) structure of "governing the Way–being governed by the Way" (治道－道治) between sage and the people, thereby outlining an ideal political vision.

KEYWORDS: 吳澄 (Wu Cheng); 《道德真經註》 (Daodejing Commentary); 詮解向度 (interpretive dimensions); 儒道會通 (Confucian-Daoist convergence); 宋元老學 (Song-Yuan Laozi studies).

Key classical references cited include: Heshanggong's Commentary (增訂河上公注疏證, 2008); Wang Bi & Han Kangbo's Zhouyi with Kong Yingda's commentary (1955); Zhang Zai's Zhengmeng (正蒙); and Shao Yong's Huangji jingshi (皇極經世書). The page also includes links to the NTNU institutional repository and fulltext access points.

This webpage is a reference/bibliography page from the Hans Publisher journal (hanspub.org), containing the reference list for a Chinese academic article on the Dao De Jing (道德经/Laozi) and associated philosophical themes.

The reference list contains 28 sources spanning:
- Classical Chinese Daoist commentaries on the Laozi: Heshang Gong's '道德真经注', Wang Bi's '道德真经注', Cheng Xuanying's '老子道德經開題序訣義疏', Wu Cheng's '道德真經注', Fan Yingyuan's '老子道德經古本集註', Chen Jingyuan's '道德真經藏室纂微篇', Lü Zhichang's '道德經講義', and Hong Yingshao's '道德經測' (all published in the 老子集成 collection, 宗教文化出版社, 2011).
- Modern Chinese scholarship: Chen Guying's '老子今注今译' (商务印书馆, 2003) and '老子注译及评介' (中华书局, 2009), and Liu Xiaogan's '老子古今' (中国社会科学出版社, 2005).
- Neo-Confucian/other classical works: Zhu Xi's '朱子全书', Wang Fuzhi's '老子衍' and '张子正蒙注', Dai Zhen's '孟子字义疏证'.
- Western philosophical works: Heidegger's '林中路' (Holzwege, trans. Sun Zhouxing), Hans-Georg Gadamer's '真理与方法' (Truth and Method), Whitehead's '过程与实在' (Process and Reality).
- Eco-philosophy sources: Naess (1973) 'The Shallow and the Deep, Long-Range Ecology Movement' (Inquiry, 16), Jonas (1985) 'The Imperative of Responsibility', Holling (1973) 'Resilience and Stability of Ecological Systems' (Annual Review of Ecology and Systematics, 4).
- A People's Daily article on Ames (安乐哲) on letting Chinese philosophy speak Chinese.

Based on the cited sources—particularly the combination of classical Daoist commentaries with Deep Ecology (Naess), Jonas's responsibility ethics, Holling's resilience theory, and Whitehead's process philosophy—the article appears to connect Daoist thought (especially concepts from the Laozi) with contemporary ecological and process philosophy themes. The bibliography is presented twice on the page.

This webpage is an academic journal article record from an Airiti Library database (a Chinese academic platform). The article is "成玄英《道德經義疏》重玄思想之探析" (Exploration and Analysis of Cheng Xuan-ying's Twofold Mystery Thoughts in Dao De Jing Yi Shu), written by 林文彬 (Wen-Ping Lin), published in 《興大中文學報》(Journal of the Chinese Department of National Chung Hsing University), Issue 29, June 2011, pages 179-192. DOI: https://doi.org/10.30091/JCDNCHU.201106.0007.

The article examines Cheng Xuan-ying (成玄英), an important representative of the School of Twofold Mystery (重玄學派) in the Early Tang Dynasty. The Dao De Jing Yi Shu is his foundational work, which uses the "Twofold Mystery" (重玄) concept to establish an ontological realm of unobstructed reason (虛通之理) and emphasize cultivation of the mind and nature through wisdom (智悟).

The paper identifies three academic contributions of the work: (1) Regarding Laozi studies, it links academia and religion while summarizing predecessors' theories; (2) In Chinese intellectual history, it represents a third period of Taoist thought development after Wei-Jin Xuanxue, serving as a fusion of Xuanxue (Neo-Taoism) and Buddhist Prajñā (Wisdom); (3) In terms of influence, it is the most philosophically significant school in Taoist history, influencing Song and Yuan dynasty Inner Alchemy (Neidan) and the Science of Mind-Nature, and likely enlightening Neo-Confucianism development.

The historical context notes that Sun Deng of the Eastern Jin Dynasty first annotated Laozi using the Twofold Mystery concept, and from the Southern and Northern Dynasties through the Sui and Tang Dynasties, many Taoists used it to comment on Laozi and Zhuangzi, forming the School of Twofold Mystery.

Keywords: 成玄英 (Cheng Xuan-ying); 重玄 (Twofold Mystery); 道德經 (Dao De Jing); 虛通之理 (unobstructed reason); 眾生之性 (nature of beings).

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is an academic paper (published in *Studies in Sinology* / 《中國學術年刊》, Volume 36, Autumn issue, September 2014, pp. 19-42, ISSN 1021-7851) by Chiang Shu-chun (National Taiwan Normal University, Department of Chinese) examining the theory of mind-nature (心性論述, xinxing) in Cheng Xuan-ying's (成玄英) commentary on the Daodejing, titled 《道德經開題序訣義疏》 (Dao Der Jing Kai Ti Xu Jue Yi Shu).

CORE ARGUMENT: The paper analyzes the theoretical structure of Cheng Xuan-ying's discussions of mind (心), nature (性), emotions (情), and desire (欲) in his Daodejing commentary, and explores their deep relationship with Buddhist thought. In the early Tang dynasty, Buddhist mind-nature theory had matured, and Daoist Chongxuan (double mystery, 重玄) studies required development of mind-nature theory, leading Daoist commentators on the Laozi to focus on "mind" and "nature" topics while integrating Buddhist thought.

THREE OBSERVATIONAL APPROACHES (the paper's structure):
1. "Dao-Nature Continuity" (道、性一貫) as the ideological premise: Cheng holds that "Dao" and "nature" are one — the innate natural nature/true nature of all beings derives from the transcendent Dao. He explains "Dao" as "void and penetrating" (虛通), and states "所謂無極大道，是眾生之正性也" (the infinite great Dao is the true nature of all beings). He uses "principle" (理) to characterize Dao, marking a major breakthrough in his Laozi scholarship. Dao's subtle principle, when internalized in humans and things, becomes their nature; hence to "preserve and return to true nature" is the path of self-cultivation.
2. "Forgetting Emotions to Complete Nature" (忘情全性) as the master thesis: In commenting on "道可道，非常道," Cheng details the relations among Dao, nature, emotions, form (形), qi (炁), and spirit (神). Since "性動為情" (nature stirring becomes emotion) and emotions contaminate, nature is damaged and distances from Dao. The key statement: "生我者道，滅我者情，茍忘其情，則全乎性" (Dao gives me life, emotions destroy me; if one forgets emotions, nature is made complete). The dialectical process runs: Dao-Nature originally one → Dao-Nature separated (through stirring emotions, deluded mind chasing external objects) → Dao-Nature re-united through cultivation ("復性歸道" / returning nature to Dao as ultimate aim).
3. "Deluded Mind," "Emotional Contamination," and "Attachment to Objects" (妄心、情染、滯境) and the path of cultivation: Cheng identifies deluded mind, emotional contamination, and attachment to sensory objects as the root causes of losing true nature. His cultivation approach incorporates extensive Buddhist concepts — "empty" (空), "mind abiding nowhere" (無所住心), "three karmas clean" (三業清靜), "liberation of six sense faculties" (六根解脫), the bodhisattva ideal, "three poisons" (貪嗔痴), "dependent arising and emptiness" (緣起性空), etc. He reframes the Daoist sage as a bodhisattva-like figure; explains "returning to root/stillness/mandate" (歸根復命); and advocates for "復於真性，反於惠命" (returning to true nature and inherent mandate).

CONCLUSIONS (two observations):
1. The mind-nature discourse of early Tang Chongxuan studies may have independently influenced the mid-Tang Confucian revival (e.g., Li Ao's (李翱) 《復性書》/ "Essay on Restoring Nature," which also advocates "滅情復性" / extinguishing emotions to restore nature). The paper argues the theory of "restoring nature" (復性) was initiated by Cheng Xuan-ying well before Li Ao, challenging the view that Laozi mind-nature interpretation only fully developed in the Song dynasty.
2. The paper highlights the distinctive features of Cheng Xuan-ying's mind-nature discourse in the 《義疏》 and evaluates his value and status in the history of Laozi scholarship — characterizing the early Tang Chongxuan mind-nature theory as marked by Buddhist-Daoist mutual influence, whereas Song Confucian-Laozi interpretation turned toward Confucian-Daoist convergence.

KEY SCHOLARS CITED: Li Gang (李剛) argues Cheng's theory of restoring nature is richer than Li Ao's and scattered across his Laozi/Zhuangzi commentaries; Tang Yi-jie (湯一介) sees Chongxuan philosophy moving from ontology to mind-nature philosophy, similar to Song-Ming Neo-Confucianism (especially Cheng-Zhu), urging attention to the Chongxuan-Song Neo-Confucianism relationship; Dong En-lin divides Tang Laozi studies into three stages (early: Chongxuan with Buddhist coloring; middle: Tang Xuanzong's politicization; late: compilations by Qiang Siqi and Du Guangting). The paper used the Yan Ling-feng (嚴靈峯) edition of the reconstructed 《義疏》 as primary text.

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage is from the Chinese Text Project (ctext.org), specifically the wiki section of the Chinese Philosophy Digital Project, presenting the text "道德真經玄德纂疏卷一" (Volume 1 of the Moral Classic's Dark Virtue Compilation Commentary). This is a Daoist commentary on the Daodejing (Tao Te Ching) compiled by Xiqiang Si (濛陽強思齊), featuring annotations from Tang Emperor Xuanzong (唐玄宗, imperial commentary), He Shang Gong (河上公), Yan Junping (嚴君平), Li Rong (李榮), and Cheng Xuanying (成玄英).

The text opens with an introduction describing the Daodejing as the crown of the three teachings and leader of all scriptures. The first chapter (道可道章第一) is divided into four sections: (1) marking the principle and teaching, (2) broadly clarifying root and traces, (3) distinguishing the two contemplations (of Existence and Non-existence), and (4) unifying the "double mystery" (重玄) principle.

Key content includes extensive commentary on the opening lines: "道可道，非常道" (The Dao that can be spoken is not the eternal Dao) and "名可名，非常名" (The name that can be named is not the eternal name). The commentary explores the concept of the Three Ones (三一: essence, spirit, and qi) as the body of Laozi, discusses creation from primordial qi (元氣), and explains that the eternal Dao transcends speech, form, sound, and thought.

The second chapter (天下皆知章第二) addresses how "when all under heaven know beauty as beauty, ugliness arises" and "when all know goodness as goodness, non-goodness arises." Commentators discuss how relative concepts (existence/non-existence, difficulty/ease, long/short, high/low, sound/voice) are all empty of inherent reality, citing Zhuangzi and other sources. The text concludes with the "double mystery" concept (玄之又玄), where one must abandon attachment not only to existence and non-existence but also to the mystery itself as the gate to all wonders (眾妙之門).

This is a WeRead (微信读书) book page for 《道德真经注》(Commentary on the Tao Te Ching of True Scripture) written by 李荣 (Li Rong), a Daoist priest of the Tang Dynasty. It is an important early Daoist systematic commentary on the 《道德经》(Tao Te Ching/Laozi). Key details:

- The current edition is included in the 《正统道藏》洞神部 (Orthodox Daoist Canon, Dong Sheng section).
- The work originally had two volumes (上/下), commenting on the 36 chapters of the Tao Te Ching; the present edition is partially incomplete (残佚).
- Written during the early Tang when "重玄学" (Chongxuan/Twofold Mystery school) flourished; Li Rong extensively used 重玄 methods and integrated Confucian, Buddhist, and Daoist views.
- The commentary interprets Laozi's core concepts: "无为" (wuwei/non-action), "致虚" (attaining emptiness), "守静" (maintaining stillness), "返本" (returning to the origin).
- Unlike later detailed textual/philological commentaries, Li Rong's annotations are concise and clear, emphasizing the philosophical structure of Laozi's thought: "虚静" as the root of cultivating the mind, "无为" as essential to all affairs, "复归本真" (returning to true nature) as the foundation of self-cultivation.
- The work reflects Daoist practice/self-cultivation elements and shows the Tang Daoist trend of moving from "玄学" (Dark Learning/Xuanxue) toward systematic commentary.
- Valued as a key text for studying early Daoist thought, the Tao Te Ching commentary tradition, and the development of "重玄学". Suitable both as academic material and as an introductory reading for understanding the philosophical layers of the Tao Te Ching.

【成书过程】唐玄宗因认为以往各家对《道德经》的注疏"并未精当，有失玄元妙旨"，担心"无为之理将失"，而决定亲自作注。他一生两度注释《道德经》：开元二十三年（735年，时年51岁）首次完成《御注道德经》并颁之全国，诏令天下"士庶家藏一本，劝令习读"，此次采用河上公本《老子》为底本；约二十年后（天宝十四年，755年）进行第二次注疏，称《道德经真经疏》，因对河上公本不满意而改用王弼本为底本，并再次亲自作序颁于天下。

【内容结构】全书共四卷，分《道经》上下、《德经》上下各二卷，总计八十一章，每章以开头三五字为章名，依从古本。唐玄宗改定章句，"凡言道者类之上卷，言德者类之下卷"。流传中存在二卷本（如《新唐书·艺文志》所载）与四卷本（《道藏》本）之别。

【主要思想】御注的根本宗旨在于"理身理国"，核心是阐发老子的无为之理，并发展了这一哲学，具体体现在君德官德思想、民本与教化思想、"国际交往"思想及军事战争哲学中的自然无为、慈爱于人、节俭爱费、谦柔不争、公平无私等主张。

【刊刻与流传】开元二十三年（735年），唐玄宗采纳道门威仪司马秀建议，诏令天下各州在主要大道观设立石台，刊刻勒石此注，以使其"晓谕天下，传之久远"。注本曾在全国多地刻石留存，包括成都、阌乡、荆州、怀州、遂州、易州、邢州、苏州等处。后世主要流传版本有易州本和邢州本。至今在河南鹿邑太清宫、河北易县、邢台市、江苏镇江焦山、陕西周至县等地仍存有唐代留下的道德经碑幢，其中鹿邑太清宫的碑刻即"开元神武皇帝《道德经》注碑"。明人焦竑《老子翼》卷七记载："唐玄宗既注《老子》，始改定章句为《道德经》……刻石涡口老子庙中"。2024年有研究著作《唐玄宗御注〈道德经〉心解》出版。

The work is included in the Zheng Tong Dao Zang (正统道藏) canon under the Dong Shen Bu Yu Jue category (洞神部玉诀类), and appears at sutra number 680 in the Dao Zang Ti Yao index, located in volume 368 of the Hanfenlou edition, volume 20 of the Xinwenfeng edition, and volume 12 of the Sanjia edition. It is also included in volume 9 of the Zhonghua Daozang under the Four Supplementary Scriptures section.

The book begins with a self-authored preface (自序) in which Lu Xisheng critiques various earlier commentators on Laozi's teachings. He argues that Yang Zhu (杨朱) adhered to Laozi's substance but fell short by excessively valuing the body and despising material things; Zhuangzi (庄周) mastered Laozi's function but went too far by seeking to abandon sageliness and discard wisdom; Shen Buhai and Han Feizi (申韩) lost Laozi's reputation through harsh and punitive governance; and Wang Bi and He Yan (王何) lost Laozi's way by falling into empty nihilism and indolence. Lu considered Sima Qian (司马迁) to be the closest approximation of true Laozi philosophy among ancient writers.

Lu Xisheng further develops his core thesis by connecting Laozi with three sages: he claims Laozi shares the same origin (同原) as Fu Xi, who drew the Eight Trigrams, depicted all phenomena, explored the principles of life, and followed the harmony of virtue; that Laozi shares the overarching lineage (通其宗) with King Wen, who observed the I Ching's yin-yang movements, valued strength and change while emphasizing moderation; and that Laozi's views align in power/application (与其合其权) with Confucius, who emulated Yao and Shun, modeled the Zhou founders Wen and Wu, and guided the people through benevolence and righteousness. Lu concludes that Laozi "transformed and connected with, turned back and merged with" all three sages, making him "utterly divine" (至神). The entire work combines Confucian and Taoist thought to present a political philosophy, making it an important source for late Tang intellectual and ideological history.

<summary>
This is a ZhiHu (知乎) article titled "苏辙《老子解》全文" (The Complete Text of Su Zhe's Commentary on Laozi) published in the column "道德经解释" (Interpretation of the Dao De Jing) by author 大风 (Big Wind). The article presents the complete text of Su Zhe's (苏辙, a Song Dynasty scholar, 1039-1112) commentary/annotations on the Dao De Jing (Tao Te Ching) by Laozi. The article has received 37 approvals ("37 人赞同了该文章").

The article contains Su Zhe's line-by-line annotations of Laozi's classic text, organized by chapter. The content covers chapters 1 through 50 of the Dao De Jing, with each chapter presented with the original Laozi text followed by Su Zhe's commentary (注解). 

Key chapters and themes covered include:
- Chapter 1 (道可道章第一): On the ineffable nature of the Dao; only what cannot be spoken is constant/eternal; the distinction between the named and unnamed
- Chapter 2 (天下皆知章第二): Relativity of beauty and goodness, opposites arising mutually
- Chapter 3 (不尚贤章第三): On not valuing worthies, avoiding contention
- Chapters on water's virtue (上善若水), the usefulness of emptiness (三十辐共一毂/无之以为用), sensory overstimulation (五色章), fame and disgrace (宠辱章)
- Later chapters discuss governing philosophy, returning to simplicity (素朴), the concept of "无为" (wu wei/non-action), and the cultivation of inner nature

The text is divided into volumes ("道德真经注卷之一" and "道德真经注卷之二"), with editorial notes marked (#1, #2, #3) noting textual corrections based on the 宝颜本 (Baoyan edition). Each volume is attributed to "眉山苏辙注" (Commentary by Su Zhe of Meishan).

The commentary frequently references other classical texts including the I Ching (《易》), the Shurangama Sutra (《首楞严》), and Confucian teachings, showing a synthesis of Confucian, Daoist, and Buddhist thought characteristic of Su Zhe's scholarly approach.
</summary>

This webpage is from dokumen.pub and presents the full text (preface, table of contents, and opening chapters) of "蘇轍行蹤考" (A Study of Su Zhe's Travels and Whereabouts), Volume 1, by author Li Changsheng (李常生), published in 2020. **Prefaces and Context:**
- The author Li Changsheng spent nearly 12 years (from 2008) following Su Shi's footsteps and wrote "蘇軾行蹤考," published August 2019 in Taiwan.
- After completing the study of Su Shi, he continued with "蘇轍行蹤考," and intends to eventually write a combined biography ("蘇軾、蘇轍史傳").

**Key Biographical Facts about Su Zhe (蘇轍):**
- Su Zhe (字子由), younger brother of Su Shi, was born on the 22nd day of the 2nd month, 1039 (仁宗寶元二年) in Meishan, Sichuan. His wife was Lady Shi (史氏).

- From the "宋史·蘇轍傳": "轍與兄進退出處，無不相同，患難之中，友愛彌篤，無少怨尤，近古罕見" (In advancement and retreat, appointments and demotions, Zhe was always inseparable from his brother; in times of hardship their fraternal love grew deeper without any complaint—a rarity in modern times).
- Su Zhe died in 政和二年 (1112) at age 74, having retired to Yingchang (潁昌, modern Xuchang) where he farmed for 11 years after returning from exile. His brother Su Shi died at age 66 in Changzhou (常州) after returning from Hainan.
- Su Zhe's career peak was during the Yuanyou era (元祐, 1086-1093): in 1086 he became 右司諫; in 1092 he rose to 太中大夫、守門下侍郎 (Vice Chancellor), reaching the highest point of his power.
- His works include 《欒城集》 (over 2500 pieces), 《詩傳》,《春秋傳》,《古史》,《老子解》,《龍川別志》,《龍川略志》,《論語拾遺》 etc. He was posthumously given the posthumous name 文定 in 1176.

**Historical Context and Genealogy:**
- The Su family of Meishan traced their origins to Su Weidao (蘇味道), a Tang dynasty official from Luancheng (欒城), Hebei, who was demoted to Meizhou as governor during Wu Zetian's reign; one of his sons stayed in Meizhou.
- Su Zhe's grandfather Su Xu (蘇序) is when the family began to prosper; Su Xu's son Su Huan (蘇渙) was the first in the family lineage to hold government office.
- Su Xun (蘇洵), father of Su Shi and Su Zhe, began studying at age 27; he and his two sons are all among the "唐宋八大家" (Eight Great Prose Masters of Tang and Song).
- Su Zhe's mother Lady Cheng (程氏) personally taught the two brothers reading; she famously encouraged them to emulate the upright official Fan Pang (范滂).

**Book Structure:**
The book is organized chronologically into 17 chapters covering Su Zhe's life from his childhood in Meishan through his various official posts, exiles, and retirement. The exhaustive table of contents shows the chapters cover: Introduction, Meishan Su Zhe, First trip to the capital and return for mother's funeral, Second departure from Sichuan, Second period in the capital, Posting as official in Daming, Return for father's funeral, Return to the capital after mourning, Chenzhou instructor, Qizhou secretary, Yingtianfu judge, Exile to supervise salt/wine tax in Junzhou, Jixi county magistrate, Capital service and embassy to Liao, First exile to Ruzhou/Yuanzhou/Junzhou, Second exile to Leizhou/Xunzhou/Yuezhou, and Retirement in Yingchang, plus appendix.

**Research Methodology and Sources:**
- The author emphasizes the importance of on-site field investigation (實地考察) combined with historical documents, because previous scholars who wrote chronological biographies (年譜) of the Sus often made errors in travel direction, distance, timing, and geographic ordering since they never physically walked the routes.
- Key reference sources include: various chronological biographies (年譜) by Sun Ruting (宋·孫汝聽), He Lun (宋·何掄), Kong Fanli, Zeng Zaozhuang; geographic works like 《輿地紀勝》,《方輿勝覽》,《太平寰宇記》,《水經注》,《元和郡縣圖志》; historical works like 《宋史》,《續資治通鑒長編》,《東都事略》; and the standard editions 《蘇軾全集校注》 and 《欒城集》.

The chapter provides a detailed year-by-year account of Su Zhe's childhood:
- 1039: Born in Meishan (born at 亥時, 9-11pm, on the 22nd day of the 2nd month).
- 1040-1042: Western Xia attacks under Li Yuanhao; Su Shi began studying around age 7-8.
- 1043: Su Shi entered elementary school under Daoist teacher Zhang Yijian (張易簡) at Tianqing Temple (天慶觀), with classmate Chen Taichu.
- 1044: Su Zhe followed his brother to study at Tianqing Temple.

- 1050: Su Shi's sister Baniang (八娘) married her cousin Cheng Zhicai; she was mistreated and died at age 18 in 1052, causing a 42-year estrangement between the families.
- 1053: Teenage Su Zhe, who suffered from lung illness ("少年常病肺"), wrote "孟子解", "論語略解", and "春秋論", studying with his father and older brother as teachers.

- 1055: Su Zhe married Lady Shi (age 15); with father and brother, visited Chengdu's Dasheng Temple (大聖慈寺/中和勝相院), meeting monk Weijian (寶月大師).
- 1056: At age 18, Su Zhe, with father Su Xun and elder brother Su Shi, departed Chengdu via Ya州 (Ya'an) and Jiamen Pass (劍門關) on their first journey to the capital Bianjing (Kaifeng) to take the imperial examinations, passing through Fengxiang, Chang'an, and Mianchi.

The document also includes extensive geographic/historical information about locations relevant to Su Zhe's life, including Meishan, Chengdu, Luancheng, Yan Prefecture, Langzhou, Huai'an, and others.

--- SOURCE 3: 三苏父子在中国文化史上的地位 ---
URL: https://www.sinoss.net/c/2010-04-21/529286.shtml

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This article, published April 21, 2010 in Guangming Daily by scholar Zeng Zaozhuang (曾枣庄), examines the historical status and achievements of the Three Su (三苏) - father Su Xun (苏洵, 1009-1066) and his sons Su Shi (苏轼) and Su Zhe (苏辙) - in Chinese culture. The essay is organized around several themes:

**Contrasting careers:** Su Xun was a late bloomer who did not begin studying seriously until age 27, failed the imperial examinations twice, and only became famous near age 50. He held only low official posts (equivalent to a section-level cadre). In contrast, his sons achieved fame young - Su Shi at 22 and Su Zhe at 19 upon passing the jinshi examination. Su Shi governed eight prefectures and reached the rank of Minister of Rites (礼部尚书), while Su Zhe rose from county magistrate to Vice Chancellor (副相), outranking his brother. Su Zhe's political abilities flourished mainly during the Yuanyou era (元祐年间).

**Political roles before and after the Wang Anshi reforms:** Su Xun was primarily a political commentator (政论家) known as "talent of a king's advisor" (王佐才), while the sons were both commentators and active politicians. Su Xun emphasized administrative reform over legal reform, arguing "政之失，非法之罪" (political failures are not the fault of the law). The sons opposed Wang Anshi's New Policies; Su Zhe opposed them four months before Su Shi and left the capital two years earlier. Su Shi criticized Emperor Shenzong for being "too hasty in governance, too broad in listening, too sharp in advancing people" (求治太急，听言太广，进人太锐). During the Yuanyou era, Su Zhe submitted 74 memorials in ten months as Right Remonstrance Official, including eight calling for punishment of Han Zhen and three for executing Lü Huiqing.

**Literary achievements:** All three are among the "Eight Great Prose Masters of Tang and Song" (唐宋八大家). Su Xun's prose was praised by Ouyang Xiu as "辞辩闳伟" and by Zhu Xi as "雄浑". Su Shi was a pioneering figure across genres - known as Ou-Su with Ouyang Xiu in prose, Su-Huang with Huang Tingjian in poetry, and Su-Xin with Xin Qiji in ci poetry (founding the heroic school). Su Zhe's poetry was praised by Su Shi as superior to his own ("子由诗过吾远甚") and by Lu You as "温雅高妙，如佳人独立".

**Artistic accomplishments:** All three understood music (Su Xun owned a Lei qin), played chess modestly, excelled in calligraphy (Su Shi ranked first among the four great Song calligraphers), and appreciated painting. Su Shi established the "painting with a complete bamboo in one's chest" (胸有成竹) theory and founded the Huzhou school of literati painting.

**Historical scholarship:** Su Xun wrote the three-part Shilun (史论), praised as showing "true historical talent" and "the brush of Sima Qian". Su Zhe wrote the Gushi (古史) to correct errors in Sima Qian's Shiji, plus Longchuan Luezhi and Longchuan Biezhi documenting contemporary history, works that Zhu Xi frequently cited.

**Unorthodox thought:** Su Xun rejected the Confucian principle of righteousness over profit, arguing "利之所在，天下趋之" (where profit lies, the world rushes there). All three interpreted the Six Classics through human emotion (人情). Su Xun viewed the I Ching as a means of divine deception. The sons opposed Wang Anshi and Cheng Yi for being "inhumane" (不近人情). Su Zhe was particularly eclectic, integrating Confucianism, Buddhism and Daoism, and famously argued that "老聃、庄周之言不可以周、孔辩" (the words of Laozi and Zhuangzi cannot be debated using Zhou and Confucius) and that one must evaluate ideas without invoking Confucius or Laozi as authorities.

**Conclusion:** The author argues that while Su Shi is generally most celebrated, Su Xun deserves greater recognition for educating and cultivating his two famous sons, achieving greatness without any teacher through his own efforts - "上继韩、欧，下开长公兄弟" (succeeding Han Yu and Ouyang Xiu above, and opening the way for his son Su Shi below).
</summary>

Lin Xiyi was a Southern Song Neo-Confucian (理學家) from Fuqing, Fuzhou, and a fourth-generation disciple of the Aixuan School (艾軒學派). The Aixuan School, founded by Lin Guangchao (林光潮), differed from Cheng Yi's tradition by taking a more tolerant attitude toward Buddhism and Daoism, which is clearly reflected in Lin Xiyi's fusion of the Three Teachings (三教). The review organizes existing research into four main categories:

1. **Harmonizing the Laozi with Neo-Confucianism (理學)**: Early research began with the relationship between the Laozi and Confucianism. Huang Yun's 2016 master's thesis first formally addressed the Neo-Confucian relationship, arguing that Lin used Zhou Dunyi's "無極而太極" (Non-Ultimate and the Great Ultimate) to explain the Dao, then shifted to using the Neo-Confucian concept of "理" (principle). Zheng Tianxi's 2020 article deepened this from a yili (義理) perspective, focusing on "道器不離" (Dao and tools are inseparable), which effectively harmonized the two traditions.

2. **Mind-Study (心學) Tendency**: Lin Xiyi showed tendencies toward mind-study, emphasizing self-attainment (自得) and inner realization rather than book learning. Liu Sihe (2013) first noted this, arguing Lin was closer to Zhuangzi and Chan Buddhism than to either Zhu Xi or Lu Jiuyuan. Huang Yun further developed this, analyzing Lin's concept of "無容心" (non-attachment of mind), distinguishing two stages of mind, and linking it to Cheng Hao's views. The article notes there is as yet no dedicated study on Lin's relationship to mind-study, suggesting this as a fruitful research avenue for understanding the continuity of mind-study between Lu Jiuyuan and Wang Yangming.

3. **Using Buddhism to Interpret the Laozi (借佛解老)**: Liu Sihe (2013) argued Lin maintained his Neo-Confucian position, using Chan concepts only as tools (e.g., using "悟"/enlightenment merely as a means to grasp 天理), with Buddhism in a subordinate position. Huang Yun disagreed, arguing Lin engaged in an equal dialogue between Buddhism and Daoism, focusing on experiential understanding (體悟) rather than subordinating one to the other; this blurred distinctions between the two traditions. Zhang Miao (2019) held that Lin was rooted in Confucianism but acknowledged the inherent commonalities between Buddhism and Daoism and adopted multi-angled, flexible approaches to integrating them. Several scholars, including Huang Yun and Zheng Tianxi, noted Lin's misreadings of Buddhist concepts but did not determine whether these were intentional or unintentional distortions. Zheng Tianxi also analyzed Lin's views on the "無心" (no-mind) state of those who attain the Dao, influenced by both Mencius's "不動心" and Chan's "無念," and Lin's cultivation practices emphasizing self-realization and the idea that "道體在我" (the Dao substance is within oneself).

4. **Literary/Language Commentary (文章學點評)**: Wang Weiqian's 2012 article first discussed the characteristics of the commentary - Lin used simple, colloquial language (口義 style) with clear explanations, rhetorical devices like metaphor, strong overall coherence, and cross-referential interpretation of chapters. Huang Yun's thesis more deeply analyzed Lin's popularization of difficult language, clarification of metaphors, and pointing out both strengths and weaknesses (verbosity where explanation was unnecessary, and overextending metaphors - e.g., interpreting literally factual statements as figurative). Sun Mingjun's 2017 article analyzed this from a rhetorical perspective, identifying three literary features Lin highlighted: 借物明道 (using objects to illuminate the Dao through metaphor), exquisite conclusions (結語精妙, similar to "煞尾" in storytelling), and direct commentary on writing style. Zheng Tianxi argued Lin's sometimes forced "借喻" analysis aimed to counter Zhu Xi's negative evaluations of the Laozi.

The article concludes that existing research remains insufficiently deep across all four areas, and suggests future research directions: exploring alternative angles beyond harmonization for the Dao-Confucianism relationship, studying Lin's influence on mind-study's development, deeper investigation of Lin's complex relationship with the vast Buddhist tradition, and examining how Lin handled passages in the Laozi that are difficult to connect coherently.
</summary>

**Key interpretive framework of Lin Xiyi's commentary:**
- Laozi's work uses analogies (借物以明道) to illuminate the Dao; it should not be read literally
- The work emphasizes 虛 (emptiness), 無 (non-being), 弱 (weakness), and 卑 (humility)
- Lin Xiyi criticizes both Daoist followers who over-elevate the text and Confucians who dismiss it as heretical without serious study
- He praises 頴濱 (Su Che, Yingbin) for approaching correct interpretation but notes gaps
- He responds to critics: 朱熹 (Zhu Xi/晦翁) called Laozi "勞攘" (troublesome), and 西山 (Zhen Dexiu) claimed it contained schemes (陰謀)
- Key positive assessments cited: 伊川 (Cheng Yi) praised the 谷神 chapter as best; 朱文公 (Zhu Xi) said Emperor Wen of Han and 曹參 (Cao Can) only got Laozi's surface, while 王導 (Wang Dao) and 謝安 (Xie An) never even got the essence
- The commentary notes Laozi's most distinctive sayings: 無為而自化 (act through non-action and self-transform), 不爭而善勝 (win by not contending)
- Lin views Laozi's teaching as centered on "能實而虛，能有而無" (can be substantial yet empty, can have yet not have)

The article explores how Wu Cheng (吳澄), a renowned Neo-Confucian (理學) scholar of the Yuan Dynasty known as one of the "two great Confucian masters" of the era (paired with Xu Heng (許衡) as 南吳北許), used Neo-Confucian "mind-nature theory" (心性之學) to interpret the Daodejing in his work Annotation of Daode Zhenjing (《道德真經註》).

Key arguments and content:
1. **Context and significance**: During the Song-Yuan-Ming period, Neo-Confucians (理學家) increasingly used "reliance on Confucianism to interpret Laozi" (援儒解老) methods. Wu Cheng's work is identified by scholars like Liu Gu-sheng (劉固盛) as best exemplifying how Neo-Confucianism influenced Laozi studies (老學), and is one of only four Laozi commentaries included in the Siku Quanshu for the Song/Yuan/Ming period.

2. **The "Dao equals Li" (道理合一) interpretation**: Wu Cheng equated the Daoist "Dao" (道) with Neo-Confucian "Principle" (理/天理), infusing the Dao with Confucian moral attributes (仁義禮智 - benevolence, righteousness, propriety, wisdom). He used the "Li Yi Fen Shu" (理一分殊, one principle, many manifestations) concept to interpret the Dao-De relationship as "Dao producing myriad virtue" (道一分殊). He viewed "Dao" as metaphysical principle and "De" as its manifestation in all things.

3. **Mind-nature theory (心性論)**: Wu Cheng drew on Lu Xiangshan's (陸九淵) concept that "mind is principle" (心即是理), arguing that all principles of things are inherent in the mind (萬事萬物之理皆備於我). He emphasized "inner contemplation" (內觀) over external seeking, distinguishing "virtue-knowledge" (德性之知) from "hearing-seeing knowledge" (聞見之知). Wu Cheng's philosophy reconciles Zhu Xi and Lu Xiangshan, though leaning toward Lu's "revering virtue" (尊德性).

4. **"Removing external delusions, taking inner truth" (去外妄，取內真)**: Wu Cheng argued that external desires (五色, 五音, 五味, fame and profit) harm life and obscure the pure human nature. He advocated returning to the infant-like (嬰兒/赤子) state of simplicity and true purity (真樸), achieving unity with the Dao.

5. **Cultivation practices (工夫修養)**: Wu Cheng proposed principles for nurturing form, qi, and spirit (形、氣、神). For recluses (出世之人): preserving form, qi, and spirit (存形、存氣、存神); for those in the world (住世之人): nourishing them (養形、養氣、養神). Additional methods include: exhausting one's nature and reaching destiny (盡性達命), overcoming self and being brave in goodness (克己勇善), inner contemplation of the mind (內觀本心), seeing truth and guarding it firmly (見真守固), mind-environment dual forgetting (心境兩忘), using qi to ward off externals (以氣禦外), mind empty without things (心虛無物), and preserving stillness and returning to destiny (守靜復命).

This academic paper, written by 楊筑 and published in 《東亞漢學研究》2017 特別號, examines Wu Cheng's (吳澄, 1249-1333) interpretive approach in his commentary 《道德真經註》 on the Laozi, focusing on the concept of "moral/dao and de" (道德). Wu Cheng, a fourth-generation disciple of Zhu Xi who was also influenced by Lu Xiangshan (known for "和會朱陸" or reconciling Zhu and Lu), was a Yuan dynasty Neo-Confucian scholar who commented on the Laozi while at Qingdu Temple in 1307. His commentary is characterized by "以理釋《老》" (interpreting the Laozi through the concept of li/principle).

The paper's central arguments are threefold:
1. **The interpretive foundation**: Wu Cheng understood the Laozi's "道" (Dao) through the Neo-Confucian "縱貫縱講" (vertical/creative) interpretive framework rather than the "縱貫橫講" (horizontal/subjective) framework that Mou Zongsan later applied to Daoism. In Wu's commentary, Dao is not merely a state/boundary (境界形態) but possesses real creative ontological status, generating the universe ("無名者，道也，天地亦由此道而生"). Wu interprets the creation sequence as 道→一(沖虛一氣) →二(陰陽) →三, incorporating "德" (virtue/de) as the "一" into the cosmic generation scheme, thereby bridging the gap that Han dynasty 氣化宇宙論 (qi-based cosmology) had created between Dao and all things.

2. **A critical reassessment**: The paper challenges scholars like Huang Zhao and Liu Yijun who equate Wu's interpretation of the Dao with the Neo-Confucian "天理" (Heavenly Principle). The author argues against this for two reasons:
   - **First**, in Wu's commentary, 無為 (non-action) serves as the ultimate value, while 仁義 (benevolence and righteousness) remain secondary virtues. This places Wu's interpretation firmly within the Daoist system, differentiating it from Neo-Confucian thought where 仁義 constitutes the Heavenly Principle itself. Wu's commentary on chapters 16/18 emphasizes that filial piety and loyalty should be practiced naturally as "常分" (ordinary duty), not through external promotion.
   - **Second**, Wu's purpose in commenting on the Laozi was to distinguish (分判) rather than reconcile Confucianism and Daoism. In the 《吳文正集》, Wu explicitly criticizes the Laoist view of "自無而有" ("有生於無") as implying 理氣二分 (division of li and qi) and 理先氣後 (li prior to qi), which Wu rejects in favor of the Neo-Confucian position that 理氣 are inseparable and without priority. Wu regarded the Laozi's teaching as "異端似是之非" (heterodox doctrine resembling the truth).

**Conclusion**: While Wu's commentary does grant the Dao real creative ontological status similar to the Neo-Confucian 天理 (justifying the "以理釋《老》" characterization), the author argues that Wu maintained a clear distinction between the Daoist interpretation of 道/理 and the Neo-Confucian 理. Wu never equated the Dao of the Laozi with the 天理, as the ultimate values differ (無為 vs. 仁義) and their respective relationships with qi differ fundamentally (理氣二分 vs. 理氣不二). Thus, prior scholars' claims of full identity between Wu's Dao and the Neo-Confucian 理 constitute over-interpretation.
</summary>

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is an academic article by Chen Xia (陈霞), a researcher at the Institute of Philosophy, Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, originally published in "World Religious Studies" (《世界宗教研究》). The article analyzes the hermeneutic methods of the "Laozi Daodejing Heshang Gong Zhangju" (《老子道德经河上公章句》), the only complete surviving Han dynasty commentary on the Laozi.

The article identifies three main interpretive methods employed by the commentary:

1. **Chapter-section division and word exegesis (分章断句、歧解字词)**: The commentary uses the "zhangju" (chapter-sentence) format, strictly preserving the original text—which gives it important textual value. It transforms metaphors into concrete referents (e.g., interpreting "谷神不死" as nourishing the "five organs' spirits" rather than the abstract philosophical concept of emptiness) and converts abstract concepts into concrete ones (e.g., transforming "道" into "气," establishing a qi-based cosmological generation model with "一" as "太和之精气," "二" as yin-yang, and "三" as "和、清、浊三气").

《老子河上公章句》是西汉时期的道家学术著作，是现存最古的《道德经》注本。据皇甫谧《高士传》记载，河上丈人（又称河上公）隐居河边著老子章句。其人姓名为不详，在河滨结草为庐，因号"河上丈人"，研精黄老之学。相传汉文帝好读《老子》而有所不解，遣使询问，河上公言"道尊德贵，非可遥问"，汉文帝亲驾往问，河上公授以素书《老子道德经章句》二卷。葛洪《神仙传》亦载此事，称河上公踊身入空，文帝稽首谢罪，乃受素书道经章句。

**作者与时代**：关于其时代及作者众说纷纭，大致有秦汉、西汉两说。赞同秦汉说者认为其产生于《老子想尔注》之前。在汉代中后期道家思想的转型时期，流传下来最典型的注本为西汉末期严遵的《老子指归》和东汉中期托名河上公的《河上公章句》。《老子指归》的思想被扬雄、王弼、成玄英等人继承，孕育了魏晋玄学"贵无"、"自然为本"的本体论与重玄学萌芽；《河上公章句》虽为道家著作，但客观上为早期道教提供了理论基础。

**版本**：在唐玄宗御注《道德真经》出现前，河上公本、王弼本和《老子指归》流传最广。近人朱谦之认为王本属文人系统，为学者推崇；河上本近民间系统，文句简古。河上本又有北方传本与南方传本不同：北方本以敦煌发现的六朝唐写本（敦煌本）为代表，南方本以日本奈良圣语藏镰仓旧抄卷子残本及武内义雄所藏室町时代抄本为代表，北方本优于南方本。另有景龙碑本、广明本及日本天文钞本、泷川本等可互校，参校本包括《四部丛刊》影印宋建安虞氏刊本及敦煌S.477、S.3926号写本。此注将《老子》分为八十一章，每章题名，今传分章标目本即始于河上公。

**释义特点**：河上注本文字简明清晰，有浓厚养生思想，反映西汉崇尚黄老神仙的思潮。强调"宝精爱气"的养生地位，如"自爱其身，以宝精气"（七十二 章）、"治身者当爱精气而不放逸"（五十九章）、"深藏其气，固守其精，使无漏泄""深根固蒂者，乃长生久视之道"、"爱精重施，髓满骨强"（一章）等。以"去六情""损情去欲"为养生重要条件。河上注将治身与治国相结合，主张身国同一，如"治身者爱气则身全，治国者爱民则国安"（十章）、"治国当爱民财，不为奢泰，治身当爱精气，不放逸"（五十九章）。"清静无为、知足俭啬"是身国共同原则。注中多有神仙思想，反映西汉黄老思想特征。

**道义思想**：河上注认为"道"是混沌未分的元气，存在于天地之前，混沌而生成万物。宇宙化生论为：道生一，一生阴阳，阴阳生和清浊三气，分为天地人，三生万物。道散而为神明，流为日月，分为五行。并将道人格化，赋予意志力和思维能力。

**Overview:** The Xiang'er commentary is one of the earliest Taoist commentaries on the Dao De Jing. Its authorship and date are debated among scholars—theories attribute it to Eastern Han Celestial Masters founder Zhang Daoling (張道陵), his grandson Zhang Lu (張魯), or place it in the Six Dynasties or Northern/Southern Dynasties periods. The text deleted filler characters to make 5000 characters (called "五千文"), and its commentary often freely interpreted or even deliberately altered the original text, occasionally in ways that contradict the scriptures' meaning. During Zhang Lu's rule of Hanzhong, the work was used to educate followers and held high status; it was still revered in the Six Dynasties as a classic recited by Celestial Masters priests. **Content and Thought:**
- Featured a "神道設教" (teaching through spiritual authority) method, personifying "道" (the Way) into a willful deity speaking in first person ("吾")
- Emphasized following "道誡" (Way precepts, known as the "想爾戒" - Xiang'er precepts) to achieve longevity and blessings
- Promoted longevity practices combining 精 (essence), 氣 (vital energy), and 神 (spirit), rejecting fatalism in favor of achievable immortality through cultivation
- Believed in a celestial bureaucracy (天曹) governing lifespan adjustment and a terrestrial office (地官) governing the dead; virtuous practitioners could attain rebirth after "refining in 太陰" (Great Yin)
- Criticized other Taoist sects, Confucian classics, sacrificial rites, the "守一" (Guarding the One) meditation on inner deities, and sexual practices (房中术) such as "還精補腦" (returning essence to replenish the brain)

**Status and Versions:** Under Zhang Lu's rule it was treated as scripture; in the Northern/Southern Dynasties it was a foundational text for Celestial Masters priests, listed in the Daozang's 太玄 section, with status second only to the Heshang Gong commentary. Jao Tsung-i (饒宗頤) produced an annotated edition (《老子想爾注校證》), and Stephen R. Bokenkamp produced an English translation published by University of California Press in 1997. The text is considered important modern research material for early Taoist history.

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage is an academic article by 李芙馥 published on the website of the Institute of Philosophy at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (中国社会科学院哲学研究所), dated 2024-06-01, originally appearing in 《中州学刊》2024年第4期. The article examines how the Western Han dynasty philosopher 严遵 (Yan Zun) interpreted the Daodejing "以老释老" (using Laozi to explain Laozi) in his commentary 《老子指归》 (Laozhi Zhigui).

KEY ARGUMENTS AND STRUCTURE:
The article argues that 《老子指归》 uniquely offers holistic, passage-level interpretations rather than character-by-character annotations (unlike the commentaries of Heshanggong or Wang Bi). Its goal is to grasp the core meaning of the Dao De Jing and use it as a gateway for theoretical explanations of heaven-earth, yin-yang, husband-wife, father-son, ruler-minister, and myriad things. The article analyzes "以老释老" across three dimensions:

1. TEXTUAL LEVEL (文句与修辞): The Zhigui inherits the Laozi's vocabulary—both core concepts (道、德、无、无为、自然、常、虚、静、柔、弱) and low-frequency words (e.g., "市" and "长生久视" used repeatedly). It adopts and innovates Laozi's sentence patterns including "……，是谓……" (defining terms), "……若……" (reformulated as "……而若……" for balance), causal constructions like "……是以…………故……", and rhetorical questions ("夫何故","何以明之"). Both texts employ extensive parallelism and antithesis.

2. THINKING LEVEL (类比与对反): The Zhigui follows Laozi's analogical and oppositional modes of thinking. It reuses key metaphors from the Laozi—Water (水, symbolizing softness overcoming hardness), Infant (婴儿/赤子, representing guileless, non-striving states), Mother (母, as origin), and Bellows (橐龠, symbolizing empty yet inexhaustible). It also inherits the "反者道之动" (reversal is the movement of Dao) thinking, elaborating on how fortune/misfortune, gain/loss, advance/retreat mutually generate one another. Yan Zun analyzes how 祸福 are "同营异域" (same origin, different domains) and how only sages who abandon cleverness and follow 无为 can escape their vicissitudes.

3. MEANING LEVEL (核心概念与思想主旨): The Zhigui constructs a cosmological conceptual system of 道—德—神明—太和, derived from the Laozi's "道生一，一生二，二生三，三生万物" and "天下万物生于有，有生于无". The concepts of 自然 (naturalness) and 无为 (non-action) are treated as core themes: 自然 stands above 道 and 德 in the sequence 自然—道德—神明—（太）和, determining success/failure of heaven, earth, and human affairs, and serving as the sage's governing principle with "自然之验" (verification of naturalness). 无为 is extended from 道 to all levels (道德、神明、太和、万物), expanded from rulers to the common people, seen as the root of good governance (versus 有为 as the source of chaos), and systematically elaborated through 26 paired concepts—13 "生之徒" (虚、无、清、静、微、寡、柔、弱、卑、损、时、和、啬) versus 13 "死之徒" (实、有、浊、扰、显、众、刚、强、高、满、过、泰、费)—most of which trace to the Laozi text.

CONCLUSION: The Zhigui, despite its verbosity, demonstrates a clear "以老释老" tendency. Later scholars praised it—the 《三国志·魏书·方技传》 notes Yan Zun's works served as a standard for measuring philosophical acumen, and 晁说之 regarded the Zhigui as a source for Wang Bi's Laozi Commentary. Through this interpretive style, Yan Zun unified the Laozi text with resources from the Zhouyi and Zhuangzi, and connected heaven-earth, yin-yang, and social hierarchies, realizing "柄自然之归，以统万方之指" (holding to naturalness to unify all approaches).

**老子道德经开题序诀义疏**，唐初道教学者[成玄英](/wiki/%E6%88%90%E7%8E%84%E8%8B%B1 "成玄英")撰。《新唐书•艺文志》及《通志•艺文略》均著录此书七卷。《[正统道藏](/wiki/%E6%AD%A3%E7%B5%B1%E9%81%93%E8%97%8F "正统道藏")》未收。现有敦煌唐人残抄本三件（P2353、S5887、P2517）。此外《[道德真经注疏](/index.php?title=%E9%81%93%E5%BE%B7%E7%9C%9F%E7%B6%93%E6%B3%A8%E7%96%8F&action=edit&redlink=1 "道德真经注疏（页面不存在）")》、《[道德真经玄德纂疏](/index.php?title=%E9%81%93%E5%BE%B7%E7%9C%9F%E7%B6%93%E7%8E%84%E5%BE%B7%E7%BA%82%E7%96%8F&action=edit&redlink=1 "道德真经玄德纂疏（页面不存在）")》等书亦选录成玄英义疏。近人蒙文通根据敦煌本及《[正统道藏](/wiki/%E6%AD%A3%E7%B5%B1%E9%81%93%E8%97%8F "正统道藏")》诸书。撰成《[校理老子成玄英疏叙录](/index.php?title=%E6%A0%A1%E7%90%86%E8%80%81%E5%AD%90%E6%88%90%E7%8E%84%E8%8B%B1%E7%96%8F%E6%95%98%E9%8C%84&action=edit&redlink=1 "校理老子成玄英疏叙录（页面不存在）")》。此书以唐代道教重玄哲学思想疏解《[老子](/wiki/%E8%80%81%E5%AD%90 "老子")》旨义。以为大道非无非有，亦有亦无，有无不定，故言恍惚。注云：“夫道无所不在，所在皆无，荡然无际，有何封域也？”道能通生万物，而与物相通。“道不离物，物不离道。道外无物，物外无道。用即道物，体即物道。”“道物不一不异，而异而一。”又认为体道悟玄之士应有无双遣，不执空见。故曰：“为学之人执于有欲，为道之士又滞无为。虽复深浅不同，而二俱有患。今欲治此两执，故有再损之文。既而前损损有，后损损无，二偏双遣，以至于一中之无为。”又曰：“有滞之人唯滞于有，无滞之士又滞于无，故说一玄以遣双执。又恐学者滞于此玄，今说又玄，更怯后病。既而非但不滞，亦乃不滞于不滞，此则遣之又遣，故日玄之又玄。”是即全书所说“重玄”要旨，对唐代道教哲学思想发展影响甚大。

args.summary: This webpage from the Daoism Culture Center Database (道教文化中心資料庫) provides an entry on 《老子道德经开题序诀义疏》 (Laozi Daode Jing Kaiti Xujue Yishu), a work on the Daodejing (Laozi) written by Cheng Xuanying (成玄英), a Daoist scholar of the early Tang Dynasty. The work originally comprised seven volumes, as recorded in the New Book of Tang (《新唐书》) and Comprehensive Treatises on Literature (《通志》). The text was not included in the Zhengtong Daoist Canon (《正统道藏》). Existing copies include three Tang dynasty Dunhuang manuscript fragments (P2353, S5887, and P2517). Selections of Cheng Xuanying's commentary also appear in other works such as 《道德真经注疏》 and 《道德真经玄德纂疏》. The modern scholar Meng Wentong (蒙文通) compiled 《校理老子成玄英疏叙录》 based on the Dunhuang manuscripts and the Daoist Canon texts. The work interprets the Laozi through the "Chongxuan" (Twofold Mystery, 重玄) philosophy of Tang Dynasty Daoism, arguing that the Great Dao (道) is neither being nor non-being, and both being and non-being simultaneously—hence described as "huanghu" (vague/obscure). The text emphasizes that Dao is not separate from things ("道不离物" - Dao is not separate from things; "道外无物" - nothing exists outside Dao). It advocates for transcending both attachment to existence and attachment to non-existence ("有无双遣"), using the concept of "xuan" (玄, mystery) and "xuan zhi you xuan" (玄之又玄, mystery upon mystery) to progressively discard dualistic attachments. This "Chongxuan" doctrine had a significant influence on the development of Tang Dynasty Daoist philosophy. The page is categorized under Dunhuang documents and Tang Dynasty Daoist classics, and cites Hu Fuchen's 《中华道教大辞典》 (1995), p. 316, as a reference source.

args.summary:
This webpage provides information about the Daoist text 《道德真经注》(Annotation on the Classic of the Way and Virtue) by Li Rong (李荣), a Daoist priest of the Tang Dynasty during the reign of Emperor Gaozong (唐高宗). The work comprises four volumes and is included in the Orthodox Daoist Canon (《正统道藏》) in the Dongshendi Yujue category. 

Key facts about the text:
- Title: 道德真经注 (Li Rong's annotation)
- Author: Li Rong (李荣)
- Length: Four volumes (四卷)
- Location in Daoist Canon: 洞神部玉诀类, 絲字号
- Editions: Hanfenlou edition volume 430, Xinwenfeng edition volume 23, Sanjia edition volume 14
- Daozang catalogue number: 717
- Included in the Zhonghua Daozang, volume 9

The surviving edition only contains annotations for chapters 1-36 of the Daodejing. The missing portions can be supplemented using Dunhuang manuscripts and cross-checked against Qiang Siqi's 《道德真经玄德纂疏》to reconstruct the complete version of Li Rong's commentary. The annotation is significant for its emphasis on the "Chongxuan" (Double Mystery/Twofold Profundity) doctrine, making it an important source for studying Tang Dynasty Daoist thought.

The reference source is: Hu Fuchen's 《中华道教大辞典》(Chinese Encyclopedia of Daoism, Beijing: China Social Sciences Press, 1995), page 316. The webpage is categorized under both "洞神部玉诀类" (Dongshen Section Jade Instructions category) and "唐代道教经典" (Tang Dynasty Daoist classics).

–97– 中國學術年刊 第三十七期（春季號） 2015 年3 月 頁97～116 臺北：國立臺灣師範大學國文學系 ISSN：1021-7851 DOI：10.6238/SIS.201503.04 李榮《道德經注》心性思想研究 謝婉馨* （收稿日期：103 年9 月30 日；接受刊登日期：104 年1 月22 日） 提要 李榮，號任真子，為唐初著名的重玄宗道士，與成玄英齊名，被視作唐代「重玄學」 的代表人物。一般認為「談心論性」為初唐重玄學鮮明的學術特色之一，本文以李榮《道 德經注》為研究對象，從「心性論」的角度切入，探討李榮的心論、性論以及修養工夫。 李氏將「性」分作本性與情性，又剖析心有活動、執取、認知之義，能玄鑑萬物，吾人心 念一動使得本性被覆，方於經驗世界中做出一些負面舉措，最後李氏提出持心守心、灰心 混心等修養方法，行雙遣工夫，遣之又遣，使本性復歸澄明，重返空靈寂靜的原初自然狀 態，便能逍遙無礙。 關鍵詞：李榮、道德經注、心性、重玄學、唐代老子學、道教 ＊ 私立德霖技術學院通識中心講師。 中國學術年刊第三十七期（春季號） –98– 一、前言 李榮，號任真子，為唐初著名的道士，關於他的生卒年與事蹟，正史上並無明確記載， 僅《舊唐書》一語帶過： 「 （羅）道琮尋以明經登第，高宗末，官至太學博士。每與太學助 教康國安、道士李榮等講論，為時所稱，尋卒。」1由是可知李榮曾活動於高宗末年，與 時人論道，其餘資料皆湮沒無考。近代學者蒙文通、黃海德曾考察李榮的生平事蹟，2認 為他是綿州巴西人（今四川綿陽） ，著有《道德經注》 、 《莊子注》 、 《西昇經注》 ，以及無可 察證是否託名偽作的《洗浴經》 。以上四部著作，在時代的洪流中或佚或缺，如今《莊子 注》已不復見，3《西昇經注》則斷簡殘篇，僅少部分被後人抄錄保留，4至於《洗浴經》 更可疑，是否為李榮親筆著作仍闕疑待考，5因此李榮的著作今惟《道德經注》傳世。是 峯 書於四○年代由蒙文通、嚴靈 各自從敦煌殘卷中輯出，是今日研究李榮思想的重要文 獻，平心而論，蒙氏、嚴氏所輯之本各有所長，可並為善本，筆者擬取蒙本研究對象，並 以嚴本為輔，期能呈現最真實的學術面貌。6 李榮為初唐著名的重玄大師，與成玄英齊名， 「重玄學」上承魏晉玄學，下啟宋明理 學，在我國學術發展史上具有重要地位，從目前已有的研究成果得知，重玄學濫觴於「玄 學」 ，並受佛教「中觀學」影響，形成一股玄之又玄、遣之又遣、不滯兩邊的哲學思維， 它不僅對魏晉玄學的深化有所推動，對宋明理學本體論、心性論的建立，也起了一定的作 1 後晉‧劉昫等撰： 《舊唐書‧列傳》 （北京：中華書局，1995 年） ，卷189 上，頁4956。 2 關於李榮的生平，可參考黃海德： 〈李榮及其《老子注》考辨〉 ， 《世界宗教研究》第4 期（1987 年 12 月） ，頁50。亦可參考強昱： 〈成玄英李榮著述年行考〉 ，收錄於《道家文化研究》 （北京：三聯書 店，2002 年）第19 輯（玄學與重玄學專號） ，頁325-329。 3 李榮《莊子注》今已亡佚，此說參見蒙文通〈輯校《李榮道德經注》敘錄〉 ： 「至榮所著書別有《莊 子注》 ，其佚文已不可考。」收錄於《道書輯校十種》 ，頁559。 4 李榮《西昇經注》全本今已不存，僅少部分殘文保留於北宋陳景元《西昇經集注》 。今見宋‧碧虛子 陳景元纂集： 《西昇經集注》六卷，收錄於《正統道藏》 （臺北：新文豐，1985 年） ，冊24，維字號， 頁529-586。 5 唐‧玄嶷 《甄正論》 ： 「道士李榮又造 《洗浴經》 以對溫室。」 收錄於 ，20易受現象界 干擾，好在它僅是人在經驗世界裡的一種行為表現，並非人之本質，故吾人應本著「人性 自然已足」的最高價值，行無為雙遣工夫，跳脫情欲牽制，使其歸返於自然。 三、心論 （一）心有三義：活動義、認知義、執取義 李榮以自然之性為吾人內在修養的根據，視情性為經驗世界中受情欲所牽的表現，並 非原初之性，因此吾人須「復性」 ，恢復情性裡種種不自然的狀態，與復性說相呼應的， 是李榮的心論，他說道： args.summary:
This academic article, "Study of mind thinking from Li Rong's (李榮) note for TaoDeJing (道德經注)" (published in Studies in Sinology, Vol. 37, Spring 2015, pp. 97-116, by Hsieh, Wan-hsin), examines the mind-nature theory (心性論) in Li Rong's commentary on the Tao Te Ching. Li Rong (號任真子) was a prominent early Tang dynasty Taoist of the Chongxuan (重玄, "Double Mystery") school, equally famous as Cheng Xuanying, and considered a representative figure of Chongxuan learning. The article argues that while Li Rong's academic importance parallels Cheng Xuanying's, he has not received commensurate scholarly attention.

The paper is organized into four main sections. First, on theory of nature (性論), Li Rong distinguishes two levels of nature: the "natural nature" (自然之性), which is innate, pure, self-sufficient, and perfectly complete (本乎自然, 樸，本也), and the "emotional nature" (情性), which derives from yin-yang qi and is subject to desires, deceptions, and sensory attractions. Li Rong advocates "以性制情" (controlling emotions with nature) and returning to one's original nature. His view of nature as the highest moral value aligns with the Cheng-Zhu school's "性即理" (nature is principle) approach.

Second, on theory of mind (心論), Li Rong attributes three functions to the mind: activity (活動義), cognition (認知義), and grasping/clinging (執取義). He calls the mind a "靈臺" (spirit tower) and "玄鏡" (mysterious mirror), which can illuminate and perceive the world, but once the mind stirs and clings to external phenomena, it covers the original nature. The mind can move toward either Dao-action (undirected) or non-Dao-action; cultivation work must therefore begin from the mind itself.

Third, on cultivation practices (心性修養工夫), Li Rong proposes three methods: (1) "制之未動，持心守心" (controlling before movement begins, guarding and keeping the mind), using the analogy of upper, middle, and lower scholars to describe levels of prevention; (2) "虛心復性" (emptying the mind and restoring nature), including "灰心" (ash-heart, extinguishing desires) and "混心" (mixing the mind, eliminating discriminations); and (3) "不滯兩邊，遣之又遣" (not adhering to either extreme, dispelling again and again), a double-dispelling Chongxuan method that transcends all dualities and even forgets the dispelling itself.

The conclusion highlights that Li Rong inherited and developed Cheng Xuanying's ideas—Cheng emphasized "復性" (restoring nature) while Li emphasized "修心" (cultivating the mind)—both predating Li Ao's famous "復性說" in the mid-Tang. Li Rong's philosophy notably shifted away from traditional Daoist immortality-seeking toward spiritual cultivation, even asserting that "心為死地" (the mind is the place of death), meaning that once the mind dies, even a living physical body is as good as a walking corpse. The article includes an abstract in English and extensive bibliographic references in Chinese and English on Chongxuan studies.
