| 14 | 絕學無憂章第罕 |
| 15 | 學擊愛 |
| 16 | 高學日益篇遭曰損不知性命之正而以學求益增其所禾聞積之不己而無以一之則以圓害方以直害曲其中紛然不勝其憂矣惠夫學者之至此也故曰絕學無憂若夫聖人禾嘗不學而以遣篇主不學而不紗笏學而不亂廓孤亂憂而安酉絕學耶 |
| 17 | 之與阿相去幾何善之與惡相去何若學者溺於所聞而無以臥之則唯之篇恭阿之篇慢不可同日言炙而沉夫善惡之相反手夫唯聖人知萬物同出於性而皆成於妄如畫馬牛如刻虎藏皆非其寶落焉無是非同具之辨孰知其相去絡蔚哉苟知此矣則萬物並育而不相害道並行而不相悖缸足怪矣 |
| 18 | 之所畏不可不畏 |
| 19 | 聖人均彼我一同異其心仙所復留然由以是忽遺世法祀分亂理而不顧哉人之所長吾亦畏之人之所為吾亦焉之雖列於君臣父子之間行於禮樂刑政之域而天下不知其異也其所以不晏於物二旨心而己 |
| 20 | 荒夸其禾果戎 |
| 21 | 人皆徇其所知故介然不出畦畛聖人兼涉有無無入而不可則荒夸其禾可夾也眾人熙熙如享太牢如春登夢義獨怕今其禾兆若嬰兒之禾核 |
| 22 | 人各溺於所好其美如享太牢其樂如春登臺賣然從之而不知其非唯聖人深究其妄遇之泊狀不動如嬰兒之禾能核也兼兼兮若無所歸 |
| 23 | 口石乘萬物之理而不自私故若無所歸眾人皆有餘面我獨若遺 |
| 24 | 眾人守其所知各自以為有餘聖含舉萬物而不主於內超然其若遺也我愚人之心也哉純純兮 |
| 25 | 純純若愚而非愚也 |
| 26 | 俗人昭昭我獨若昏俗人察察我獨悶悶世俗以分別為智聖人知群妄之不足韓也故其殊若昏莫申若悶 |
| 27 | 心若晦寂若無所止 |
| 28 | 忽焉若晦不見其津涯過寂騰無朕不見其所止宿也 |
| 29 | 眾人皆有以我獨頑似鄙 |
| 30 | 人各有能故世皆得而用之聖人才全德備若無所施故疑於頑鄙 |
| 31 | 我獨異於人兒青登毋 |
| 32 | 遺者萬物之毋眾人徇物忘道而聖人脫遺萬物以遁君崇塵茹嬰兒訛祈雜食食於母而己 |
| 《孔德之容章第幸角》 |
| 1 | 孔德之容惟道是從 |
| 2 | 遭無形也及其運面柄德則有容矣故德者運之見也自是推之則眾有之容皆道之見於物者也 |
| 3 | 道之篇物唯悅唯惚惚兮悅某中有象愧兮惚某甲有物 |
| 4 | 道非有無故以恍惚呂之然及其運而成象署而成物禾有不出於懈恍者也窈兮雲奪某甲有精 |
| 5 | 方有無之末定惚恍而不可見及夫有無之交則見共窈冥深眇雖未成形而精存手其中矣 |
| 6 | 曳精甚真其中有信 |
| 7 | 物至於咸形則真偶雜果方其有精不容偽也真偽既雜目一而為二自二而為二紛然錯出不可復信寒方其有精不吾欺黃 |
| 8 | 也 |
| 9 | 曰古厥今其二不去以閎眾甫古今雖異而道則不去故以不去名之淮未當晏枚能以閱眾有之戀苞甫秉也雖萬鍾亶余免於變也 |
| 10 | 五荷以知眾甫之騎載以此 |
| 11 | 聖人之所狀知萬鐘蕭以然者以能體道而不去故也 |
| 《曲則全章第幸一》 |
| 1 | 田則全 |
| 2 | 聖人動必循理理之所枉哉證具熙曲嬰於通而己通故與物不迎不迂故全也枉則直 |
| 3 | 直而非理則非直也循理雖枉而矢下之至直也 |
| 4 | 霍則盈 |
| 5 | 眾之所歸考口也雖欲不盈不鴈刊弊則新 |
| 6 | 昭昭察察非遭也悶悶芳將懸謚之所自出也 |
| 7 | 少則得 |
| 8 | 道一而己待朗無不得矣拭 |
| 9 | 多則惑笑 |
| 10 | 二學而無以芝剋藝久 |
| 11 | 包甸岳浹聖人抱睹兩天下式 |
| 12 | 抱署復性者也蓋曲則全杜則直霆則盈弊則新少則待皆抱一之餘也故以抱一終之 |
| 13 | 不三見故明 |
| 14 | 目不自見故能見物鏡不自照改能照物如使自見自肌則目篇之不暇而何暇及物哉 |
| 15 | 不自是故彰不自伐故功不目矜改長天惟不爭故天下稟能與奚予 |
| 16 | 不自見不自是不目伐不自矜皆不爭之餘也故以不華終之 |
| 17 | 芝所謂曲則全者豈臺義誠全而歸之世以直篇是蠶篇非將循理而行於世則有不免於曲者矣故給篇復呂之曰此逞臺盍蠹全而歸之天所謂全者非獨全身也內以全身外以全物物裁兼全而歸復於性則其篇直也大矣 |
| 《希言目然章第二士二》 |
| 1 | 莒自然 |
| 2 | 變口言出於自然則簡而中非其百然而強呂之則煩而難信矣改曰道之出口淡乎其無味視之不足見聽之不足聞用之不可既此所謂希言矣 |
| 3 | 飄風不終朝暴雨不總曰軸蠶狗此者天池天地尚不能久而況於人乎 |
| 4 | 陰湯不爭風雨時至不疾不徐盡其勢之所至而放止若失湯亢於上陰伏於下否而不待洩於是簾飄風暴雨若將不勝然其藝朱能以終曰古之聖人呂出於希行出於夷皆因其自瓜故久而不窮世惑厭之以為不若詭辯之悅耳怪行之驚世不知其不能久也 |
| 5 | 故從事於道者道者同於道德者同於德失者同於失同於道者道亦得之同於德者德亦得之同於失者失亦得之 |
| 6 | 孔子曰苟志於仁矣無惡也故曰仁者之過易辭怠於仁猶若此而況志於遺者乎夫茍從事於道矣則其所鳥合於道者得道合於德者得德不辜而失雖失於祈扁亡定然必有得於道德矣 |
| 7 | 信不足有不信 |
| 8 | 不知道者信道不罵因其失而疑之於是益以不信天惟覆遭然後不以得器疑道也 |
| 《跂二不立章茅戶高》 |
| 1 | 舅畫跨者不行自見者不朋目是者不影自伐者無功目矜者不長 |
| 2 | 人禾有不能立且行看也苟以立焉禾足而加之以跂以行為奉足而加之以跨未有不喪失其行立者彼某目見自是自伐自矜者亦二是矣 |
| 3 | 其於道也曰餘食贅打 |
| 4 | 譬叢童麓顧暑餘墨彊宴蠱 |
| 5 | 適完則已有瞽鑒系 |
| 6 | 物或惡之故有道者爪處 |
| 《有物混咸寶弟季五》 |
| 1 | 有物混成先天地生 |
| 2 | 夫遣非清非濁非高非下非去非來非善非惡混然而成體甚於令為住故曰有物混成此未有知其生者蓋湛然常存而天地生於其中耳 |
| 3 | 寂兮家含獨立而不恢周行而不殆可以為天下母 |
| 4 | 寂兮無聲寥夸蕪形獨立無輯而未當變行於群有而末嘗殆俯以化育萬物則皆其母矣 |
| 5 | 吾不知其名字之曰道強羈之名曰大道本無名聖人見萬物之無不由也故字之曰遺見萬物之莫能加也故強為之名曰大然其寶鑒搏而稱之也 |
| 6 | 大曰逝逝曰逮達曰反 |
| 7 | 自火而求之則慚蔬往矣目往而求之則逮不及矣雖逝雖速胎反而求之一心足矣 |
| 8 | 故遺大天大地大王亦大減中有四大而王后冠馬人法地地法天天法道道法自然由道呂之則雖天池與王皆不足大也恥世之人習知三若乏大而不信道之大也故以霍善之人不若地地不若天天不若更仁遣道不若自孤狀崔人一日復性則此三者人皆足以盡之矣 |
| 《重為輕根贊第韋八》 |
| 1 | 重羈輕根靜為躁君 |
| 2 | 凡物輕不能戴重小不能鏤大不行者使行不動者制動該輕以重為根躁以靜慕君 |
| 3 | 筵以君子終日行不離輔重雖有榮觀盛處超然 |
| 4 | 行欲輕而不離輕重榮觀雖樂而必有燕處董靜之不可失如此 |
| 5 | 奈何萬棄之主而以身輕天下人主以身任天下而輕其身則霆以隼天下矣 |
| 6 | 輕則朱臣躁則失君 |
| 7 | 輕英躁無施而豆輦鍾則臣舜基簟穎臣躁則君知其隊於利故曰輕翹玳臣躁則失君 |
| 《善行無轍藝第韋七》 |
| 1 | 善行無轍逝良蠡登理而行故無迎 |
| 2 | 善言無瑕謫 |
| 3 | 時然後言故言滿天下無口過善計不用壽笄 |
| 4 | 萬物之數畢陳於前不計而知安用籌簟善開無關桂而不可開喜結無繩約而不可卒 |
| 5 | 賁 |
| 6 | 全德之人其於萬物如母之於子雖縱之而不去故無關而能閒亂繩而能約是以聖人常善救人故無棄人常二救物葭無棄物 |
| 7 | 彼方執笄以計設關以閉持繩以結其力之所及者少矣聖人之於人非特蓉之又善救之我不棄人而人安待不歸我手是謂襲明 |
| 8 | 赦人於危難之中非救之大者也方其流轉生死為物所蔽而雅吾至明以輿之使暗者皆明如燈相傳相襲而不絕則可謂善救人矣 |
| 9 | 轂善人不善人之師不善全二人之資不責亡迂其師不愛其賢 |
| 10 | 聖人無心於教故不已奪雲蠢余無心於學故不貴其師聖人非獨吾忘天下亦籬使天下忘我故也 |
| 11 | 雖智天迷是謂要妙 |
| 12 | 聖人之妙雖智者有所不諭也 |
| 《知其雄章第幸八》 |
| 1 | 知其椎守其雌為天下谿為天下谿常德不離復歸於嬰兒知其白守其黑為天下式焉天下式常德不忒復歸於無極知其榮守其慕天下谷為天下谷常德乃足復歸於樸雄雌先稷之及我者也白黑明閭之及我者也榮辱竟觸之及我若也夫欲先而惡後欲明而惡閒欲貴而惡賤物之情也然而先役之及我不若明閻之功明闇之及我不若音賤之源古之聖人去妄以求復性其性愈明則其守愈下其守愈下則其德愈厚其德愈厚則其歸愈太蓋不知而不為不若知而不為之至也知其雄守其雌知性若也知性而爭心止則天下之等已 |
| 2 | 先者皆將歸之如水之赴谿草宥去者雖鮮嬖茹要兒能受而未能用也故曰復歸於嬰兒知其白守其黑見性者也居閣而視明天下之明若皆不能以形逃也故眾明則之以焉法雖應萬物而法束嘗霆用未嘗窮也故曰復歸於無極知其縈守其辱復性若也諸妄己盡處辱而無憾曠兮如谷之虛物來而應之德足於此純性而無雜矣故曰復歸於樸 |
| 3 | 散斟為器聖人用之則為官長故大制不霸 |
| 4 | 聖人既歸於樸復散樸為體琢應萬楊譬如人君分政以立官長亦因其勢膏然雖制而非有所割裂也 |
| 《將欲敢天下章第章九》 |
| 1 | 得八牙一肝欲取天下而焉之吾見其不得己聖人之有天下非取之也萬物歸之不得已而受之其治天下非為之也因萬楊之自然而除某害旨若欲取而焉之則不可得笑 |
| 2 | 定 |
| 3 | 天下神器不可為也為若敗之執者失之凡物皆不可為也雖有百人之聚不楯其自然而妄為之空肩湖語不服者而況天下卑雖然小物震丁蓋有可以力取面智奢暑至於天下之大有神主之不待其自歸則叛不聽其自治則亂矣 |
| 4 | 凡物或行或隨或呵或吹惑強盛羸惑誣跳器是以聖人云甚去奢蓄察 |
| 5 | 陰陽相盪高下相傾天小相使或行於前或隨於後惑呵而煖之或吹而寒宴碧正而強之部璜西羸妻墨軌而成之鐵重而毀之皆物之自恕而勢之不魚箸也然世之愚人私已而務得乃欲拒前違之其禍不覆則折淮聖人知其不可遂則順以符之去其甚去其奢去其泰使不至於過而傷物而天下無患矣此不焉之至也堯湯之於水旱雖不能免而終不至於敗由此故也易髦泰曰后以財成天地之道輔相天池之宜以左右民三陽在內三陰在外物之泰桂矣聖人懼其過而害生故財城百 |
| 6 | 而輔相之使不至於過此所謂去甚去奢去秦也 |
| 《以道佐人主章第江》 |
| 1 | 遷佐人主者不以兵強天下其事好還聖人用兵皆出不得已非不得己而欲以行八中四強勝天下雖或灶勝其禍必還報之楚靈齊潛秦始辜讓梁武或以殺其身或以禍其子孫人之所毒鬼之所疾末有得免君以 |
| 2 | 也 |
| 3 | 師之所處荊棘生焉犬軍之後必有凶年兵之所在民臺廢故田不修用兵之後殺氣勝故年縠傷兄兵皆然而況以兵強天下者耶 |
| 4 | 故善者果而巳不敢以取強 |
| 5 | 果淚也德所不能綏政所不能服不得己而後以兵快之耳 |
| 6 | 果而勿矜果而勿伐果而勿驕果而不得己是果而勿強 |
| 7 | 勿矜勿伐勿驕不得己四者所以鴻勿強也 |
| 8 | 物壯則老是謂不道不道旱巳壯之必老物無不然者唯有道者成而蘆鈇盈而芳沖末嘗蓋禾嘗老禾嘗死逃兵強天下壯亦甚矣而能無二乎 |
| 《夫佳兵童第三十內》 |
| 1 | 得八中蠹天佳兵者不祥之器物或惡之故有道者不三口 |
| 2 | 廣 |
| 3 | 以之濟難而不以篇常是謂不處君子居則貢左用兵則貢右兵者不祥之器非君子之器不得己而用物恬淡高上勝而不美而美之者是樂殺人夫樂殺人者不可待志於天下吉事尚左凶事尚右偏將軍處左上將室處右呂以喪禮處之殺人眾多以悲哀泣之戰勝則以喪禮處之 |
| 《道常無名量第三十判》 |
| 1 | 道常無名樸雖小天下不敢臣侯王若能守禹物將自賓 |
| 2 | 樸性也道常無名則性亦不可名矣故其為物舒之無所不在而斂之不盈毫末此所以雖小而不可臣也故匹夫之賤守之片巳則塵垢杜糠足以陶鑄堯舜而侯王之尊不能守則萬物不君夏 |
| 3 | 天地相合以降甘露人莫琴而自均沖氣升降相合為禹韓露昭然糞萬物無不均遍聖人體至道以應諸有亦露之無不及者此所以能賓萬物也始制有名名亦既有夫亦將知止知止所以霍 |
| 4 | 矛舜 |
| 5 | 聖人散樸焉器因器制名事其徇名而忘樸逐末而喪木哉蓋亦知復於性是以乘萬變而不殆也 |
| 6 | 單遺之在天下猶川谷之輿江海江海水之鍾也川谷水之分也這冀物之宗也萬物道之末也皆爪也故川谷歸其所鐘皆道也故萬物賓其所宗 |
| 《知人老智童第三十三》 |
| 1 | 恥人者智自知者明 |
| 2 | 分別為知蔽盡為明分別之心未除故止於知人而不能自知蔽盡則無複分別改能自知而又可以及人也 |
| 3 | 定 |
| 4 | 勝人者有力自勝者強 |
| 5 | 力能及人而不能及我能克己復性則非力之所及故可謂強矣 |
| 6 | 知足者富 |
| 7 | 知更者所遇而足則末二禾富矣雖有天下而常挾不足之心以處之則是終身不能富也 |
| 8 | 強行者有志 |
| 9 | 不異物爭而自強不息物苴寵奪某忌也不失其所者久 |
| 10 | 物變無窮而心束嘗失則久矣死而不亡者壽 |
| 11 | 死王之變孟大矣而其住湛然不亡此口之至人能不生不死者也 |
| 《大遺汎兮童第洞十四》 |
| 1 | 任父十乏大道汎今其可左右 |
| 2 | 汎兮無可無不可故左右上下周術無禾至遭 |
| 3 | 翼物恃之以生而不辭功咸不名有世有生物而不辭者必將名之壑翩己孝乙已世有避物而不有者必將辭物而不生生而不辭成而不有二唯道而己愛養萬物而不為主常無欲可名於小苗聘歸之不篇主可名於大是以聖人終不為大故能成其大 |
| 4 | 大而有為大之心則小矣 |
| 《隸太象章第四十玉》 |
| 1 | 執太象天下往 |
| 2 | 遭非有無故謂之大囊葛其照然涓形則有同有異同者好之異者惡之好之則來惡之則去不足以使天下皆牲矣往而不害安辛泰 |
| 3 | 有好有惡則有所利有所害好惡既盡則其於萬物皆無害慕收至者無不安無不平無不奉 |
| 4 | 樂輿餌遇容止道之出口淡平其無味視之不足見聽之不足閒閣之不可既作樂設餌以壽藜若豈不足以止過客我然而樂閔餌盡彼將捨之丙去二夫執大象以待丞卜天下不知好之又況得而惡二舊之手雖無臭味形色聲音以悅人而其用不可盡矣 |
| 《將欲獻之章弟三十六》 |
| 1 | 將欲默之必固張之將欲弱之必固強之將欲廣之必固輿之將欲奪之必固輿之是謂棗曼省入十八繞陟 |
| 2 | 未當奠漱而遽輦則勢有所不極理有所不足勢不極則取之難理不足則物不服啟此幾於用智也與管仲孫武何異聖人之典世俗其遊固有相似者也聖人秉理而世俗周智乘理妒醫藥鑿應憑用智如商賈巧於射利 |
| 3 | 事勝剛弱勝強 |
| 4 | 聖人知剛強之不足恃故以柔弱目處夭下之剛強方櫓傾梢乳而吾獨柔弱以待之及其大者傷小者死而吾以不校坐待其斃此所謂勝也雖然聖念它用貴寫此以勝物哉類勢之自然而居其自然耳夏不可以脫於淵國之利器不可以示人且含芝為物非有爪矛之刊足以勝物也謀建 |
| 5 | 方其託於深淵雖強有力者莫能執之及其脫澗而陸則蠢然易耳何能焉載聖人居於柔弱而剛強者莫能傷非徒莫能傷也又將以全制其後此不亦天下之利器也哉願惟脫於淵然後人得制之聖人二八十九惟處於柔弱而不厭故終能服天下此豈輿眾人共之者哉 |
| 6 | 道常無耦責第三宅 |
| 7 | 常簪需無不為 |
| 8 | 私所不為而無焉之之意耳 |
| 9 | 侯王若能守萬物將自化化而欲作吾將鎮之以無名之樸 |
| 10 | 聖人以無焉化物萬物化之始於無為而漸至於作譬如嬰兒之長人偽日起故三代之衰人情之變日以益甚方其欲作而工之人興夫下皆靡故其變王一有不可勝言者苟其方作而不為之動終以氣名之樸鎮之庶幾可得而工也 |
| 11 | 無名之樸亦將不欲不欲以竇天下將自正聖人甲無抱樸之念外無抱撲之近故模全曲用剛 |
| 12 | 之迷矣 |
| 13 | 憶直經口陟 |
| 14 | 陌德真經註卷之刑覺眉山蘇轍註 |
| 《上德不德囂聖事八》 |
| 1 | 丘德不德是率涓德丁德不失德是以無德聖人縱心所欲不鷺矩非有意於德而德自足其下卻德之得翹強以宋不失盍僅目完耳而何德之百 |
| 2 | 山德亂為而無以篇下德扁之而有以為無為而有以篇之則猶有厲適唯無為而無以馬之者可謂無為矣其下非憤不成忒猶有以為之非徒作而無術者也仁烏之而無以馬一義篇之而有以為仁擊領皆不免於篇之矣其所以異者仁以無以為為勝義署駑篇功耳德有上下而仁義有上無下何也下德在仁義之間而仁蓄臺下若不足復言故迄禮焉之而莫之應則攘庸而仍之自德以降而至於禮聖人之所以濟昏君極矣故為之而不應則至於攘臂而強之強之而又不應於是刑罰興而申兵起則徒作而無術矣 |
| 3 | 畋失道而稷德後德而後仁夫仁而役雲奕義而後禮乂豐一桑著忠信之薄面亂之首忠信而無禮則忠信不見禮立而忠信之美發越於外君臣父子之閭矢婦門友之際其外粲然而其中無餘矣故順之則治違之則亂治亂之相去其間不能以臺故曰亂之首也 |
| 4 | 前識者道之華而愚之始 |
| 5 | 聖人玄覽萬物是非得容卑陳於前蘆之照形無所不見而孰篇前役世人視止於目聽止於邑思止於心冥行於萬物之間役智以求識而偶有見焉雖自以為明而不知至愚之目是始也 |
| 6 | 足以天丈夫處其厚不處甚轉居某實不居昨辜故去彼取此 |
| 7 | 世之鄙矢樂某有得於下而忘其一鑿吾薄而遺厚采華面棄宮罪大丈夫孰能去彼取此 |
| 《昔之得辜曩密幸九》 |
| 1 | 昔之得署天得尸以清地得裏寧轉夏靈谷得絹以盈萬物得竅生侯王得輕以鳥天下貞 |
| 2 | 傾適也物濕所以得篇物君皆道也天下之人見物而忘道天知其情而己地知其寧而己神知其靈而己谷知其盈而己萬物知其生而巳侯王知其為天下貞而已不知其所以得此若皆遣存馬耳其致之天無以清辯恐裂地無以寧將恐發神無以靈將恐歇谷無以盈持恐竭萬物無冀 |
| 3 | 以生將恐滅侯王無以貴高將恐慶致之吉極也天不得裏遽裂也地不得一末遽發也神不待栗遽歇也谷不得嗜爪遽竭也萬物不得永遽臧也侯王不得慕遽慶也忍其極必至於此耳政貴以賤題本高以下篇基 |
| 4 | 天地之大侯王之貴皆玄憂夫粟何物也視之不見執之不得則亦天下之至微也此所謂賤且下也 |
| 5 | 是以侯王自謂狐寡不穀憚其以賤鵲琴耶非乎 |
| 6 | 昔之為此稱者亦舉其本而潰箕末耳改致教輿無輿不欲祿隸如玉落落如石輪輻蓋軫衡覲轂鬱會曹章物物可數而車不可數蒸役知無有蜜截軍所謂無之以為用者也縣則天地將以大篇天地耶侯王將盛貫篇侯王耶大裹墓請有二行罵此其所以寫天地侯玉者面藝臭知之耳故戶處貴而非貴處賤而非賤非正若玉之諫祿貴而不能賤石豈路落賤而載亡不能貢也 |
| 《反者遺之動童第四卞》 |
| 1 | 反者道之動 |
| 2 | 復性則靜耒納其寂然不動感而憐盡笑下之故則動之祈自起也 |
| 3 | 弱著道之用 |
| 4 | 道無形無聲季之弱考莫如道然而夭下之至強莫頓馬此其所以能迅禹物也天下之物主於有有生於乳 |
| 5 | 世不知靜之漏動弱之為強故告之以物之所自生者蓋天下之物聞有以母制子而末聞有以子制毋者也 |
| 6 | 上士聞遣草第四十一 |
| 7 | 士聞錯窮而行之中士聞道若存若亡下聞道岑失之不笑不足以篇道豈四道非形不可見菲聲不可聞不先知萬物之享爵然弘蔽卓然有見禾免於不信也故下士聞道壑壺廷唐謬德而笑之中士聞道異之存亡出段而疑之惟了然見之者減投勤行服膺而不怠孔子曰語之而旦 |
| 8 | 不惰者其回也輿斯所謂上士也哉建言有之 |
| 9 | 建立也古之立言者有是說而老子取下之所陳者是也 |
| 10 | 明道若妹 |
| 11 | 無所不照兩非察也 |
| 12 | 進道若遐 |
| 13 | 若止不行而天下之迷者莫之惑先己夷道若類 |
| 14 | 或君或顯所至則平而末嘗削也上德若谷 |
| 15 | 上德不德如谷晷虛也 |
| 16 | 大白若辱 |
| 17 | 便白而不受汙此則不絜不眉之士四非聖人也 |
| 18 | 行九籌一廣德若不足 |
| 19 | 廣大而不可復加則止於此悶己深廣也建德若偷 |
| 20 | 因物之自然而無所豈者札岳偷惰曲買建也 |
| 21 | 更 |
| 22 | 山舊琴若渝 |
| 23 | 體性抱神隨物變而刀 |
| 24 | 喻也 |
| 25 | 大方無隅 |
| 26 | 全其大方不小享相大器睨成 |
| 27 | 器大不可近用也 |
| 28 | 木音希聲 |
| 29 | 非旨之所得聞也 |
| 30 | 本象無形 |
| 31 | 誑目之所得見也 |
| 32 | 揖屠無名夫惟道喜貸最 |
| 33 | 道嘉臺所不見凡此十二者皆遺之見於事者也而道之大全則隱於無名惟其所遇推其有餘返貸不足物之額之以成者如此 |
| 《道生缸旱弟四十一》 |
| 1 | 道生一一生二一生二一生萬物萬據眉蔭而抱湯沖氣以篇和 |
| 2 | 卷道非嘉二及其果物希偶道一而道已 |
| 3 | 不一故以了程迴然而道則非一也訊與八篇二二典重僧百是以往而萬物生雖有萬不同而莫不眉陰抱湯沖氣以鴟和者蓋物生於一而一生於一理之旨然也 |
| 4 | 今之蘊鉛懸惟孤寡不穀而王公以羈稱世之人不知萬易之所目生莫不賤寡小而貴泉大然王公之尊而自稱孤寡曩古之達二蓋已知之矣 |
| 5 | 憑軸損之而益或盎之而損人之所教亦我義教之強梁者不得其死吾將寥翩教父世以柔弱為損強梁篇益不知其非也故將便天下之教者皆以此教之曰不見強旗若之不得其死乎強梁妄之極也人知強梁之不免於死則知妄之不可焉笙女之不可焉而彼可典語道棗故曰吾將以悉教父 |
| 《天下之至柔童第四十三》 |
| 1 | 天下之至柔馳騁天下之至堅無有入於無憫吾是以知無焉之有益 |
| 2 | 尸 |
| 3 | 慕了以堅御堅不折則碎以柔御堅柔亦不摩迄堅亦不病求之於物則水是也以有入右土捍不相受以無入有無禾嘗勞有禾嘗愚求之於物則鬼神是也是以聖人唯能無篇故能役使眾強出入群有 |
| 4 | 工芝教無篇之益天下希及之名輿身章第覃四 |
| 5 | 真身孰親身興貨孰多 |
| 6 | 先身而復名貢身而賤賀稽禾篇忘我也夫忘我者身且不有而況於名輿背軍瓜貴以身為天下非忘我不能故使天下知名之不足親貨之不聲駑役知貴身知貴身而後知忘我此老子之意也但冀亡敦病 |
| 7 | 不得者以亡焉病及其既得而患失則川又有甚於亡者惟濟有無均得喪而役無病也 |
| 8 | 是故甚愛必大曹琴藏必厚卜愛之甚則凡可以求之者無所不為能無曹輦藏臺則攻之者必眾能無亡乎知足不辱知止不殆可以長久 |
| 《太成若缺童第四十五》 |
| 1 | 本咸窘缺其用不弊大盈若沖其用不窮天下以不缺篇成故成必有弊以不虛焉盈故盈必有窮聖令要於太成而不䘏其缺期於大勉普曲不惡其沖是以戍而不弊盈而不窮也 |
| 2 | 大直若屈大巧若拙大辯若訥直而不屈苴置必折循理而行雖曲而直巧而不拙其巧必榮付物目然雖拙而巧辯而不訥冀辯黑躬因理而呂雖訥而辯勝寒靜勝熟清滑馮天下正 |
| 3 | 成而不缺盈而不沖直而不屈巧而不拙辯而不訥蓐茹躁之不能靜靜之不能躁耳夫躁能川寒而不能勝熟靜能勝熟而不能勝寒營滯於禹而非其正也唯泊然清淨不染濟嘉成非缺非盈非沖非直非屈非巧非拙非辯非訥而後無所不勝可以為天下正矣 |
| 4 | 天下右蓮量蠹霆十八 |
| 5 | 仁 |
| 6 | 天下有道聚走馬繆異 |
| 7 | 天下各安其分則不爭而自治故卻走馬而糞田 |
| 8 | 天下洲遁茂馬生於郊罪裏大於可欲禍莫大於不知足咎莫大於欲待 |
| 9 | 以其可欲者示人固有罪矣而不足其足者其禍又其薪歡必得若其咎寂大匹夫有幕身蕙愛之俠王而焉是則戎馬之所自起也 |
| 10 | 改知足之足常岸稟 |
| 11 | 知足者所遇而足故無不足也 |
| 《不出屢草第四十七》 |
| 1 | 瓜出戶知天下不窺牖見天道其出彌連其湘彌少 |
| 2 | 性之為體充遍宇宙無速近古令之異古之聖人其所以不出羌牖而無所不知者特其性全故耳世之入為物所蔽性分於耳目內焉身心之所紛亂外為山河之所障寒見不出視聞不出聽完牖之微能蔽而絕之不知聖人復性而足乃欲出而束二迄之是以彌遠而彌少也 |
| 3 | 是以聖人不行而知不見而名不羔而成性之所及非特能知能名而己蓋可以因物之自然不勞而成之矣 |
| 《為學日益董第四十八》 |
| 1 | 黯學日益 |
| 2 | 不知道而務墨閒見日多而無以一之木免為墨若靜李曰多聞擇甚屢者而從之多見而識之知之次也 |
| 3 | 為道日損 |
| 4 | 苟一日知道額槐萬物無菲妄去妄以求復性而性寶無幾孔手謂子貢曰賜也女以于篇茅學而識之考歟曰然非歟曰非也予一以貫之 |
| 5 | 賣牙之又損以至於無為無為而無不篇去妄以求復性基明指矣而去妄之心猶存及其兼忘此心純性而無餘然後無所不篇而不失於難為矣 |
| 6 | 取天下常以墨宇及其有事不足以取天下人皆有欲取天下之心故造事壺水之心昭蠶見於外而物惡之故終不可得聖人無麗故無事其心見於外而物安之雖不取天下而天下歸之矣 |
| 《聖人無常心章第四十九》 |
| 1 | 聖人無常心以百姓心為心善者吾善之不吾者吾亦善喜舊童奢若量璽棗暑昔亦信之德信失 |
| 2 | 虛空無形冒禹物之形慘扁形在方篇方在圓為圓絮蓬皇碧則何以形萬物哉是以聖人無心因百姓少心以為心無善不善管善之堯信不信皆信之善不善在彼而吾之所以呈夏者禾嘗渝也璽明德善參渠信在彼而吾收所以信之若末嘗變也可謂德信矣不然善善翼栗善信信墮葉不信豈所謂常善救衾非棄食 |
| 3 | 霆之在天盃陣慄為天下渾其心百姓皆上眇其耳目聖人普孩之天下善惡信偽方各自是以相非相賊不知所定聖人憂之故標川為天下渾其心建 |
| 4 | 無喜惡無信偽皆以山符之彼方注其耳目以觀聖人之予奪尚吾尸以嬰兒遇之於善無墮告於惡無所嫉夫是以善者不矜惡者不攝釋然皆化而天下始定矣 |
| 《出生入死章茅五十》 |
| 1 | 二山竟十一出生入死 |
| 2 | 性無生死出則篇生入則篇舜生之徒十有一死之徒十有三人之生動之死地一十有三 |
| 3 | 用物取精以自滋養者生之徙也聲色鼻味以自我賊者死之徒也一若既分生死之道矣吾又知作而不知休知言而不知尤知思而不知忘以趣於盡則所謂動而之死地者己生死之道以十呂之三者各居共三矣豈熊生死之遭丸而不生不死之道一而己手不生不死則易所輔寂然不動者也老子言蓋允不呂其覆人自得之以寄蕪思無篇之妙也 |
| 4 | 柯故以其生生之厚 |
| 5 | 肩生則有死故生之徒則苑之促也人之口己所潁於生者厚則死之道常十九芸罟旨善攝生者陸行不遇兕虎入軍不被甲兵兕無所投其角虎無所措其爪兵無所容其刃夫何故以耳蕪死地 |
| 6 | 至人常在不生不死中生旭且無焉有死 |
| 《臥吐》 |
| 1 | 地截 |
| 《道生之章第五十一》 |
| 1 | 道生之德畜之物形之藝箴之道君萬物之母故生萬物者道己及其鍾而篇穗牧泰群眾而沐辭故畜萬物考德也然而道德則不能自形因物而後形見物則不能自成逐近相取剛柔相交積而篇勢而後興亡冶亂之變感天是以萬物莫不尊道而貴德 |
| 2 | 形雖由物成雖由勢而非道不生非德不二怪重一畜是以尊道重貫穗尊赤父光貴茹侯王道無位而德有名故也 |
| 3 | 違之尊德之青衾舍忝鳶爾而常自然悖嘗而後尊普著非實尊貴也殊追生之畜之長臺育之成之熟之養之覆口己之生而不有篇而不恃長而不室卓寵玄德 |
| 《天下有始章第五十二》 |
| 1 | 天下有始以高天下母 |
| 2 | 無名天池之始有名萬物之母道方無名則物之所皆是也及其有名則物之所費生也故謂之始又謂之母其子則萬物也既得共母以知其千既知具子復守其母役身不殆 |
| 3 | 聖人體道以周物壁茹以毋知千了然無不察也雖其智能同之然而末嘗以物忘遭故總守其毋也 |
| 4 | 塞其跪閉其門終身不勤開冀筵濟其事終身不枚 |
| 5 | 天下皆具此遺然常患心道而徇物目悅於色耳悅於聲開其悅之之心而以其事八究十一濟之是以終夏蔭溺而不能救夫聖人之所以終身不勤者唯塞而閉之末嘗出而刀一山 |
| 6 | 積之坦 |
| 7 | 見小曰明 |
| 8 | 悅之羈害始小而浸大知小之將大而閉二亡之可謂明笑 |
| 9 | 暫柔曰強 |

| 1 | 善建煮小據喜抱若不脫于孫祭祀不輟世豈有建而不拔抱而不脫者子惟聖人知性之真審物之妾捕物而脩身其德充精韻只無所立而其廷有不可拔者害蕪所執而其抱有不可胱者故至其于孫糟以祭祀不輟也 |

| 1 | 也 |
| 2 | 故以身觀身以家觀家以鄉觀鄉以國先國以天下觀天下吾何以知天下之然哉鸞此天地外者世俗所不見牟默其理可蕪而更 |

| 1 | 道者萬鍾童喜人臺景善人之所保夫呂可以市尊行可以加人人之不善何棄之口 |
| 2 | 雍 |

This webpage is from the Chinese Text Project (ctext.org), a digital library of Chinese philosophical texts. The page presents the full text of 《道德真經註》 (Commentary on the True Scripture of the Way and Virtue / Daodejing Commentary), a traditional Chinese commentary on the Dao De Jing (Tao Te Ching) attributed to Su Che (蘇轍, styled "眉山蘇轍"), a famous Song Dynasty scholar and official from Meishan, Sichuan.

The content consists of the complete commentary text organized by chapter following the structure of the Dao De Jing, including chapters such as:
- 《道可道章第一》 (Chapter on the Way that can be spoken)
- 《天下皆知章第二》
- 《不尚賢章第三》
- 《道沖章第四》
- 《天地不仁章第五》
- 《谷神不死章第六》
- 《容長久章第七》
- 《上善若水章第八》
- And continuing through all 81 chapters of the Daodejing, ending with 《信言不美章第八十一》

The commentary provides Su Che's philosophical interpretations of each chapter of the Dao De Jing, drawing on Confucian concepts and comparing them with Buddhist thought. A notable concluding section contains a conversation where Su Che discusses the relationship between Confucianism and Buddhism, quoting the Doctrine of the Mean (中庸) and the Sixth Patriarch (六祖) of Zen Buddhism, arguing that Confucian and Buddhist principles ultimately converge—particularly in his interpretations of concepts like "中" (the mean/center) and "和" (harmony).

第三十九章

昔之得一者，天得一以清，地得一以宁，神得一以灵，谷得一以盈，万物得一以生，侯王得一以为天下贞。其致之。天无以清将恐裂，地无以宁将恐发；神无以灵将恐歇，谷无以盈将恐竭，万物无以生将恐灭，侯王无以贵高将恐蹶。故贵以贱为本，高以下为基。是以侯王自谓孤寡不谷。此非以贱为本邪？非乎？故致数舆无舆。不欲[琭琭](https://zhida.zhihu.com/search?content_id=217008096&content_type=Article&match_order=1&q=%E7%90%AD%E7%90%AD&zd_token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJpc3MiOiJ6aGlkYV9zZXJ2ZXIiLCJleHAiOjE3ODc0ODYzMDgsInEiOiLnkK3nkK0iLCJ6aGlkYV9zb3VyY2UiOiJlbnRpdHkiLCJjb250ZW50X2lkIjoyMTcwMDgwOTYsImNvbnRlbnRfdHlwZSI6IkFydGljbGUiLCJtYXRjaF9vcmRlciI6MSwiemRfdG9rZW4iOm51bGx9.UIVEj9la4Z3RqvEcUNjNUoBgK0YAsTlzzyp_Jcg5o-g&zhida_source=entity)如玉、珞珞如石。

**l****昔之得一者，**

[王弼](https://zhida.zhihu.com/search?content_id=217008096&content_type=Article&match_order=1&q=%E7%8E%8B%E5%BC%BC&zd_token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJpc3MiOiJ6aGlkYV9zZXJ2ZXIiLCJleHAiOjE3ODc0ODYzMDgsInEiOiLnjovlvLwiLCJ6aGlkYV9zb3VyY2UiOiJlbnRpdHkiLCJjb250ZW50X2lkIjoyMTcwMDgwOTYsImNvbnRlbnRfdHlwZSI6IkFydGljbGUiLCJtYXRjaF9vcmRlciI6MSwiemRfdG9rZW4iOm51bGx9.ZDuuk5Wy-0PJNYBBahG-NRm2UpuSySXpW18B3AsQ9r0&zhida_source=entity)：昔，始也。一，数之始而物之极也。各是一生，所以为物之主也。物各得此一以成，既成而舍一以居成，居成则失其母，故皆裂、发、歇、竭、灭、蹶也。

译文：昔，是初始的意思。一，是数的起点，也是万物的终极状态。万物都是由道而生，所以道是万物之主。万物各自因道而形成，舍弃道而去坚守已成的具体形器，那就失去了它的根本，所以都会崩裂、荒废、消散、干涸、灭亡、衰败。

**l****天得一以清，地得一以宁，神得一以灵，谷得一以盈，万物得一以生，侯王得一以为天下贞。其致之。**

王弼：各以其一，致此清、宁、灵、盈、生、贞。

译文：万物各凭大道，达到了天清、地宁、神灵、谷盈、生存、忠诚等状态。

**l****天无以清将恐裂，**

王弼：用一以致清耳，非用清以清也。守一则清不失，用清则恐裂也。故为功之母不可舍也。是以皆无用其功，恐丧其本也。

译文：天要凭借道才能达到清明，而不是用清理来达到清。天能坚守道就能不失清明，如果采取清理的方式那恐怕就要崩裂。所以建功立业的道是不能舍弃的。所以舍弃道而只关注功绩，恐怕就丧失根本了。

**l****地无以宁将恐发；神无以灵将恐歇，谷无以盈将恐竭，万物无以生将恐灭，侯王无以贵高将恐蹶。故贵以贱为本，高以下为基。是以侯王自谓孤寡不谷。此非以贱为本邪？非乎？故致数舆无舆。不欲琭琭如玉、珞珞如石。**

王弼：清不能为清，盈不能为盈，皆有其母，以存其形。故清不足贵，[盈不足](https://zhida.zhihu.com/search?content_id=217008096&content_type=Article&match_order=1&q=%E7%9B%88%E4%B8%8D%E8%B6%B3&zd_token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJpc3MiOiJ6aGlkYV9zZXJ2ZXIiLCJleHAiOjE3ODc0ODYzMDgsInEiOiLnm4jkuI3otrMiLCJ6aGlkYV9zb3VyY2UiOiJlbnRpdHkiLCJjb250ZW50X2lkIjoyMTcwMDgwOTYsImNvbnRlbnRfdHlwZSI6IkFydGljbGUiLCJtYXRjaF9vcmRlciI6MSwiemRfdG9rZW4iOm51bGx9.GtFG1Yfw7RfZc8pdv_cMRhK8-KyqAGzG8XWE9fNUZXA&zhida_source=entity)多，贵在其母，而母无贵形。贵乃以贱为本，高乃以下为基。故致数舆乃无舆也。玉石琭琭、珞珞，体尽于形，故不欲也。

译文：清理无法达到清明，充填无法达到盈满，都是要从根本的道来入手，才能保存各自的形象状态。所以不该看重清理和填充，而应该关注道，然而道没有形象。贵以贱为根本，高以下为基础。所以就算多次得到了名誉也和没有名誉一样。玉美、石坚，全部表露于外形上，而不能深藏，因而贵贱、毁誉一目了然，所以不要像玉石这样。

args.summary:
This is a Zhihu (Chinese Q&A platform) article by author 子燊 (Zi Shen) published on November 3, 2022, providing a translation and annotation of Chapter 39 of the Daodejing (Tao Te Ching) based on Wang Bi's (王弼) commentary. The article is part of the "觉醒之旅" (Journey of Awakening) column.

The article presents the original classical Chinese text of Chapter 39 alongside Wang Bi's annotations and the author's modern Chinese translations. The core content covers the concept of "obtaining the One" (得一) — how heaven obtains the One to become clear, earth to become peaceful, spirits to become spiritual, valleys to become full, myriad things to be born, and lords to become upright rulers. The chapter warns that if these states are lost, disaster follows: heaven would crack, earth would collapse, spirits would dissipate, valleys would run dry, things would perish, and rulers would fall.

Key interpretive points from Wang Bi's commentary (as translated by the author):
- "一" (the One) is the starting point of numbers and the ultimate state of all things; the Dao is the mother/master of all things, and clinging to formed shapes while abandoning the Dao leads to ruin
- Heaven attains clarity through the Dao, not through "clearing" (清) itself; one must hold to the Dao (守一) rather than focus on the achievement
- Nobility is rooted in lowliness (贵以贱为本), height is based on lowness (高以下为基)
- The chapter concludes that one should not be like sparkling jade or hard stone — things that reveal all their qualities externally — but should return to fundamental simplicity, because even attaining many honors is like having no honor

The article includes two endorsements ("2 人赞同") and is categorized under topics including Laozi Daodejing (老子道德经) and History of Chinese Philosophy (中国哲学史). Recommended readings at the bottom link to other Daodejing study notes on Zhihu, including chapters 32 and 46.

Chapter 20 of the Dao De Jing presents the text with the line "绝学无忧" (Abandon learning and you will be free from worries). The webpage provides two commentaries: "道德经注" (annotation on the Dao De Jing) and "无上妙道文始真经" (another interpretive layer).

The annotations explain key phrases: "唯之与阿，相去几何" (How much difference is there between respectful response and careless response?), and "众人熙熙，如享太牢" (The multitude bustle about, as if enjoying a great feast).

The commentary notes: "绝学无忧" means abandoning excessive study can bring freedom from worries, and describes the sage as one who is childlike and undifferentiated, unlike the bustling multitude.

The webpage includes navigation to all 81 chapters and is part of a dedicated Dao De Jing resource site.
args.summary:
This webpage is part of daodejing.org (道德经), a dedicated Chinese-language resource site for the Dao De Jing (Tao Te Ching). The page presents Chapter 20 (第二十章) of the classic text alongside two layers of commentary: a primary annotation titled "道德经注" and a second interpretive layer titled "无上妙道文始真经."

The chapter's core text includes the opening line "绝学无忧" (Abandon learning and you will be free from worry), followed by the passage "唯之与阿，相去几何？善之与恶，相去若何" (How much difference between respectful response and careless response? How much between good and evil?), and "众人熙熙，如享太牢" (the multitude bustle about as if at a great feast), along with descriptions contrasting the sage, who remains childlike and undifferentiated (如婴儿之未孩), with the bustling masses.

The annotations explain these passages in detail: interpreting "绝学无忧" as freedom from worries through abandoning excessive study; analyzing the difference between respectful and careless responses as nearly nonexistent; and elaborating on how the sage embodies a childlike simplicity, not distinguishing sharply between things that conventional people fuss over. A referential note cites interpretations suggesting the passage reflects on how ordinary people enjoy themselves like at a grand banquet while the sage remains content with simple desires (食母/以食其母), emphasizing a state of undifferentiated simplicity.

The page is part of a broader site offering the complete Dao De Jing across all 81 chapters (linked via numbered navigation 1 through 81), with additional resources on related Laozi topics including feng shui, translations, audio readings, biographies, and philosophical interpretations. The content reflects a largely unreadable/mangled text encoding in the raw scrape, but the visible structure indicates a traditional Chinese scholarly page presenting the original text of Chapter 20 with commentary and translations.

| 1 | 老子道德经下篇 魏 王弼 注三十八章案河上公注本，此为论德章。永乐大典此章以下块注张之象所录王注脱误甚多，今无别本可校，姑仍旧文。上德不德，是以有德，下德不失德，是以无德。上德无为而无以为，下德为之而有以为，上仁为之而无以为，上义为之而有以为，上礼为之而莫之应，则攘臂而扔之。案扔，各本俱作仍}}故失道而后德，失德而后仁，失仁而后义，失义而后礼。夫礼者，忠信之薄而乱之首。前识者，道之华而愚之始。是以大丈夫处其厚不居其薄，处其实不居其华。案焦竑云古本四句并作处故去彼取此。德者，得也。常得而无丧，利而无害，故以德为名焉，何以得？德由乎道也，何以尽德？以无为用。以无为用则莫不载也。故物无焉则无物，不经有焉则不足以免其生，是以天地虽广，以无为心；圣王虽大，以虚为主。故曰：以复而视，则天地之心见；至日而思之，则先王之至覩也。故灭其私而无其身，则四海莫不瞻，远近莫不至，殊其己而有其心，则一体不能自全，肌骨不能相容。是以上德之人唯道是用，不德其德，无执无用，故能有德而无不为，不求而得，不为而成。故虽有德而无德名也。下德求而得之，为而成之，则立善以治物，故德名有焉。求而得之，必有失焉；为而成之，必有败焉；善名生，则有不善应焉。故下德为之而有以为也无以为者无所徧为也凡不能无为而为之者皆下德也仁义礼节是也将明轴之上下辄举下德以对上德至于无以为极下德下之量上仁是也足及于无以为而犹为之焉为之而无以为故有为为之患矣本在乳为母在无名弃本拾毋而适其子功虽大焉必有不济名虽美焉伪亦必生不能不为而成不典而治则乃为之故有弘普博施仁爱之者而爱之无所偏私故上仁为之而无以为也爱不能兼则有抑抗正真而义理之者忿枉佑直助彼攻此物事而有以心为矣故上义为之而有以为也直不能笃则有游饰修文礼敬之者尚好修敬校责往来则不对之间忿怒生焉故上礼为之而莫之应则攘臂而仍之夫大之极也其唯道乎自此己往岂足尊哉故虽盛业大富而有万物犹谷得其德虽贵以无为用不能拾无以为体也不能拾无以为体则失其为大矣所谓失道而后德也以无为用德其毋故能己不劳马而物无不理下此己往则失用之母不能无为而贵博施不能博施而贵正直不能正直而贵饰敬所谓失德而后仁失仁而后义笑义而役礼也夫礼也所始首于忠信不笃通简不阳贵备于表机微竽制夫仁义发于内为之犹伪况务外饰而可久手故夫礼者忠信之簿而乱之首也前识者前人而识也即下德之伦也竭其聪明以为前识役具智力以营庶事虽德其情奸巧弥密虽丰其誉愈丧笃实劳而事昏务而治盖虽竭圣智而民愈害舍己任物则无为而泰守夫素朴则不顺典制听彼所获禁此所守识道之华而愚之首故苟得其为功之毋则万物作马而不辞也万事存焉而不劳也用不以形御不以名故名仁义可显礼敬可彰也夫载之以大遗镇之以示名则物无所尚忘无所启容仕其贞事用其诚则仁德厚焉行义正焉礼敬清台禁其所载舍其所测用其成形役其聪明仁则诚马义其竞焉礼其字焉故仁德之厚非用仁之所能也行义乏正非用义之所成也礼敬之清非用礼之所济也载之以道统之以毋故显之而无所尚彰之而无所竞用天无名故名以笃焉用天无形故形以感马守母以存其子崇本以举其末则形名俱有而邪不生大美配天而华不作故母不可远本不可夫仁义母之所生非可以为母形器匠之所成非可以为匠也拾具母而用其子弃其本而适其末名则有所分形则有所止虽极其大必有不周虽盛其美必有患忧功在为之岂足处也 |

args.summary:
This webpage is from the Chinese Text Project (中国哲学书电子化计划, ctext.org), specifically the wiki page for the "Lower Section" (下篇) of the Laozi Daodejing (老子道德经), in simplified Chinese. It presents the complete text of chapters 38-81 of the Daodejing with the annotations of Wang Bi (王弼, 226-249 CE), a renowned Wei dynasty commentator.

The page includes:
- The full annotated text of the "Lower Section" (chapters 38 through 81) with Wang Bi's commentary
- Chapters covered include: 38 (论德), 39 (法本), 40 (去用), 41 (同异), 42 (道化), 43 (徧用), 44 (立戒), 45 (洪德), 46 (俭欲), 47 (鉴远), 48 (忘知), 49 (任德), 50 (贵生), 51 (养德), 52 (归元), 53 (益证), 54 (修观), 55 (玄符), 56 (玄德), 57 (淳风), 58 (顺化), 59 (守道), 60 (居位), 61 (谦德), 62 (为道), 63 (恩始), 64 (守微), 65 (淳德), 66 (后己), 67 (三宝), 68 (配天), 69 (玄用), 70 (知难), 71 (知病), 72 (爱己), 73 (任为), 74 (制惑), 75 (贪损), 76 (戒强), 77 (天遗/天道), 78 (任信), 79 (任契), 80 (独立), 81 (显质)
- Reference to the Siku Quanshu (钦定四库全书) edition, with officials listed including 详校官侍郎臣谢墉, 检讨臣何思钧, etc.
- Note that the text is an initial draft created via OCR (字符识别) from a photographic copy, with a request for users to help correct errors
- Key philosophical themes preserved in Wang Bi's commentary include: wuwei (无为, non-action), the concept of Dao (道) as the mother/origin of all things, the priority of the root (本) over branches (末), the virtue of weakness/flexibility over strength, and the critique of ritual (礼) as "the thin edge of loyalty and trust and the beginning of chaos"
- The URN for this resource is ctp:ws767045
- Includes a colophon noting the text was transcribed in 政和乙未 (1115 CE) and references to editions by 熊克 and others

The page also provides navigation and metadata about the Chinese Text Project website, including copyright information (2006-2026), contact methods via social media (Facebook, Twitter, Weibo, Douban), and information about supporting the project.

第六章

**谷神不死，是谓玄牝，[玄牝之门](https://zhida.zhihu.com/search?content_id=214060680&content_type=Article&match_order=1&q=%E7%8E%84%E7%89%9D%E4%B9%8B%E9%97%A8&zd_token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJpc3MiOiJ6aGlkYV9zZXJ2ZXIiLCJleHAiOjE3ODcxNjgxODUsInEiOiLnjoTniZ3kuYvpl6giLCJ6aGlkYV9zb3VyY2UiOiJlbnRpdHkiLCJjb250ZW50X2lkIjoyMTQwNjA2ODAsImNvbnRlbnRfdHlwZSI6IkFydGljbGUiLCJtYXRjaF9vcmRlciI6MSwiemRfdG9rZW4iOm51bGx9.prNvdFx9pYzQnRkOTUZ7qjJxXEDAPRPnaarEN4gPw_o&zhida_source=entity)，是谓天地根。绵绵若存，用之不勤。**

[王弼](https://zhida.zhihu.com/search?content_id=214060680&content_type=Article&match_order=1&q=%E7%8E%8B%E5%BC%BC&zd_token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJpc3MiOiJ6aGlkYV9zZXJ2ZXIiLCJleHAiOjE3ODcxNjgxODUsInEiOiLnjovlvLwiLCJ6aGlkYV9zb3VyY2UiOiJlbnRpdHkiLCJjb250ZW50X2lkIjoyMTQwNjA2ODAsImNvbnRlbnRfdHlwZSI6IkFydGljbGUiLCJtYXRjaF9vcmRlciI6MSwiemRfdG9rZW4iOm51bGx9._I5RF_yRslYWlBvO0-Yg-nqFuk1OK-fD0F6f8JK2inU&zhida_source=entity)：谷神，谷中央无谷者也。无形无影，无逆无违，处卑不动，守静不衰，谷物以之成而不见其形，此至物也。处卑而守静不可得而名，故谓之玄牝。门，玄牝之所由也。本其所由，与[太极](https://zhida.zhihu.com/search?content_id=214060680&content_type=Article&match_order=1&q=%E5%A4%AA%E6%9E%81&zd_token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJpc3MiOiJ6aGlkYV9zZXJ2ZXIiLCJleHAiOjE3ODcxNjgxODUsInEiOiLlpKrmnoEiLCJ6aGlkYV9zb3VyY2UiOiJlbnRpdHkiLCJjb250ZW50X2lkIjoyMTQwNjA2ODAsImNvbnRlbnRfdHlwZSI6IkFydGljbGUiLCJtYXRjaF9vcmRlciI6MSwiemRfdG9rZW4iOm51bGx9.tLQ8QX_R-Enr9CK9FN2sgLdjpuVlbE6guMfhgyy3ImU&zhida_source=entity)同体，故谓之“天地之根”也。欲言存邪，则不见其形；欲言亡邪，万物以之生，故“绵绵若存”也。无物不成用而不劳也，故曰用而不勤也。

译文：道就像山谷，它的中间是空虚的。没有形象也没有影子，没有服从也没有违背，处在下位丝毫不动，守着虚静而不衰败，道就是以这样的特性存在而又看不见它的形相，这是事物达到极限的状态。处在下位且守着虚静，无法理解所以这么称呼它，把它叫作玄牝。门，万物最初生养的地方。正因为它是本源，和太极是同一个东西，所以叫天地之根。想说它存在，但又看不到它的形相；想说它不存在，但万物又依靠它才能生长，所以叫绵绵若存。没有事物不依靠它而生成，然而它又不操劳费神，所以叫用而不勤。

args.summary:
This is a Zhihu (知乎) article by author 子燊 (Zishen), part of the "觉醒之旅" (Awakening Journey) column, providing a translation and commentary on Chapter 6 of Wang Bi's (王弼) "老子道德经注" (Annotation of the Laozi/Daodejing). The article was published on November 14, 2023, in Shanghai.

The chapter text (第六章) reads: "谷神不死，是谓玄牝，玄牝之门，是谓天地根。绵绵若存，用之不勤。" (The valley spirit never dies - this is called the Mysterious Feminine. The gate of the Mysterious Feminine is called the root of heaven and earth. It continues endlessly as if existing, yet functions without exertion.)

Wang Bi's original commentary explains that the "valley spirit" (谷神) refers to the empty center of a valley, which is formless and shadowless, neither resisting nor disobeying, dwelling low without moving, guarding stillness without decline. It is how things are formed invisibly. Because it is lowly and still, it cannot be named, hence called the Mysterious Feminine (玄牝). Its "gate" (门) is where the Mysterious Feminine originates, sharing the same essence as the Ultimate (太极/Taiji), hence called the "root of heaven and earth." It cannot be said to exist (form unseen) nor to not exist (all things born from it), hence "continues endlessly as if existing" (绵绵若存). Nothing is formed without it, yet it does not labor, hence "functions without exertion" (用之不勤).

The author's vernacular Chinese translation explains that the Dao is like a valley with an empty center - without form or shadow, neither obeying nor disobeying, dwelling below without moving, guarding stillness without decaying. This is the state of things reaching their limit. The Mysterious Feminine is so named because its lowly, still nature makes it hard to comprehend. The gate is where all things are initially born; since it is the origin and is identical to Taiji, it is called the root of heaven and earth. It cannot be said to exist (form unseen) nor not to exist (all things depend on it for growth) - hence "continues endlessly as if existing." Nothing exists without it, yet it does not exert itself - hence "functions without exertion."

The article has 2 likes and 3 comments. One commenter noted a typographical error in the commentary ("与太九极同体" instead of "与太极同体"), which the author confirmed as a typo and corrected. Related recommended readings include articles on the Mawangdui silk manuscript version of the Laozi, the Wang Bi edition of the Daodejing, and a full 81-chapter translation of the text.

# 老子成玄英疏

[跳到导航](#mw-head) [跳到搜索](#p-search)

《老子成玄英疏》由唐代[成玄英](/wiki/%E6%88%90%E7%8E%84%E8%8B%B1 "成玄英")所撰，原疏已散佚，散见于《道藏》本强思齐《道德真经玄德纂疏》和顾欢《道德真经注疏》等，近人蒙文通将其搜集整理，辑校为《老子成玄英疏》六卷，由四川省立图书馆于1946年石印刊行。另有严灵峰《道德经开题序诀义疏》五卷、日人藤原高男《辑校赞道德经义疏》两种辑校本。作者在书中阐述了“重玄之道”，认为玄的含义为深远，既不执著有也不执著无，即“非有非无”；但还不能执著于玄，必须否定玄，即“非非有非无”，才能彰明重玄之道。此即对老子“玄之又玄”一语的诠释。这样解释引进了庄子思想和佛教中观哲学，为本书的一大特色。本书反映了唐代道教哲学的理论思辨水平，是唐代道教[重玄学派](/wiki/%E9%87%8D%E7%8E%84%E5%AD%B8%E6%B4%BE "重玄学派")的代表作之一。

args.key_excerpts: 作者在书中阐述了"重玄之道"，认为玄的含义为深远，既不执著有也不执著无，即"非有非无"；但还不能执著于玄，必须否定玄，即"非非有非无"，才能彰明重玄之道。此即对老子"玄之又玄"一语的诠释。这样解释引进了庄子思想和佛教中观哲学，为本书的一大特色。本书反映了唐代道教哲学的理论思辨水平，是唐代道教重玄学派的代表作之一。近人蒙文通将其搜集整理，辑校为《老子成玄英疏》六卷，由四川省立图书馆于1946年石印刊行。
args.summary:
《老子成玄英疏》是由唐代成玄英撰写的一部道教经典注疏著作。原疏已散佚，其内容散见于《道藏》本强思齐的《道德真经玄德纂疏》和顾欢的《道德真经注疏》等文献中。近人蒙文通将该书辑校为六卷本，由四川省立图书馆于1946年以石印方式刊行。此外还有严灵峰的《道德经开题序诀义疏》五卷和日人藤原高男的《辑校赞道德经义疏》两种辑校本。

本书的核心内容在于阐述"重玄之道"的思想。作者认为"玄"的含义是深远，既不执著有也不执著无，即"非有非无"；但更进一步，还不能执著于"玄"本身，必须否定"玄"，即达到"非非有非无"，才能彰明重玄之道。这是对老子"玄之又玄"一语的诠释。该书的一大特色是引进了庄子思想和佛教中观哲学来阐释道家思想。

本书反映了唐代道教哲学的理论思辨水平，是唐代道教重玄学派的代表作之一。文中还提供了相关参考资料，包括卿希泰主编的《中国道教史》（四川人民出版社，1992年）第二卷第174至189页、《中国道教》（知识出版社，1994年）第二卷第90至92页，以及胡孚琛主编的《中华道教大辞典》（中国社会科学出版社，1995年）第316页。

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage is an academic journal article record from an Airiti Library database (a Chinese academic platform). The article is "成玄英《道德經義疏》重玄思想之探析" (Exploration and Analysis of Cheng Xuan-ying's Twofold Mystery Thoughts in Dao De Jing Yi Shu), written by 林文彬 (Wen-Ping Lin), published in 《興大中文學報》(Journal of the Chinese Department of National Chung Hsing University), Issue 29, June 2011, pages 179-192. DOI: https://doi.org/10.30091/JCDNCHU.201106.0007.

The article examines Cheng Xuan-ying (成玄英), an important representative of the School of Twofold Mystery (重玄學派) in the Early Tang Dynasty. The Dao De Jing Yi Shu is his foundational work, which uses the "Twofold Mystery" (重玄) concept to establish an ontological realm of unobstructed reason (虛通之理) and emphasize cultivation of the mind and nature through wisdom (智悟).

The paper identifies three academic contributions of the work: (1) Regarding Laozi studies, it links academia and religion while summarizing predecessors' theories; (2) In Chinese intellectual history, it represents a third period of Taoist thought development after Wei-Jin Xuanxue, serving as a fusion of Xuanxue (Neo-Taoism) and Buddhist Prajñā (Wisdom); (3) In terms of influence, it is the most philosophically significant school in Taoist history, influencing Song and Yuan dynasty Inner Alchemy (Neidan) and the Science of Mind-Nature, and likely enlightening Neo-Confucianism development.

The historical context notes that Sun Deng of the Eastern Jin Dynasty first annotated Laozi using the Twofold Mystery concept, and from the Southern and Northern Dynasties through the Sui and Tang Dynasties, many Taoists used it to comment on Laozi and Zhuangzi, forming the School of Twofold Mystery.

Keywords: 成玄英 (Cheng Xuan-ying); 重玄 (Twofold Mystery); 道德經 (Dao De Jing); 虛通之理 (unobstructed reason); 眾生之性 (nature of beings).

CORE ARGUMENT: The paper analyzes the theoretical structure of Cheng Xuan-ying's discussions of mind (心), nature (性), emotions (情), and desire (欲) in his Daodejing commentary, and explores their deep relationship with Buddhist thought. In the early Tang dynasty, Buddhist mind-nature theory had matured, and Daoist Chongxuan (double mystery, 重玄) studies required development of mind-nature theory, leading Daoist commentators on the Laozi to focus on "mind" and "nature" topics while integrating Buddhist thought.

THREE OBSERVATIONAL APPROACHES (the paper's structure):
1. "Dao-Nature Continuity" (道、性一貫) as the ideological premise: Cheng holds that "Dao" and "nature" are one — the innate natural nature/true nature of all beings derives from the transcendent Dao. He explains "Dao" as "void and penetrating" (虛通), and states "所謂無極大道，是眾生之正性也" (the infinite great Dao is the true nature of all beings). He uses "principle" (理) to characterize Dao, marking a major breakthrough in his Laozi scholarship. Dao's subtle principle, when internalized in humans and things, becomes their nature; hence to "preserve and return to true nature" is the path of self-cultivation.
2. "Forgetting Emotions to Complete Nature" (忘情全性) as the master thesis: In commenting on "道可道，非常道," Cheng details the relations among Dao, nature, emotions, form (形), qi (炁), and spirit (神). Since "性動為情" (nature stirring becomes emotion) and emotions contaminate, nature is damaged and distances from Dao. The key statement: "生我者道，滅我者情，茍忘其情，則全乎性" (Dao gives me life, emotions destroy me; if one forgets emotions, nature is made complete). The dialectical process runs: Dao-Nature originally one → Dao-Nature separated (through stirring emotions, deluded mind chasing external objects) → Dao-Nature re-united through cultivation ("復性歸道" / returning nature to Dao as ultimate aim).
3. "Deluded Mind," "Emotional Contamination," and "Attachment to Objects" (妄心、情染、滯境) and the path of cultivation: Cheng identifies deluded mind, emotional contamination, and attachment to sensory objects as the root causes of losing true nature. His cultivation approach incorporates extensive Buddhist concepts — "empty" (空), "mind abiding nowhere" (無所住心), "three karmas clean" (三業清靜), "liberation of six sense faculties" (六根解脫), the bodhisattva ideal, "three poisons" (貪嗔痴), "dependent arising and emptiness" (緣起性空), etc. He reframes the Daoist sage as a bodhisattva-like figure; explains "returning to root/stillness/mandate" (歸根復命); and advocates for "復於真性，反於惠命" (returning to true nature and inherent mandate).

CONCLUSIONS (two observations):
1. The mind-nature discourse of early Tang Chongxuan studies may have independently influenced the mid-Tang Confucian revival (e.g., Li Ao's (李翱) 《復性書》/ "Essay on Restoring Nature," which also advocates "滅情復性" / extinguishing emotions to restore nature). The paper argues the theory of "restoring nature" (復性) was initiated by Cheng Xuan-ying well before Li Ao, challenging the view that Laozi mind-nature interpretation only fully developed in the Song dynasty.
2. The paper highlights the distinctive features of Cheng Xuan-ying's mind-nature discourse in the 《義疏》 and evaluates his value and status in the history of Laozi scholarship — characterizing the early Tang Chongxuan mind-nature theory as marked by Buddhist-Daoist mutual influence, whereas Song Confucian-Laozi interpretation turned toward Confucian-Daoist convergence.

KEY SCHOLARS CITED: Li Gang (李剛) argues Cheng's theory of restoring nature is richer than Li Ao's and scattered across his Laozi/Zhuangzi commentaries; Tang Yi-jie (湯一介) sees Chongxuan philosophy moving from ontology to mind-nature philosophy, similar to Song-Ming Neo-Confucianism (especially Cheng-Zhu), urging attention to the Chongxuan-Song Neo-Confucianism relationship; Dong En-lin divides Tang Laozi studies into three stages (early: Chongxuan with Buddhist coloring; middle: Tang Xuanzong's politicization; late: compilations by Qiang Siqi and Du Guangting). This webpage is from the Chinese Text Project (ctext.org), specifically the wiki section of the Chinese Philosophy Digital Project, presenting the text "道德真經玄德纂疏卷一" (Volume 1 of the Moral Classic's Dark Virtue Compilation Commentary). This is a Daoist commentary on the Daodejing (Tao Te Ching) compiled by Xiqiang Si (濛陽強思齊), featuring annotations from Tang Emperor Xuanzong (唐玄宗, imperial commentary), He Shang Gong (河上公), Yan Junping (嚴君平), Li Rong (李榮), and Cheng Xuanying (成玄英).

The text opens with an introduction describing the Daodejing as the crown of the three teachings and leader of all scriptures. The first chapter (道可道章第一) is divided into four sections: (1) marking the principle and teaching, (2) broadly clarifying root and traces, (3) distinguishing the two contemplations (of Existence and Non-existence), and (4) unifying the "double mystery" (重玄) principle.

Key content includes extensive commentary on the opening lines: "道可道，非常道" (The Dao that can be spoken is not the eternal Dao) and "名可名，非常名" (The name that can be named is not the eternal name). The commentary explores the concept of the Three Ones (三一: essence, spirit, and qi) as the body of Laozi, discusses creation from primordial qi (元氣), and explains that the eternal Dao transcends speech, form, sound, and thought.

The second chapter (天下皆知章第二) addresses how "when all under heaven know beauty as beauty, ugliness arises" and "when all know goodness as goodness, non-goodness arises." URL: https://weread.qq.com/web/reader/9da32eb0813abad60g01907d

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is a WeRead (微信读书) book page for 《道德真经注》(Commentary on the Tao Te Ching of True Scripture) written by 李荣 (Li Rong), a Daoist priest of the Tang Dynasty. It is an important early Daoist systematic commentary on the 《道德经》(Tao Te Ching/Laozi). Key details:

- The current edition is included in the 《正统道藏》洞神部 (Orthodox Daoist Canon, Dong Sheng section).
- The work originally had two volumes (上/下), commenting on the 36 chapters of the Tao Te Ching; the present edition is partially incomplete (残佚).
- Written during the early Tang when "重玄学" (Chongxuan/Twofold Mystery school) flourished; Li Rong extensively used 重玄 methods and integrated Confucian, Buddhist, and Daoist views.
- The commentary interprets Laozi's core concepts: "无为" (wuwei/non-action), "致虚" (attaining emptiness), "守静" (maintaining stillness), "返本" (returning to the origin).
- Unlike later detailed textual/philological commentaries, Li Rong's annotations are concise and clear, emphasizing the philosophical structure of Laozi's thought: "虚静" as the root of cultivating the mind, "无为" as essential to all affairs, "复归本真" (returning to true nature) as the foundation of self-cultivation.
- The work reflects Daoist practice/self-cultivation elements and shows the Tang Daoist trend of moving from "玄学" (Dark Learning/Xuanxue) toward systematic commentary.

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage from the 道教文化中心資料庫 (Daoism Culture Center Database) documents the **唐玄宗御制道德真經疏** (Commentary on the Daodejing Authored by Emperor Xuanzong of Tang), a ten-volume Daoist text. Key details include:

- **Authorship**: Ostensibly written by Emperor Xuanzong (李隆基) of the Tang Dynasty, but in reality compiled jointly by Daoist priests and officials proficient in Laozi's teachings. Completed in the 23rd year of the Kaiyuan era (735 CE).
- **Structure**: Originally six volumes, but the Zhengtong Daozang (正統道藏) edition comprises ten volumes, categorized under the 洞神部玉訣類 (Dongshen Division, Jade Instructions section, 效 character number). Also exists in Dunhuang manuscript fragments.
- **Content**: Serves as a sub-commentary (疏) explaining Xuanzong's own earlier work 道德真經注 (Commentary on the Daodejing), incorporating older interpretations and contemporary discussions referred to as "又解" (additional explanations). It reflects early Tang debates between Buddhism and Daoism concerning the doctrinal principles of the Daodejing.
- **Methodology**: Adopts the 重玄學 (Chongxuan) "開題釋義" (opening topic and explanation) writing format, providing a "釋題" (explaining the title) before each chapter to clarify the chapter structure and layers of meaning. This approach parallels the method used by Cheng Xuanying (成玄英) in his 道德經開題序訣義疏.
- **Relation**: It is a continuation of Xuanzong's 道德真經注, sharing the same doctrinal purpose.
- **Reference**: Cited from 胡孚琛 (Hu Fuchen) ed., 中華道教大辭典 (Beijing: 中國社會科學出版社, 1995), p. 316.
- **Classification**: Categorized under 洞神部玉訣類 and 唐代道教經典 (Tang Dynasty Daoist classics).
</summary>

SUMMARY:
<summary>
《唐玄宗御注道德真经》是唐玄宗李隆基对《道德经》的御注著作，全书四卷，共八十一章，成书于开元二十年（732年）至二十一年（733年）之间。

【成书过程】唐玄宗因认为以往各家对《道德经》的注疏"并未精当，有失玄元妙旨"，担心"无为之理将失"，而决定亲自作注。他一生两度注释《道德经》：开元二十三年（735年，时年51岁）首次完成《御注道德经》并颁之全国，诏令天下"士庶家藏一本，劝令习读"，此次采用河上公本《老子》为底本；约二十年后（天宝十四年，755年）进行第二次注疏，称《道德经真经疏》，因对河上公本不满意而改用王弼本为底本，并再次亲自作序颁于天下。

【内容结构】全书共四卷，分《道经》上下、《德经》上下各二卷，总计八十一章，每章以开头三五字为章名，依从古本。唐玄宗改定章句，"凡言道者类之上卷，言德者类之下卷"。流传中存在二卷本（如《新唐书·艺文志》所载）与四卷本（《道藏》本）之别。

【主要思想】御注的根本宗旨在于"理身理国"，核心是阐发老子的无为之理，并发展了这一哲学，具体体现在君德官德思想、民本与教化思想、"国际交往"思想及军事战争哲学中的自然无为、慈爱于人、节俭爱费、谦柔不争、公平无私等主张。

【刊刻与流传】开元二十三年（735年），唐玄宗采纳道门威仪司马秀建议，诏令天下各州在主要大道观设立石台，刊刻勒石此注，以使其"晓谕天下，传之久远"。注本曾在全国多地刻石留存，包括成都、阌乡、荆州、怀州、遂州、易州、邢州、苏州等处。后世主要流传版本有易州本和邢州本。至今在河南鹿邑太清宫、河北易县、邢台市、江苏镇江焦山、陕西周至县等地仍存有唐代留下的道德经碑幢，其中鹿邑太清宫的碑刻即"开元神武皇帝《道德经》注碑"。明人焦竑《老子翼》卷七记载："唐玄宗既注《老子》，始改定章句为《道德经》……刻石涡口老子庙中"。2024年有研究著作《唐玄宗御注〈道德经〉心解》出版。
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"唐玄宗李隆基注。成书于开元二十年（732年）至二十一年（733年）之间。原书四卷，章数八十一章。", "唐玄宗一生中两度注释《道德经》。开元二十三年(735年)首次完成《御注道德经》，并颁之全国。此次注疏采用河上公本《老子》。天宝十四年(755年)，唐玄宗第二次注《道德经》，是谓《道德经真经疏》，此次重新采用王弼本加以注释。", "唐玄宗御注《道德真经》的根本宗旨在于'理身理国'，其思想核心是阐发老子的无为之理。", "焦竑在《老子翼》卷七中记载：'唐玄宗既注《老子》，始改定章句为《道德经》。凡言道者类之上卷，言德者类之下卷。刻石涡口老子庙中。'", "开元二十三年（735年），唐玄宗采纳道门威仪司马秀的建议，诏令天下各州于主要大道观设立石台，刊刻勒石《御注道德真经》，以推广其注本，旨在使注本'晓谕天下，传之久远'。"

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is a Chinese Taoist studies encyclopedia page about the "Daode Zhenjing Zhuan (道德真经传)" — a four-volume commentary on the Daodejing (Tao Te Ching) written by Lu Xisheng (陆希声), a Tang Dynasty scholar. The work is included in the Zheng Tong Dao Zang (正统道藏) canon under the Dong Shen Bu Yu Jue category (洞神部玉诀类), and appears at sutra number 680 in the Dao Zang Ti Yao index, located in volume 368 of the Hanfenlou edition, volume 20 of the Xinwenfeng edition, and volume 12 of the Sanjia edition. It is also included in volume 9 of the Zhonghua Daozang under the Four Supplementary Scriptures section.

The book begins with a self-authored preface (自序) in which Lu Xisheng critiques various earlier commentators on Laozi's teachings. He argues that Yang Zhu (杨朱) adhered to Laozi's substance but fell short by excessively valuing the body and despising material things; Zhuangzi (庄周) mastered Laozi's function but went too far by seeking to abandon sageliness and discard wisdom; Shen Buhai and Han Feizi (申韩) lost Laozi's reputation through harsh and punitive governance; and Wang Bi and He Yan (王何) lost Laozi's way by falling into empty nihilism and indolence. Lu considered Sima Qian (司马迁) to be the closest approximation of true Laozi philosophy among ancient writers.

Lu Xisheng further develops his core thesis by connecting Laozi with three sages: he claims Laozi shares the same origin (同原) as Fu Xi, who drew the Eight Trigrams, depicted all phenomena, explored the principles of life, and followed the harmony of virtue; that Laozi shares the overarching lineage (通其宗) with King Wen, who observed the I Ching's yin-yang movements, valued strength and change while emphasizing moderation; and that Laozi's views align in power/application (与其合其权) with Confucius, who emulated Yao and Shun, modeled the Zhou founders Wen and Wu, and guided the people through benevolence and righteousness. Lu concludes that Laozi "transformed and connected with, turned back and merged with" all three sages, making him "utterly divine" (至神). The entire work combines Confucian and Taoist thought to present a political philosophy, making it an important source for late Tang intellectual and ideological history.

The page cites Hu Fuchen's "Zhonghua Daojiao Da Cidian" (Chinese Taoist Encyclopedia, China Social Sciences Press, Beijing, 1995, p. 316) as a reference. The page is categorized under the Dong Shen Bu Yu Jue (洞神部玉诀类) and Tang Dynasty Taoist Classics (唐代道教经典).
</summary>

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage presents an academic thesis record from Airiti Library (華藝線上圖書館) for a master's thesis titled 陸希聲《道德真經傳》思想詮構 (An Interpretation of the Thought of Lu Xisheng's "Commentary on the Dàodéjīng" / Dao De Jing Zhuan) by 林佳蓉 (Lin Chia-jung), advised by 江淑君 (Jiang Shu-jun), from the Department of Chinese Literature, National Taiwan Normal University (國立臺灣師範大學), completed in 2012.

The abstract outlines the thesis's key findings: the author examines the philosophical system within Lu Xisheng's commentary on the Laozi (老子). Key research conclusions include: (1) Lu Xisheng sought to integrate Daoist thought with Confucian ideas; (2) he introduced the "權-實" (quan-expedient/shí-substantial) category as a framework for rulers' governance, built on a tǐ/yòng (substance/function) model where the expedient derives from the substantial; (3) the thesis addresses the structure of the work across Dao-ontology (道體論), human nature theory (性情論), and self-cultivation theory (修身論), all ultimately serving governance theory (治國論); (4) Lu proposed concepts like "化情復性" (transforming emotions to restore nature) and "以性正情" (correcting emotions through nature); and (5) the thesis situates Lu's interpretation within the Tang dynasty's "老學" (Laozi studies) tradition, showing the convergence of Confucian and Daoist thought and the merging of Daoist-legalist (黃老) approaches to governance, particularly the emphasis on ritual (禮) to govern a chaotic era.

Keywords: 陸希聲 (Lu Xisheng); 《道德真經傳》 (Commentary on the Dàodéjīng); 性情論 (theory of human nature and emotions); 修身治國 (self-cultivation and governance); 唐代老學 (Tang dynasty Laozi studies).

The page also lists several classical references (works by 王邦雄, 朱伯崑, 牟宗三, etc.) and two theses that cited this work, along with a link to the institutional repository (National Taiwan Normal University).
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
筆者以《道德真經傳》為主要研究對象，藉由〈道德真經傳序〉的內容，以及書中詮解《老子》所引用的文獻與概念，釐清其撰作動機與目的。接著，進一步深入探索、詮構文本中的思想體系。,陸希聲援引眾多儒家典籍文獻與《老子》交相比附，這對於儒、道思想的融通，是值得考索的一個面向；然而，從傳解內容中，也可見其轉化老子思想之處。,最後，考索陸希聲運用「權─實」這組範疇的淵源，倡議「權─實」為安頓上位者治國統御的思想。並以體用模式建構權實之間的關係，權實之間相依不二：權既由實所生、為實之用，行權之時，須以實為基準與目標。,陸希聲點掇性、情、欲之義，論證性何以化而為情，又如何受到愛欲的影響，並由此提出「化情復性」、「以性正情」等等概念，導正人們日益放失的嗜欲之情。,如此以儒、道思想相融共濟的政治訴求，可謂唐代以「修身治國」解《老子》突出的特色之一。

--- SOURCE 1: 谷神不死，是謂玄牝-譯文_意思_解釋_原文_出處_賞析_河上公 ---
URL: https://www.shidianguji.com/zh/mingju/7621557849307824178

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage presents an annotated analysis of the classical Chinese Daoist quote "谷神不死，是谓玄牝" (gu shen bu si, shi wei xuan pin), which is attributed to the Han dynasty commentator Heshang Gong (河上公) and sourced from the "老子道德經" (Dao De Jing), specifically the "成象" (Cheng Xiang) chapter six of the SBCK (四部叢刊) edition based on the Changshu Qu family's Song dynasty print.

The quote is categorized under the theme of "无为自然" (Wu Wei / natural action) with the genre being classical prose (古文).

Key content elements:
- Original quote: "谷神不死，是謂玄牝。玄牝之门，是谓天地根。绵绵若存，用之不勤。" (The valley spirit never dies; this is called the mysterious feminine. The gate of the mysterious feminine is called the root of heaven and earth. Continuous, as if existing, yet functioning without exertion.)
- The translation provided: "虚空神妙的道，永恒不灭，这就是玄妙的母体。" (The empty and mysterious Dao is eternal and indestructible; this is the mysterious maternal source.)
- Context note: This sentence is described as one of the core expressions of the chapter, elaborating the eternal and original nature of the Dao, reflecting Laozi's profound thinking on the origin of the universe.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
谷神不死，是謂玄牝。玄牝之门，是谓天地根。绵绵若存，用之不勤。, 虚空神妙的道，永恒不灭，这就是玄妙的母体。 (The empty and mysterious Dao is eternal and indestructible; this is the mysterious maternal source.), 阐述道的永恒与本源特性，是老子对宇宙生成根源的深刻思考。 (It elaborates the eternal and original nature of the Dao, reflecting Laozi's profound thinking on the origin of the universe.)
</key_excerpts>

--- SOURCE 2: 老子道德经开题序诀义疏 - 道教文化中心資料庫 ---
URL: https://zh.daoinfo.org/index.php?title=%E8%80%81%E5%AD%90%E9%81%93%E5%BE%B7%E7%B6%93%E9%96%8B%E9%A1%8C%E5%BA%8F%E8%A8%A3%E7%BE%A9%E7%96%8F&variant=zh-hans

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage from the Daoism Culture Center Database (道教文化中心資料庫) provides an entry on 《老子道德经开题序诀义疏》 (Laozi Daode Jing Kaiti Xujue Yishu), a work on the Daodejing (Laozi) written by Cheng Xuanying (成玄英), a Daoist scholar of the early Tang Dynasty. The work originally comprised seven volumes, as recorded in the New Book of Tang (《新唐书》) and Comprehensive Treatises on Literature (《通志》). The text was not included in the Zhengtong Daoist Canon (《正统道藏》). Existing copies include three Tang dynasty Dunhuang manuscript fragments (P2353, S5887, and P2517). Selections of Cheng Xuanying's commentary also appear in other works such as 《道德真经注疏》 and 《道德真经玄德纂疏》. The modern scholar Meng Wentong (蒙文通) compiled 《校理老子成玄英疏叙录》 based on the Dunhuang manuscripts and the Daoist Canon texts. The work interprets the Laozi through the "Chongxuan" (Twofold Mystery, 重玄) philosophy of Tang Dynasty Daoism, arguing that the Great Dao (道) is neither being nor non-being, and both being and non-being simultaneously—hence described as "huanghu" (vague/obscure). The text emphasizes that Dao is not separate from things ("道不离物" - Dao is not separate from things; "道外无物" - nothing exists outside Dao). It advocates for transcending both attachment to existence and attachment to non-existence ("有无双遣"), using the concept of "xuan" (玄, mystery) and "xuan zhi you xuan" (玄之又玄, mystery upon mystery) to progressively discard dualistic attachments. This "Chongxuan" doctrine had a significant influence on the development of Tang Dynasty Daoist philosophy. The page is categorized under Dunhuang documents and Tang Dynasty Daoist classics, and cites Hu Fuchen's 《中华道教大辞典》 (1995), p. 316, as a reference source.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"夫道无所不在，所在皆无，荡然无际，有何封域也？" (The Great Dao is everywhere present; where it is present, it is nothing; it is vast and boundless, so what boundaries does it have?), "道不离物，物不离道。道外无物，物外无道。用即道物，体即物道。" (Dao is not separate from things, things are not separate from Dao. There is nothing outside Dao, and no Dao outside things.), "为学之人执于有欲，为道之士又滞无为。虽复深浅不同，而二俱有患。今欲治此两执，故有再损之文。既而前损损有，后损损无，二偏双遣，以至于一中之无为。" (Those who study cling to desire; those who practice the Dao become attached to non-action. Though different in depth, both have afflictions. To cure these two attachments, there is the teaching of further diminishment.), "有滞之人唯滞于有，无滞之士又滞于无，故说一玄以遣双执。又恐学者滞于此玄，今说又玄，更怯后病。既而非但不滞，亦乃不滞于不滞，此则遣之又遣，故曰玄之又玄。" (Those attached cling to being; those unattached cling to non-being, so one mystery (xuan) is taught to dispel both attachments. Fearing students would cling to this mystery, the "further mystery" is taught—not only not clinging, but not clinging to non-clinging—this is the dispelling of dispelling, hence "mystery upon mystery.")
</key_excerpts>

--- SOURCE 4: 成玄英《道德經義疏》重玄思想之探析 ---
URL: https://www.airitilibrary.com/Article/Detail/19914822-201106-201108300014-201108300014-179-192

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage is an academic journal article record from an Airiti Library database (a Chinese academic platform). The article is "成玄英《道德經義疏》重玄思想之探析" (Exploration and Analysis of Cheng Xuan-ying's Twofold Mystery Thoughts in Dao De Jing Yi Shu), written by 林文彬 (Wen-Ping Lin), published in 《興大中文學報》(Journal of the Chinese Department of National Chung Hsing University), Issue 29, June 2011, pages 179-192. DOI: https://doi.org/10.30091/JCDNCHU.201106.0007.

The article examines Cheng Xuan-ying (成玄英), an important representative of the School of Twofold Mystery (重玄學派) in the Early Tang Dynasty. The Dao De Jing Yi Shu is his foundational work, which uses the "Twofold Mystery" (重玄) concept to establish an ontological realm of unobstructed reason (虛通之理) and emphasize cultivation of the mind and nature through wisdom (智悟).

The paper identifies three academic contributions of the work: (1) Regarding Laozi studies, it links academia and religion while summarizing predecessors' theories; (2) In Chinese intellectual history, it represents a third period of Taoist thought development after Wei-Jin Xuanxue, serving as a fusion of Xuanxue (Neo-Taoism) and Buddhist Prajñā (Wisdom); (3) In terms of influence, it is the most philosophically significant school in Taoist history, influencing Song and Yuan dynasty Inner Alchemy (Neidan) and the Science of Mind-Nature, and likely enlightening Neo-Confucianism development.

The historical context notes that Sun Deng of the Eastern Jin Dynasty first annotated Laozi using the Twofold Mystery concept, and from the Southern and Northern Dynasties through the Sui and Tang Dynasties, many Taoists used it to comment on Laozi and Zhuangzi, forming the School of Twofold Mystery.

Keywords: 成玄英 (Cheng Xuan-ying); 重玄 (Twofold Mystery); 道德經 (Dao De Jing); 虛通之理 (unobstructed reason); 眾生之性 (nature of beings).

References cited include works by 牟宗三 (才性與玄理, 1980), 牟鐘鑒/張踐 (中國宗教通史, 2003), 任繼愈 (道藏提要, 1991; 中國道教史, 1990), and 袁保新 (老子哲學之詮釋與重建, 1991), all with Google Scholar links.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
The content is to discuss Metaphysics with Twofold Mystery and narrate the process of cultivation and realization of pure mind based on mind and nature.
</key_excerpts>

--- SOURCE 5: 成玄英《道德經開題序訣義疏》中的心性論述 - 國文學系 ---
URL: https://www.ch.ntnu.edu.tw/SIS/downloadfile.php?periodicalsPage=2&issue_id=13&paper_id=59

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is an academic paper (published in *Studies in Sinology* / 《中國學術年刊》, Volume 36, Autumn issue, September 2014, pp. 19-42, ISSN 1021-7851) by Chiang Shu-chun (National Taiwan Normal University, Department of Chinese) examining the theory of mind-nature (心性論述, xinxing) in Cheng Xuan-ying's (成玄英) commentary on the Daodejing, titled 《道德經開題序訣義疏》 (Dao Der Jing Kai Ti Xu Jue Yi Shu).

CORE ARGUMENT: The paper analyzes the theoretical structure of Cheng Xuan-ying's discussions of mind (心), nature (性), emotions (情), and desire (欲) in his Daodejing commentary, and explores their deep relationship with Buddhist thought. In the early Tang dynasty, Buddhist mind-nature theory had matured, and Daoist Chongxuan (double mystery, 重玄) studies required development of mind-nature theory, leading Daoist commentators on the Laozi to focus on "mind" and "nature" topics while integrating Buddhist thought.

THREE OBSERVATIONAL APPROACHES (the paper's structure):
1. "Dao-Nature Continuity" (道、性一貫) as the ideological premise: Cheng holds that "Dao" and "nature" are one — the innate natural nature/true nature of all beings derives from the transcendent Dao. He explains "Dao" as "void and penetrating" (虛通), and states "所謂無極大道，是眾生之正性也" (the infinite great Dao is the true nature of all beings). He uses "principle" (理) to characterize Dao, marking a major breakthrough in his Laozi scholarship. Dao's subtle principle, when internalized in humans and things, becomes their nature; hence to "preserve and return to true nature" is the path of self-cultivation.
2. "Forgetting Emotions to Complete Nature" (忘情全性) as the master thesis: In commenting on "道可道，非常道," Cheng details the relations among Dao, nature, emotions, form (形), qi (炁), and spirit (神). Since "性動為情" (nature stirring becomes emotion) and emotions contaminate, nature is damaged and distances from Dao. The key statement: "生我者道，滅我者情，茍忘其情，則全乎性" (Dao gives me life, emotions destroy me; if one forgets emotions, nature is made complete). The dialectical process runs: Dao-Nature originally one → Dao-Nature separated (through stirring emotions, deluded mind chasing external objects) → Dao-Nature re-united through cultivation ("復性歸道" / returning nature to Dao as ultimate aim).
3. "Deluded Mind," "Emotional Contamination," and "Attachment to Objects" (妄心、情染、滯境) and the path of cultivation: Cheng identifies deluded mind, emotional contamination, and attachment to sensory objects as the root causes of losing true nature. His cultivation approach incorporates extensive Buddhist concepts — "empty" (空), "mind abiding nowhere" (無所住心), "three karmas clean" (三業清靜), "liberation of six sense faculties" (六根解脫), the bodhisattva ideal, "three poisons" (貪嗔痴), "dependent arising and emptiness" (緣起性空), etc. He reframes the Daoist sage as a bodhisattva-like figure; explains "returning to root/stillness/mandate" (歸根復命); and advocates for "復於真性，反於惠命" (returning to true nature and inherent mandate).

CONCLUSIONS (two observations):
1. The mind-nature discourse of early Tang Chongxuan studies may have independently influenced the mid-Tang Confucian revival (e.g., Li Ao's (李翱) 《復性書》/ "Essay on Restoring Nature," which also advocates "滅情復性" / extinguishing emotions to restore nature). The paper argues the theory of "restoring nature" (復性) was initiated by Cheng Xuan-ying well before Li Ao, challenging the view that Laozi mind-nature interpretation only fully developed in the Song dynasty.
2. The paper highlights the distinctive features of Cheng Xuan-ying's mind-nature discourse in the 《義疏》 and evaluates his value and status in the history of Laozi scholarship — characterizing the early Tang Chongxuan mind-nature theory as marked by Buddhist-Daoist mutual influence, whereas Song Confucian-Laozi interpretation turned toward Confucian-Daoist convergence.

KEY SCHOLARS CITED: Li Gang (李剛) argues Cheng's theory of restoring nature is richer than Li Ao's and scattered across his Laozi/Zhuangzi commentaries; Tang Yi-jie (湯一介) sees Chongxuan philosophy moving from ontology to mind-nature philosophy, similar to Song-Ming Neo-Confucianism (especially Cheng-Zhu), urging attention to the Chongxuan-Song Neo-Confucianism relationship; Dong En-lin divides Tang Laozi studies into three stages (early: Chongxuan with Buddhist coloring; middle: Tang Xuanzong's politicization; late: compilations by Qiang Siqi and Du Guangting). The paper used the Yan Ling-feng (嚴靈峯) edition of the reconstructed 《義疏》 as primary text.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"所謂無極大道，是眾生之正性也。" (卷二章一 Annotated in Cheng Xuan-ying's commentary on the first chapter — "the infinite great Dao is the true nature of all beings.") , "生我者道，滅我者情，茍忘其情，則全乎性。" (From his commentary on "道可道，非常道" — the master thesis of "forgetting emotions to complete nature.") , "湯一介：『重玄學』以「理」釋「道」，又提出「道者，虛通之理，眾生之正性」……通過「窮理盡性」而實現與道合一。這與宋明理學（特別是程朱派）的路數極為相近。" , "李剛：『對重玄學來說，要體認重玄之道，其途徑就在於從心性入手，做到心空，不起妄心；性真，復歸真性。典型代表是成玄英。』" , "與李翱的復性論比較起來，成玄英具有自己的特色且內容更為豐富，只不過李翱的學說集中於〈復性書〉，而成玄英論復性則散見於他對老莊的解讀中。"
</key_excerpts>

--- SOURCE 6: 道德真经注（李荣） - 道教文化中心資料庫 ---
URL: https://zh.daoinfo.org/index.php?title=%E9%81%93%E5%BE%B7%E7%9C%9F%E7%B6%93%E8%A8%BB%EF%BC%88%E6%9D%8E%E6%A6%AE%EF%BC%89&variant=zh-hans

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage provides information about the Daoist text 《道德真经注》(Annotation on the Classic of the Way and Virtue) by Li Rong (李荣), a Daoist priest of the Tang Dynasty during the reign of Emperor Gaozong (唐高宗). The work comprises four volumes and is included in the Orthodox Daoist Canon (《正统道藏》) in the Dongshendi Yujue category. 

Key facts about the text:
- Title: 道德真经注 (Li Rong's annotation)
- Author: Li Rong (李荣)
- Length: Four volumes (四卷)
- Location in Daoist Canon: 洞神部玉诀类, 絲字号
- Editions: Hanfenlou edition volume 430, Xinwenfeng edition volume 23, Sanjia edition volume 14
- Daozang catalogue number: 717
- Included in the Zhonghua Daozang, volume 9

The surviving edition only contains annotations for chapters 1-36 of the Daodejing. The missing portions can be supplemented using Dunhuang manuscripts and cross-checked against Qiang Siqi's 《道德真经玄德纂疏》to reconstruct the complete version of Li Rong's commentary. The annotation is significant for its emphasis on the "Chongxuan" (Double Mystery/Twofold Profundity) doctrine, making it an important source for studying Tang Dynasty Daoist thought.

The reference source is: Hu Fuchen's 《中华道教大辞典》(Chinese Encyclopedia of Daoism, Beijing: China Social Sciences Press, 1995), page 316. The webpage is categorized under both "洞神部玉诀类" (Dongshen Section Jade Instructions category) and "唐代道教经典" (Tang Dynasty Daoist classics).
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
道德真经注，唐高宗时道士李荣撰。四卷，收于《正统道藏》洞神部玉诀类。, 此本仅存第一至三十六章经注，其缺佚部分可据敦煌抄本补，复校以强思齐《道德真经玄德纂疏》，可得李荣注本完帙。, 其注主重玄说，是研究唐代道教思想的重要资料。, 胡孚琛主编：《中华道教大辞典》（北京：中国社会科学出版社，1995年），第316页。
</key_excerpts>

--- SOURCE 8: [PDF] 李榮《道德經注》心性思想研究 - 國文學系- 國立臺灣師範大學 ---
URL: https://www.ch.ntnu.edu.tw/SIS/downloadfile.php?periodicalsPage=2&issue_id=12&paper_id=55

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This academic article, "Study of mind thinking from Li Rong's (李榮) note for TaoDeJing (道德經注)" (published in Studies in Sinology, Vol. 37, Spring 2015, pp. 97-116, by Hsieh, Wan-hsin), examines the mind-nature theory (心性論) in Li Rong's commentary on the Tao Te Ching. Li Rong (號任真子) was a prominent early Tang dynasty Taoist of the Chongxuan (重玄, "Double Mystery") school, equally famous as Cheng Xuanying, and considered a representative figure of Chongxuan learning. The article argues that while Li Rong's academic importance parallels Cheng Xuanying's, he has not received commensurate scholarly attention.

The paper is organized into four main sections. First, on theory of nature (性論), Li Rong distinguishes two levels of nature: the "natural nature" (自然之性), which is innate, pure, self-sufficient, and perfectly complete (本乎自然, 樸，本也), and the "emotional nature" (情性), which derives from yin-yang qi and is subject to desires, deceptions, and sensory attractions. Li Rong advocates "以性制情" (controlling emotions with nature) and returning to one's original nature. His view of nature as the highest moral value aligns with the Cheng-Zhu school's "性即理" (nature is principle) approach.

Second, on theory of mind (心論), Li Rong attributes three functions to the mind: activity (活動義), cognition (認知義), and grasping/clinging (執取義). He calls the mind a "靈臺" (spirit tower) and "玄鏡" (mysterious mirror), which can illuminate and perceive the world, but once the mind stirs and clings to external phenomena, it covers the original nature. The mind can move toward either Dao-action (undirected) or non-Dao-action; cultivation work must therefore begin from the mind itself.

Third, on cultivation practices (心性修養工夫), Li Rong proposes three methods: (1) "制之未動，持心守心" (controlling before movement begins, guarding and keeping the mind), using the analogy of upper, middle, and lower scholars to describe levels of prevention; (2) "虛心復性" (emptying the mind and restoring nature), including "灰心" (ash-heart, extinguishing desires) and "混心" (mixing the mind, eliminating discriminations); and (3) "不滯兩邊，遣之又遣" (not adhering to either extreme, dispelling again and again), a double-dispelling Chongxuan method that transcends all dualities and even forgets the dispelling itself.

The conclusion highlights that Li Rong inherited and developed Cheng Xuanying's ideas—Cheng emphasized "復性" (restoring nature) while Li emphasized "修心" (cultivating the mind)—both predating Li Ao's famous "復性說" in the mid-Tang. Li Rong's philosophy notably shifted away from traditional Daoist immortality-seeking toward spiritual cultivation, even asserting that "心為死地" (the mind is the place of death), meaning that once the mind dies, even a living physical body is as good as a walking corpse. The article includes an abstract in English and extensive bibliographic references in Chinese and English on Chongxuan studies.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
物之性也，本乎自然，欲者以染愛累真，學者以分別妨道，遂使真一之源不顯，至道之性難明，不入於無為，但歸於敗失。聖人順自然之本性，輔萬物以保真，不敢行於有為，導之以歸虛靜也。, 亦言人性自然已足，益之則憂，夫進智以徇美，與飾偽以為惡，事雖不同，失性均也。, 李榮以靈臺、玄鏡稱呼此心，言人心如水，水心靜而明，人心虛而鑑。, 夫生我者神，殺我者心，我殺由心，心為死地。若能灰心息慮，不構有為，無死地也。, 不滯兩邊，自合中道。
</key_excerpts>

--- SOURCE 9: 道德真經章句訓頌 - 维基文库，自由的图书馆 ---
URL: https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/%E9%81%93%E5%BE%B7%E7%9C%9F%E7%B6%93%E7%AB%A0%E5%8F%A5%E8%A8%93%E9%A0%8C

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is a Wikisource page hosting the complete text of "道德真經章句訓頌" (Commentary and Eulogy on the Chapters and Sentences of the True Scripture of the Way and Virtue), a commentary on the Daodejing (Tao Te Ching) written by Zhang Sicheng (張嗣成), the 39th Celestial Master of the Zhengyi (Orthodox Unity) Daoist sect, during the Yuan Dynasty. The work is dated to the summer of 1322 (至治壬戌). It is included in the Orthodox Daoist Canon (正統道藏). The page contains the author's preface, followed by the text of all 81 chapters of the Daodejing divided into two volumes (卷上 and 卷下), with each chapter providing the original text, a poetic eulogy (頌), and a prose commentary (訓). Zhang Sicheng's interpretation emphasizes that Dao (道) consists of principle (理) and vital energy (氣), and explains concepts like non-action (無為), the unity of heaven, earth, and humanity, cultivation of spirit and vital energy for longevity, and the nature of the Dao as formless yet all-pervading. The work synthesizes Daoist cosmology with inner cultivation practices. The page notes the work is in the public domain since the author died over 100 years ago. The complete commentary text through chapter 64 is included, with chapters 65-81 listed in the table of contents but their content appears to be missing/empty in this version. The page also lists other Daodejing commentaries available on Wikisource, including Wang Bi's, Heshang Gong's, Tang Xuanzong's, Song Huizong's, Ming Taizu's, and others.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>

<summary>
This is a Chinese Taoist studies encyclopedia page about the "Daode Zhenjing Zhuan (道德真经传)" — a four-volume commentary on the Daodejing (Tao Te Ching) written by Lu Xisheng (陆希声), a Tang Dynasty scholar. The work is included in the Zheng Tong Dao Zang (正统道藏) canon under the Dong Shen Bu Yu Jue category (洞神部玉诀类), and appears at sutra number 680 in the Dao Zang Ti Yao index, located in volume 368 of the Hanfenlou edition, volume 20 of the Xinwenfeng edition, and volume 12 of the Sanjia edition. It is also included in volume 9 of the Zhonghua Daozang under the Four Supplementary Scriptures section.

The book begins with a self-authored preface (自序) in which Lu Xisheng critiques various earlier commentators on Laozi's teachings. He argues that Yang Zhu (杨朱) adhered to Laozi's substance but fell short by excessively valuing the body and despising material things; Zhuangzi (庄周) mastered Laozi's function but went too far by seeking to abandon sageliness and discard wisdom; Shen Buhai and Han Feizi (申韩) lost Laozi's reputation through harsh and punitive governance; and Wang Bi and He Yan (王何) lost Laozi's way by falling into empty nihilism and indolence. Lu considered Sima Qian (司马迁) to be the closest approximation of true Laozi philosophy among ancient writers.

Lu Xisheng further develops his core thesis by connecting Laozi with three sages: he claims Laozi shares the same origin (同原) as Fu Xi, who drew the Eight Trigrams, depicted all phenomena, explored the principles of life, and followed the harmony of virtue; that Laozi shares the overarching lineage (通其宗) with King Wen, who observed the I Ching's yin-yang movements, valued strength and change while emphasizing moderation; and that Laozi's views align in power/application (与其合其权) with Confucius, who emulated Yao and Shun, modeled the Zhou founders Wen and Wu, and guided the people through benevolence and righteousness. Lu concludes that Laozi "transformed and connected with, turned back and merged with" all three sages, making him "utterly divine" (至神). The entire work combines Confucian and Taoist thought to present a political philosophy, making it an important source for late Tang intellectual and ideological history.

The page cites Hu Fuchen's "Zhonghua Daojiao Da Cidian" (Chinese Taoist Encyclopedia, China Social Sciences Press, Beijing, 1995, p. 316) as a reference. The page is categorized under the Dong Shen Bu Yu Jue (洞神部玉诀类) and Tang Dynasty Taoist Classics (唐代道教经典).

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage from Chinese Wikisource (zh.wikisource.org) presents the complete text of 《唐玄宗御註道德真經》(Tang Xuanzong's Imperial Commentary on the True Scripture of the Way and Virtue), an annotated edition of the Tao Te Ching (道德經) written by Emperor Xuanzong of Tang, Li Longji (李隆基). The work is part of a series of Tao Te Ching commentaries catalogued on the page, which includes other notable commentaries such as Wang Bi's edition, the He-shang Gong chapter commentary, Song Huizong's royal commentary, Zhu Yuanzhang's commentary, and others.

The document is structured into four volumes (卷之一 through 卷之四) covering the Dao Jing (道經) and De Jing (德經) sections, containing all 81 chapters of the Tao Te Ching. Each chapter presents the original text followed by the Emperor's annotations in angle brackets (〈〉). Volume 1 (道經上) covers chapters 1-19, Volume 2 (道經下) covers chapters 20-37, Volume 3 (德經上) covers chapters 38-59, and Volume 4 (德經下) covers chapters 60-81.

The commentary provides philosophical interpretations grounded in Daoist concepts: the emperor explains key notions such as the Dao as formless and ineffable ("道者，虛極之妙用"), the harmony of yin-yang and qi (沖氣), the virtues of emptiness, stillness, and non-action (無為), and the importance of humility and yielding (守雌). The commentary frequently cites concepts from Zhuangzi and applies the teachings to governance, emphasizing that rulers should practice wu-wei (non-interference), rely on naturalness, avoid excessive warfare, and cultivate moral virtue to bring order to the state. For example, in Chapter 57 the emperor writes that "我無為而民自化，我無事而民自富，我好靜而民自正，我無欲而民自樸" (when I practice non-action the people transform themselves; when I am without affairs the people prosper; when I love stillness the people correct themselves; when I am without desire the people become simple). 

The work is attributed to the Tang dynasty, is classified under Emperor Li Longji, the Zhengtong Daozang, and the Tang dynasty, and is noted to be in the public domain since the author died over 100 years ago and the work was published before January 1, 1931.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
唐玄宗御註道德真經 is a Tang dynasty imperial commentary on the Tao Te Ching authored by Emperor Li Longji (唐玄宗/李隆基), included in the Zhengtong Daozang (正統道藏), "唐玄宗御註道德真經"

URL: https://zh.wikipedia.org/zh-hans/%E7%B6%93%E5%85%B8%E9%87%8B%E6%96%87

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is a Chinese Wikipedia article about the 《经典释文》 (Jingdian Shiwen / "Classics Explained"), a comprehensive phonetic annotation work on Chinese classics written by the Sui-Tang dynasty Confucian scholar 陆德明 (Lu Deming). Key facts:

**Background and Purpose:**
- Completed in 583 CE (至德元年 of Southern Chen dynasty / 开皇三年 of Sui dynasty), making it a late 6th-century work, not a Tang dynasty work as sometimes thought
- Authored to address the problem that classical texts had "旧音太简" (old pronunciations were too simple) and divergent interpretations had arisen; Lu Deming compiled it based on collating texts and consulting the Cangjie pian and Erya
- Contains 30 volumes (卷), providing phonetic annotations (mainly using 反切 fanqie method) for both classical texts and their commentaries
- Used and cited over 230 scholars' analyses of sounds and meanings, citing 20 Han and Six Dynasties scholars for phonetic research including 徐邈, 李轨, 刘昌宗, 郭璞, 郭象, 韦昭, 向秀, 王元规, 崔撰, 吕忱, 沈重, 戚衮, 沈旋, 谢峤, 顾野王, 孙炎, 郑玄, 王肃, 何胤, 施干
- Since the Tang dynasty, it served alongside the 《十三经注疏》 (Thirteen Classics with Commentaries) as a basis for reading classics
- Still preserves quotations from many now-lost ancient books

**Linguistic Significance:**
- Scholar 高本汉 (Bernhard Karlgren) called the 《经典释文》 and the 《切韵》 (Qieyun, 601 CE) the two main bases for reconstructing Middle Chinese (中古汉语)
- It is a representative work of southern standard pronunciation slightly earlier than the Qieyun, notable for its numerous polysemous readings (异读)

**Content Structure (30 volumes):**
- Vol 1: Preface/General records (序录)
- Vol 2: Zhouyi phonetic annotations
- Vols 3-4: Shangshu (2 vols)
- Vols 5-7: Maoshi/Book of Songs (3 vols)
- Vols 8-9: Zhouli (2 vols)
- Vol 10: Yili
- Vols 11-14: Liji (4 vols)
- Vols 15-20: Chunqiu Zuozhuan (6 vols)
- Vol 21: Chungqiu Gongyang
- Vol 22: Chunqiu Guliang
- Vol 23: Xiaojing
- Vol 24: Lunyu
- Vol 25: Laozi
- Vols 26-28: Zhuangzi (3 vols)
- Vols 29-30: Erya (2 vols)

**Textual History/Editions:**
- The earliest copies were written in two colors: black for the classic text, red for the annotation; by late Tang this was simplified to single-color writing with red dots above the text, and later to monochrome entirely
- Earliest surviving version: Song dynasty carved edition with Song-Yuan repairs (宋刻宋元递修本), not reprinted during Yuan and Ming dynasties
- Qing Kangxi period: Xu Qianxue's Tongzhitang Jingjie edition, based on a manuscript copy by Ye Linzong of a Song edition (since destroyed) held in Qian Qianyi's Jiangyunlou collection
- Qing Qianlong period: Lu Wenchao's edition with 30-volume 《考证》 (Textual Research) inscribed in the Baowentang Congshu, collated against Ye Linzong's copy with broad use of various scholars' findings
- The Song-Yuan repaired edition was only photographically reprinted by Shanghai Ancient Books Publishing House in 1985
- Comparatively: the Tongzhitang edition is the poorest, the Baowentang edition better but not ideal due to collation issues; the Song edition is high quality in original leaves but its Yuan-dynasty repaired leaves contain many errors
- 2006: Zhonghua Book Company published Huang Zhuo's 《经典释文汇校》 (Collected Collations), based on the Tongzhitang edition, collating against all 30-volume carved editions, 30-volume manuscript copies, and the Yuan-Ming editions of the Thirteen Classics commentaries, incorporating Qing-era collation results; format shows Tongzhitang text on top and collation notes below
- Huang's work is considered the most reliable edition, extensively using Dunhuang manuscripts and fragmentary copies in collation, deemed "天下至慎" (the most cautious in the world) for not making hasty judgments

**References and External Links:**
- References Victor H. Mair's work in The Indiana Companion to Traditional Chinese Literature (1998)
- Links to various scholarly articles and the ctext.org project for different editions
</summary>

《经典释文》成书于南朝陈至德元年（583，隋开皇三年），是隋唐经学家陆德明的著作，解释儒家经典与《老》、《庄》音义的专著。他鉴于当时经典"旧音太简，微言久绝，大义愈乖，后人攻乎异端，竟生穿凿"的现象，于是在校理群书的基础上，著《经典释文》30卷。, 其列举徐邈、李轨、刘昌宗、郭璞、郭象、韦昭、向秀、王元规、崔撰、吕忱、沈重、戚衮、沈旋、谢峤、顾野王、孙炎、郑玄、王肃、何胤、施干等汉六朝二十家音切考证，基于230家诸说分析字音字义。, 高本汉称《经典释文》和《切韵》(601)是构拟中古汉语两个主要的根据。, 在汉语音韵史上，《经典释文》是比《切韵》略早的南方标准音代表著作，以极多的异读为重要特征。, 2006年，中华书局排印出版了黄焯的《经典释文汇校》。……《汇校》之作就已远超乾嘉以来诸家。……可谓"天下至慎"，所以堪称目前值得信赖的版本。

The chapter text is: "谷神不死，是謂玄牝" (The valley spirit never dies; it is called the mysterious female), followed by "玄牝門，天地根" and "綿綿若存，用之不勤" (Although it remains continuously, its use cannot be exhausted).

The chapter text centers on the famous line "谷神不死，是謂玄牝" (The valley spirit never dies; it is called the mysterious female).

The page presents the core text of Chapter Six:
- 谷神不死，是謂玄牝。 (The valley spirit never dies, which is called the mysterious female.)
- 玄牝門，天地根。 (The gate of the mysterious female is the root of heaven and earth.)
- 綿綿若存，用之不勤。 (Continuously existing as if present, yet used without exertion.)

The annotation section presents extensive textual criticism and variant readings from numerous scholars:

1. **Textual variants of "谷":** Multiple scholars (畢沅, 俞樾, 洪頤烜, 徐鼒) debate whether the character should be 谷, 浴, or 穀. The He-shang Gong (河上公) edition used 浴, which various scholars argue was a phonetic loan for 穀/谷 meaning "to nourish" (養). Scholar 俞樾 argues "浴" has no true meaning of nourishing and should be read as 谷. Wang Bi's (王弼) base text used 穀.

2. **Semantic interpretation:** Scholars like 司馬光 (Sima Guang) and 嚴復 (Yan Fu) interpret 谷 (valley) as representing emptiness, 神 (spirit) as the unfathomable, and 不死 (not dying) as the inexhaustible nature of the Dao.

3. **勤 (qin) readings:** Scholar 洪頤烜 reads 勤 as 廑 (weak/small). Scholar 於省吾 argues against this, reading 勤 as 覲 (to be seen), interpreting "用之不見" (used but not seen), connecting to the idea that it is subtle and seemingly nonexistent.

4. **Rhyme analysis (音韻):** The chapter's rhyme scheme is analyzed by 江氏, 姚文田, 鄧廷楨, 王念孫, 顧炎武 (Gu Yanwu), 江永, 嚴可均, and 魏建功. The characters 死、牝 (si, pin) rhyme in the 脂 rhyme group, while 門、根、存、勤 (men, gen, cun, qin) rhyme in the 文 group. Historical pronunciations of 牝 (formerly read 扶履反) and 谷 are discussed based on ancient texts.

5. **Word counts:** The chapter's variants differ: the 景龍碑 (Jinglong Stele) text has 22 characters, 敦煌 (Dunhuang) text 23 characters, the He-shang Gong, Wang Bi, and 範應元 editions have 25 characters, and the 傅奕 (Fu Yi) edition has 26 characters. The He-shang Gong text titles it "成象第六" (Chengxiang Chapter 6), Wang Bi calls it "六章" (Chapter 6), and 範應元 titles it "谷神不死章第六".

The page concludes with the URN ctp:ws467344 for citation, links to view the main text, and standard site navigation. The copyright notice indicates the site's design and content are copyrighted from 2006-2026.

SUMMARY:
